INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and
Culture, having been authorized by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this Two
Hundred and Fifty First Report on “Action Taken Replies by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on the observations/
recommendations as contained in its Two Hundred Forty Fourth Report on Demands for Grants
(2017-18) of the Ministry of Civil Aviation”.
2. The Two Hundred Forty Fourth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented on the 17th March, 2017 to the Parliament.
3. The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its Two Hundred
Forty Fourth Report was received from the Ministry of Shipping on 21st July, 2017.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on the 8th August, 2017.
NEW DELHI; MUKUL ROY
August 8, 2016 Chairman,
Sravana 17, 1939 (Saka) Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Transport, Tourism and Culture,
Rajya Sabha.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
recommendations/observations as contained in its Two Hundred Forty Fourth Report on Demands for
Grants (2017-18) of the Ministry of Civil Aviation which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament
on 17th March, 2017.
2. Action Taken Replies were received from the Government on 21st July, 2017, in respect of
all the recommendations/observations contained in the Report. The replies have been categorized as
follows:-
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Paragraph Nos.: 10, 17, 19, 25, 27, 30, 33, 33B, 33D, 35, 37, 45, 46, 50, 53, 54, 56, 58,
Total: 26
(ii) Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of
the Government replies:-
Total: 3
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not
been accepted by the Committee:
Total: 5
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still
awaited.
Total: 13
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of those recommendations/observations
which have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished at the
earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of
Action Taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee contained
in the Two Hundred Forty Fourth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry and recommendations/
observations of the Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the succeeding
paragraphs:
ASSESSMENT OF THE DEMANDS FOR GRANTS (2017-18) OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee notes that ` 2702.40 crores has been allocated for the Ministry of Civil Aviation
for 2017-18 against the allocation of ` 3452.37 crores at RE stage in 2016-17. (Para 10)
61,  65,  78,  81,  82,  83,  85  and  86
Paragraph  Nos.:  22,  23  and  33F
Paragraph  Nos.  :  25A,  41,  72,  72A  and  73
Paragraph  Nos.:  14,  22A,  30A,  33C  ,  43,  48,  52,  63,  66,  76,  80,  81B  and  84

2
Reply of the Government
6. Noted.
Further Recommendations/Observations
7. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
8. The Committee notes that there is considerable shortfall in budgetary allocation for 2017-18
especially on the Revenue side and that the Ministry of Finance has not intimated any reason for this
reduction. Keeping in view the considerable growth of the civil aviation sector, Committee is of the
considered view that with the present allocation, it would be difficult to run the existing schemes and
other activities undertaken by the Ministry. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the Ministry
should actively pursue the matter of increasing the allocation in the first supplementary and at the RE
stage in the current financial year 2017-18, with the Ministry of Finance. (Para 14)
Reply of the Government
9. The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. The proposal for
increase in allocation of funds for Ministry of Civil Aviation for 2017-18 will be taken up with Ministry
of Finance through 1st Supplementary grant and at RE stage as well.
Further Recommendations/Observations
10. The Committee may be apprised of the progress made in this regard.
Recommendation/Observation
11. The Committee may be apprised of the details of the Skill Development Scheme at the implementing
stage. (Para 17)
Reply of the Government
12. The details of the Skill Development Scheme are given as under:-
(a) Ministry had engaged M/s iMaCS for conducting a comprehensive skill gap analysis and
future Road Map for skill development in Civil Aviation Sector. M/s iMaCS submitted the
final report on 15.03.2016.
(b) A workshop on raising awareness about National Skill Qualification Framework was held
on 20.10.2016 with training institutions.
(c) An MoU b/w MoCA and MSDE was signed on 20.10.2016 for collaboration on skill
development.
(d) A Workshop on Recognition of Prior Learning for Aviation Professionals in the Airline/
Airport/Ground Handling/MRO services was held on 08.02.2017. Further, through the
Workshop, Data Entry operators of Ministry of Civil Aviation, DGCA and BCAS have been
given training under RPL on 28th - 31st March, 2017.

3
(e) The skill development programme has been launched in the cargo sector with the introduction
of the Basic Cargo Awareness Programme (BCAP) programme at Joint Venture and AAI
Airports. The pilot BCAP was launched at Delhi i.e. IGIA Cargo Terminal on 20/10/2015.
(f) Industry validation of 38 QPNOS for civil aviation sector is in process by the AASSC and
they will be finalized in due course of time, after which NSQF aligned training can commence.
The first Executive Development Programme (EDP) was held by Rajiv Gandhi National
Aviation University (RGNAU) on 2-4 February 2017.
Further Recommendations/Observations
13. The Committee notes the reply.
TWELFTH FIVE YEAR PLAN
Recommendation/Observation
14. The Committee takes note of the projects initiated by the Ministry during the Twelfth Five year
Plan. (Para 19)
Reply of the Government
15. Noted.
Further Recommendations/Observations
16. The Committee notes the reply.
AIR INDIA LIMITED
Recommendation/Observation
17. The Committee feels that the reduction in equity infusion to the tune of Rs. 787 crores will
adversely affect the financial and operational performance of the company since it may be forced to take
loans from banks and financial institutions at a higher interest rate to meet the short fall, which was
not contemplated under the Financial Restructuring Plan. The Committee, therefore, is of the considered
view that such short fall, at this stage when the company is presently placed at a critical position in
achieving the TAP targets, should be avoided. Since the committed financial support from the Government
is vital to sustain the momentum of performance of Air India, the Committee strongly recommends that
the full amount of equity infusion should be restored to Air India. The Committee recommends that in
future, the amount committed under the TAP should be allocated to Air India at the BE stage itself.
(Para 22)
Reply of the Government
18. With regard to increase in allocation of funds for the current financial year, the matter has been
taken up with Secretary (Finance). However, a formal proposal for additional funds will be taken up at
the time of 1st Supplementary grant.
Further Recommendations/Observations
19. The Committee hopes that the amount committed under the TAP would be allocated to Air
India at the RE stage.

4
Recommendation/Observation
20. The Committee was informed by the Secretary that the profit of Air India has been severely dented
to the tune of ` 1000 crore due to rupee depreciation and foreign exchange variation. The Ministry of
Finance has not taken into account the factor of rupee depreciation and foreign exchange variation while
deciding the equity infusion. The Committee, therefore, recommends that if the intention of the Ministry
of Finance is the revival of Air India, then the former should seriously consider the factors which are
beyond the control of Air India such as depreciation of rupee and foreign exchange variation, while
deciding the amount of equity infusion. (Para 22A)
Reply of the Government
21. The Ministry of Civil Aviation has requested Air India to submit a proposal on the reduction in
profit due to rupee depreciation and foreign exchange variation. Once the proposal from Air India is
received, the matter will be taken up with Ministry of Finance.
Further Recommendations/Observations
22. The Committee may be apprised of the progress made in this regard.
Recommendation/Observation
23. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation may take up this matter
with the Ministry of Finance for the restoration of the full amount of Equity Infusion of 
` 2587 crores
as requested for in the Annual Plan for the financial year 2017-18 by Air India Ltd.
(Para 23)
Reply of the Government
24. The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. The proposal for
restoration of full amount of Equity infusion of ` 2587.00 crore for 2017-18 will be taken up with
Ministry of Finance through 1st Supplementary grant and at RE stage as well.
Further Recommendations/Observations
25. The Committee hopes that the amount committed under the TAP would be allocated to Air
India at the RE stage.
Recommendation/Observation
26. The Committee appreciates Air India for making operational profits in the financial year 2015-
16. The Committee hopes that Air India would register further profits in the coming months. The
Committee emphasizes the need for micromanaging routes and timings of Air India flights to make Air
India more competitive and passenger friendly. (Para 25)
Reply of the Government
27. Air India schedule is prepared on the basis of its independent assessment of demand, availability
of requisite resources and subject to allotment of the requisite time slots at the various airports. The

5
schedule preparation is aimed at optimizing the deployment of the airline’s resources in order to meet
demands and maximize profits. With the creation of Delhi as its main hub utmost importance is given
to provide seamless and convenient connections both for the domestic as well as international passengers
travelling on its flights. The schedule is drawn with the sole purpose of maximising the yield and
enhancing the revenue on the network by providing convenient connectivity. The feeder traffic to Air
India’s International and Domestic flights have grown over the period which has resulted in better
revenue generation.
28. Air India reviews the performance of its flights on a regular basis. The carriage / load factors /
financial performance of services on its network are regularly monitored and also efforts made to
improve their performance like increase or decrease frequency on existing routes /modifying the existing
schedule by changing the departure time or equipment on a particular route etc. Inputs and suggestions
from Sales and Marketing team regarding change in departure time of a particular flight are also analyzed
for enhanced revenue and implemented subject to availability of Slots at the Airports.
29. Major route restructuring was done in winter 15 schedule with an aim to operate point to point
flights to / from major hubs thereby increasing availability of aircraft and crew for optimum utilization
of available resources and increasing revenue.
30. Following main points are considered in managing the routes operated by Air India:
1. Serve Metro markets, which account for bulk of domestic traffic with multiple daily
frequencies.
2. Aim to serve all markets nonstop to the extent feasible / viable and restructure round robin/
one halt services to nonstop.
3. Aim to serve all markets with at least a daily service, subject to feasibility and viability.
4. Endeavour to provide day return connectivity which are already served with a daily service.
5. Focus on improving connectivity between DEL and other domestic points to strengthen the
hub at DEL.
6. Gain reasonable presence in the growing low cost market segments.
7. Develop new feeder networks to increase flows on trunk and metro routes with focus on
tier-II / tier-III cities.
Further Recommendations/Observations
31. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
32. During the deliberations of the Committee, many Members of the Committee have complained that
the catering services in Air India aircrafts are not up to the mark and that it needs improvement to attract
more passengers. The Committee notes that this is an oft repeated complaint which needs serious attention
of the top management of Air India and Ministry of Civil Aviation. The Committee urges upon the

6
Ministry to evaluate the standards of the catering services in Air India flights and take necessary steps
to improve the same. The Committee may be informed about the action taken in this regard.
(Para 25A)
Reply of the Government
33. Air India uplifts its meal from the reputed caterers on its flights who also cater to several domestic
and international airlines and have various requisite regulatory certifications and licences. The caterers
also undergo regular audits and checks from these regulatory bodies and Air India to ensure quality.
34. Meal service is reviewed from time to time and menus are updated as per sector-wise requirements
putting emphasis on regional cuisine and also taking into consideration duration of flight, flight timings
and local infra-structural & raw material availability. It is ensured that hygienic, palatable and wholesome
meals are provided to the passengers.
35. The views of the Committee members about quality of food are noted and the caterers would be
urged to ensure and improve quality.
Further Recommendations/Observations
36. The Committee notes that there is ample scope for improvement in the standards of
catering services made available in Air India flights.
AIRPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
Recommendation/Observation
37. The Committee notes that earlier , the cargo sector was dominated by private airlines. The Committee
welcomes the entry of AAI into the cargo sector. (Para 27)
Reply of the Government
38. Noted.
Further Recommendations/Observations
39. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
40. The Committee feels concerned about the huge amount of outstanding dues of AAI for a long time.
AAI, being the highest revenue generator, has to be actively helped by the Ministry of Civil Aviation
in this regard by taking it up with the defaulting Organizations and Ministries including legal recourse.
The Committee recommends that consistent steps should be taken by AAI to recover the outstanding dues.
(Para 30)
Reply of the Government
41. Statement of dues of various major airlines and concessioners is enclosed at Annexure-A. It may
be seen that there is considerable improvement in recovery of dues in all cases. In case of National

7
Carrier (Air India Group) tripartite meeting was held on 1st March, 2017 with Air India officials along
with Ministry of Civil Aviation officials to expedite the settlement/clearance of dues. Action is being taken
up accordingly.
42. Other scheduled domestic operators are also being pursued to speed up the payment process. Dues
are being monitored closely. As suggested all the Regions/Airports have been instructed to closely monitor
the dues and to report immediately to CHQ in case of any major variation/delay in realization.
Further Recommendations/Observations
43. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
44. The Committee notes that ` 294.69 crores is due from now defunct Kingfisher Airlines. The
Committee also notes that legal suit has been filed against Kingfisher Airlines to recover the dues. The
Committee observes that the Airports Authority of India allowed the accumulation of dues to such a high
level in violation of all the existing rules and procedures in practice. The Committee recommends that
Airports Authority of India should be cautious in future to ensure that no individual stakeholder/airlines
is accumulating such high levels of dues. The Committee also recommends that Airports Authority of
India may conduct an internal inquiry (i) to fix the responsibility of Airports Authority of India officials
for the accumulation of dues by Kingfisher Airlines and (ii) to strengthen the systems and procedures to
prevent the recurrence of accumulation of dues. The Committee may be intimated about the outcome of
the internal inquiry. 
Reply of the Government
45. All Regional Hqrs. and airports have been instructed to ensure that such cases are not repeated
in future. An Internal Committee has been constituted in AAI headed by the senior officer to fix the
responsibility of the officials for the accumulation of dues by Kingfisher Airlines and to strengthen the
systems and procedures further to ensure prevention of recurrence of such accumulation of dues. On
receipt of the report of the said Internal Committee further action will be taken.
46. The dues of Private Concessioners have accumulated mainly because of Arbitration, Court cases,
service tax and royalty. All the cases are consistently being followed up. Government and other PSUs
are pursued with the respective Departments.
Further Recommendations/Observations
47. The Committee desires that strict action should be taken against the responsible officials
found guilty by the Internal Committee.
Recommendation/Observation
48. The Committee hopes that the monetization of AAI land will generate considerable revenue to AAI.
(Para 33)
Reply of the Government
49. Noted.
(Para  30A)

8
Further Recommendations/Observations
50. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
51. The Committee recommends that Airports Authority of India should take initiatives to establish
sufficient commercial activities at the Kolkata airport to generate reasonable level of non-aeronautical
revenue. The Committee is afraid that the neglect of the airport may be a prelude to making it a loss
making airport which may pave the way for privatization of services at the airport.
(Para 33B)
Reply of the Government
52. To optimize utilization of available space and to increase Non-aeronautical revenue, new licenses
for various facilities have been awarded since 2016. Details of major contract is appended below:
Sl. No. Facility Space Revenue
1. Duty Free Outlet 605 sqm. `1,84,43,840/- p.m
2. Master Concessionaire for General Retail 1050 sqm. ` 86,07,500/- p.m
3. Advertisement Rights 14697 sqm. `3,13,48,701/- p.m
53. For non-aeronautical revenue of Kolkata Airport is continuously increasing year by year with
following details:
2013-14 `178.46 Crores
2014-15 `217.63 Crores
2015-16 `257.99 Crores
54. Further, endeavor is being made to exploit the available space, without encroaching into passenger
convenience and safeguarding the safety concern by introducing various new licenses to enhance AAI
Non-aeronautical revenue and to improve passenger experience.
Further Recommendations/Observations
55. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
56. It has been brought to the notice of the Committee that Gir Forest which is one of the sanctuaries
for Asiatic Lion is a much visited area by the domestic as well as foreign tourists. However, there is no
air operations anywhere near the sanctuary. The Committee noticed that there is an airstrip near Gir
which can be developed to improve air connectivity. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Airports
Authority of India should take the lead to enable the Gir airstrip to start commercial air operations.
(Para 33C)

9
Reply of the Government
57. Airports Authority of India owns and maintains Keshod Airport near the Gir Forest which is
approximately 92 km by road and aerial distance of 40 NM (approx.). Keshod Airport is having a runway
dimesions of 1372m x 45m is an operational airport of AAI suitable for handling ATR-42 type of aircraft
under Visual Flight Rules conditions. Airport is having a Terminal Building suitable for handling 50 peak
hour passengers at a time and two parking stand for parking ATR-72 type of aircraft. At present, no
airlines is operating scheduled flights from Keshod Airport.
Further Recommendations/Observations
58. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may explore the possibility of operating
flights from Keshod Airport soon.
Recommendation/Observation
59. During the deliberations of the Committee, it was brought to the notice of the Committee that the
passenger amenities at the Ahmedabad airport is in bad shape. The officials of the airport are not taking
sufficient steps to improve the facilities at the airport. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
Airports Authority of India should intervene immediately to ensure that passenger facilities are improved
at the Ahmedabad airport. 
Reply of the Government
60. Action taken in respect of Ahmedabad Airport is as under:
1. Restaurant: Restaurant is available at International Terminal (Terminal-2). For Domestic
Terminal (Terminal-1) tendering is in process.
2. Passenger Chairs: Upholstery and painting work for passenger chairs is in progress to
improve quality of passenger comfort during their waiting time.
3. FIDS Boards: All FIDS boards are going to be replaced with bigger size and latest technology
boards.
4. In-line Baggage System: In-line Baggage System at Domestic Terminal to reduce waiting
time of baggage screening with adding ATR (auto tag reader) for more passenger security
aspect. At International Terminal procurement of in-line baggage system is under process
at CHQ.
5. It has been ensured that passenger baggage trolleys must be available at all the time at trolley
slots.
6. For any enquiry/help/assistance shift duty in-charge available in round the clock in both
Domestic & International Terminals.
7. Self Boarding kiosks have been installed at Terminal-1.
(Para  33D)

10
Further Recommendations/Observations
61. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
62. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation made in its 231st Report that the senior
positions of BCAS may be held exclusively by the cadre officials of BCAS. The Committee further
recommends that the Recruitment Rules of BCAS should be amended in such a way that the cadre officers
may, without any hindrance, be promoted up to the level of Joint Director General. The Committee
desires that the Ministry may submit a note in this regard for the consideration of the Committee.
(Para 33F)
Reply of the Government
63. Consequent to the approval of ‘re-structuring of BCAS’, proposal for creation of one additional
post of Joint Director General (formerly known as Joint Commissioner of Security (CA)) is under
submission for the approval of the Cabinet. Further, the re-structuring plan provides for an additional post
of Deputy Director General (the erstwhile post of Additional Commissioner of Security (Civil Aviation))
in BCAS.
1. Process of amendment of RRs for Post of Joint Director General (JDG) would be initiated
after the additional post is approved by the Cabinet.
2. The recruitment rules for the post Deputy Director General (DDG) are currently being
examined wherein one post of DDG has been earmarked for filling through promotion
“failing which” on deputation. Once it is approved at appropriate level, the necessary action
would be taken in this regard.
3. RRs of Group ‘A’  posts pertaining to Asst. Director (AD), Deputy Director (DD) and Joint
Director (JD) has been approved by the DOP&T and UPSC. While submitting the RRs for
the above posts to UPSC/DOP&T, it was proposed to keep Ten per cent of total number
of posts for promotion. However, UPSC after examining the proposal has recommended the
following percentage of total posts for promotion “failing which” on deputation: -
(a) For AD: Seven (7) Per cent
(b) For DD: Five (5) Per cent
(c) For JD:
(i) 1/24(One post) by way of composite method [deputation(ISTC) plus promotion];
and
(ii) 23/24 (23 posts) by way of deputation (ISTC).
These would be notified in due course after approval of Competent Authority.

11
Further Recommendations/Observations
64. The Committee notes the reply.
DIRECTORATE GENERAL OF CIVIL AVIATION (DGCA)
Recommendation/Observation
65. The Committee notes the allocation made for DGCA. (Para 35)
Reply of the Government
66. Noted.
Further Recommendations/Observations
67. The Committee notes the reply.
INDIRA GANDHI RASHTRIYA URAN AKADEMI (IGRUA)
Recommendation/Observation
68. The Committee desires that IGRUA may be allocated adequate funds to ensure that the steps taken
to make IGRUA self sufficient turn out to be fruitful. (Para 37)
Reply of the Government
69. This Ministry has sought ` 5.00 crore for replacement of diesel engine training aircraft at IGRUA
in 1st Supplementary demands for Grants 2017-18. Also, a Cabinet Note is under inter-ministerial
circulation seeking subsidy for IGRUA.
Further Recommendations/Observations
70. The Committee notes the reply.
PAWAN HANS LTD.
Recommendation/Observation
71. The Committee notes that Pawan Hans is a profit making Organization. However, this profit alone
will not be adequate for its own fleet expansion and fleet replacement. The Committee is sure that the
investment made in Pawan Hans Ltd. would generate adequate returns to the Government. The Committee,
therefore, reiterates its recommendation made in its 231st Report that giving 
` 600 crores to Pawan Hans
as one time grant for its ambitious expansion plan needs to be seriously considered. Keeping in view the
urgent need for fleet replacement and augmentation, the Committee recommends that adequate provisions
may be made in the budget for Pawan Hans to cater to its imminent requirements.
(Para 41)
Reply of the Government
72. As the process of Strategic Disinvestment of PHL has started, the guidelines categorically states
“the fact company has been identified for strategic disinvestment must be kept in mind before any major

12
investment decision is taken”. In view of the above, M/o Finance has also returned the proposal for
replacement of 09 medium helicopters to be funded by Government equity.
Further Recommendations/Observations
73. The Committee fails to understand why strategic disinvestment has been started for Pawan
Hans which is a profit making Organization.
Recommendation/Observation
74. The Committee hopes that the heliport at Rohini will become operational soon. The Committee
is of the view that the helicopter industry has tremendous potential to provide services in the tourism
sector, disaster management etc. The Committee desires that more such heliports may be set up throughout
the country. The Committee reiterates its recommendation that Air India and Pawan Hans can work

EXORBITANT AIRFARES
Recommendation/Observation
122. The Committee takes note of the fact that there are no existing rules and regulations which are
working in the way of regulating airfares after the repeal of Air Corporation Act in 1994. The Committee
desires that the Ministry of Civil Aviation should specify the limitations, legal and otherwise, which need
to be amended or other measures to be put in place to tackle this problem after consulting all the
stakeholders. We are a developing country and many of the pricing mechanism applicable to the developed
countries may not suit the Indian people and Indian conditions. The Ministry should consider fixing an
upper limit for every sector, especially in the economy class of air fares. (Para 72)
Reply of the Government
123. Under the provision of Sub Rule (1) of Rule 135, Aircraft Rules 1937, airlines are free to fix
reasonable tariff having regard to all relevant factors, including the cost of operation, characteristics of
services, reasonable profit and the generally prevailing tariff. Air fare so established by the airlines is
published on their respective website under the provision of Sub Rule (2) of Rule 135, Aircraft Rules
1937.
124. In order to prevent excessive charging and sudden surges in airfares and to promote transparency
by scheduled domestic airlines, DGCA has also issued Air Transport Circular 02 of 2010 wherein airlines
are required to display on their respective websites the tariff sheet route-wise across their network in
various fare categories and the manner it is offered in the market. The intention behind the above
directions is to keep the passengers informed of pricing pattern of airlines. DGCA has also set up a Tariff
Monitoring Unit in 2010 that monitors airfares on certain routes selected on random basis to ensure that
the airlines do not charge airfares outside the range declared by them.

20
Further Recommendations/Observations

may be apprised of the steps taken by the Ministry to ensure that the public is protected from

On international routes, including Kerala - Gulf , the fares being offered are reasonable and have been
constructed based on market considerations such as fares offered by competitors, seasonality, extent of
competition and product features like frequency, timing’s, direct / indirect operations etc. All fares
offered by Air India are published fares with given validity and are not changed arbitrarily to take
advantage of holiday / festival season. Closer to departure higher fares may be available as low fares get
sold out first.
Further Recommendations/Observations
128. The Committee is not satisfied with the reply furnished by the Ministry. The Committee
may be apprised of the steps taken by the Ministry to ensure that the public is protected from

Recommendation/Observation
129. The Committee also notes that even after 50% reduction of the ATF prices over a period of time,
the airlines have not passed on the benefit of reduction in ATF prices to the consumers. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry should take effective steps to ensure that the airlines pass on the benefit
to the travellers by reducing the air fares and inform the Committee about the specific steps taken in
this regard and the outcome thereof. (Para 73)
Reply of the Government
130. Airfares are not regulated by the Government and airlines are free to fix reasonable charges/fee
subject to compliance with rule 135 of Aircraft Rules 1937. The prices are fixed by airlines keeping in
mind the market demand, seasonality and other market forces. Air fares established by the airlines under
the provision of Sub Rule (1) of Rule 135 of Aircraft Rules 1937, considering all relevant factors,
including the cost of operation, characteristics of service, reasonable profit and the generally prevailing
tariff. The airfares so established are required to be displayed under the provisions of Sub Rule (2) of

21
Rule 135 of Aircraft Rules 1937. Airline remains compliant to the regulatory provisions of Rule 135 as
long as the fare charged by them does not exceed the fare established and displayed on their website.
131. The domestic airline pricing runs in multiple levels (bucket or Reservation Booking Designator
(RBD)) which are in line with the practice followed globally. Usually, the lower levels of the fare in the
fare bucket are assigned to advance purchase (popularly known as Apex Fares) bookings (e.g. up to 90,
60, 30, 14 and 07 days before departure). As time lapses and date of journey approaches closer (from
07 days to date of departure), the fare in higher side of fare bucket are available for purchase. Airline
remains compliant to the regulatory provisions of Rule -135 as long as the fare charged by them does
not exceed the fare established and displayed on their website. In order to prevent excessive charging
and sudden surges in airfares and to promote transparency by scheduled domestic airlines, DGCA has
issued Air Transport Circular 02 of 2010 wherein airlines are required to display on their respective
website the tariff sheet route- wise across their network in various fare categories and the manner it is
offered in the market. The intention behind the above directions is to keep the passengers informed of
pricing pattern of airlines. DGCA has also set up a Tariff Monitoring Unit in 2010 that monitors airfares
on certain routes selected on random basis to ensure that the airlines do not charge airfares outside the
range declared by them.
132. With regard to have maximum retail price on airline tickets, the petition filed with Competition
Commission of India (CCI) in a matter on charges of arbitrary high air fare case No. 68/2012 for issue
of direction to DGCA, Secretary (CA) to fix MRP for airlines, CCI has stated in their order that
Commission cannot give direction to this effect. In fact that will be contrary to the spirit of competition
law. Today, the forces of demand and supply govern the airfares.

Report on the issue of preferential treatment given to some airlines (Indigo)
while landing/takeoff:
1 Air Traffic Services are provided to all the airlines as per provisions the provisions of ICAO PAN
ATM Doc 4444 (AAI’s Manual of Air Traffic Services) and National rules/regulations. The approach
sequence is established in a manner which will facilitate arrival of the maximum number of aircraft
with the least average delay. In case of extended delays due to congestion, runway closures/
maintenance, airspace activities etc. the approach sequence is judiciously established on the principle
of accommodating maximum number of aircraft (including departures) irrespective of the airlines,
with least average delay by taking into consideration the total track mileage from touchdown,
respective positions and flight levels, performance profiles etc.
2 Priority is given to:
(a) An aircraft which anticipates being compelled to land because of factors affecting the safe
operation of the aircraft (engine failure, shortage of fuel, etc.);
(b) Hospital aircraft or aircraft carrying any sick or seriously injured person requiring urgent
medical attention;
(c) Aircraft engaged in search and rescue operations; and
(d) VIP I (President), VIP II (Vice President), VIP III (Prime Minister) and VIP V (Foreign
Heads of State/Govt.) aircraft.

constituted at each of six Metro airports (Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad and
Bengaluru) which accounts for more than 60% of air traffic in India. One team was required to
monitor traffic pattern and handling of traffic in Aerodrome Control Tower and other team was
required to do the same in Approach Radar Unit for a duration of one hour during peak traffic
hour of that airport.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the observations/
recommendations as contained in its Two Hundred and Forty Sixth Report on Demands for Grants
(2017-18) of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways which was presented to both the Houses
of Parliament on 17th March, 2017.
2. Action Taken Replies were received from the Government on 19th July, 2017, in respect of all
the observations/recommendations contained in the Report. The replies have been categorized as follows:—
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Paragraph Nos.: 6, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 22, 23, 32, 34, 40, 42, 47, 59, 68, 71, 72, 80, 83,
84, 86, 91, 94, 97, 102, 104, 110, 117, 119, 121, 129, 132, 151 and 159 Total: 34
(ii) Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of
the Government replies:-
Paragraph Nos.: 123, 137, 140, 148 and 160 Total: 5
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not
been accepted by the Committee:
Paragraph Nos. : 13, 18, 19, 30, 53, 65 and 133 Total: 7
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still
awaited.
Paragraph Nos: 9, 10, 15, 41, 50, 75 and 107 Total: 7
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of those recommendations/observations
which have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished at the
earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of
Action Taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee contained
in the Two Hundred and Forty Sixth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry and recommendations/
observations of the Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs:
ASSESSMENT OF THE DEMANDS FOR GRANTS (2017-18) OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee has been given an understanding by the Secretary that total budget allocated would
be utilized during the financial year 2016-17. However, the Committee strongly recommends that the
expenditure percentage may be reviewed on quarterly basis as per expenditure guidelines of the Ministry

2
of Finance and the major portion of the Budget should not be left behind to be incurred in the last
quarter of the financial year. (Para 6 of the 246th Report)
Reply of the Government
6. Noted for compliance
Further Recommendations/Observations
7. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
8. The Committee is distressed to note that the additional fund was not provided to the Ministry at
RE stage and instead it got a cut for SARDP-NE and Externally Aided Projects (Para 9)
Reply of the Government
9. Out of total 2016-17 RE outlay of ` 52,447 crore, ` 38,209 crore was earmarked to be met from
the Central Road Fund (CRF). Requirements of funds for the schemes SARDP-NE, Road Transport,
EAP, a portion of fund for Maintenance of National Highways and fund for Secretariat Expenditure is
met from Gross Budgetary Support (GBS). Fund under CRF for 2016-17 was reduced by Ministry of
Finance at RE stage based on revised estimated collection of cess on petrol and HSD oil. Fund for GBS
was also reduced.
10. Keeping in view of the availability of fund under GBS and total budget provision of the Ministry,
fund was reduced for the schemes EAP and SARDP-NE accordingly. However, mandatory provision of
10% of total budget provision for NE Region was made under the scheme SARDP-NE. For the current
financial year 2017-18, budget for SARDP-NE has been kept ` 5,765 crore.
11. The Ministry shall take up the issue of enhancement of budgetary allocation at RE stage
2017-18 appropriately with the Ministry of Finance based on estimated requirement at that stage.
Further Recommendations/Observations
12. The Committee hopes that the Ministry will pursue the matter vigorously with the Ministry
of Finance for enhancement of budgetary allocation at RE stage (2017-18).
Recommendation/Observation
13. There is a sharp contrast between the reply given by the Ministry and the data shown in the figure
attached to the reply. The Committee further wants to know what are the factors which blocked the work
of awarding projects to the contractors. The Ministry could achieve only one third of stipulated target
of awarding the projects for 25,000 km. Secondly, the Committee is further dismayed to note that the
target of constructions out of the 10,000 km. of the road projects only 5,498 km could be constructed
upto January, 2017. Hence, the Committee recommends that the Ministry has to put extra effort to
achieve the target what it has set for the construction of the road for the year 2017-18.
(Para 10)

3

projects hassle free. To expedite completion of these projects various steps have been taken which
include streamlining of land acquisition and environment clearances, exit for equity investors, premium
re-schedulement, close coordination with other Ministries, revamping of dispute resolution mechanism,

(a) Environment and Forest Clearance
• Delegation of powers to Regional Offices by Ministry of Environment and Forest.

km. EC is not required if widening is restricted to 40m and realignment to 60m.

(c) Financial initiatives

• Infrastructure debt fund - Long term financing at low interest rates

• 100% exit after 2 years of completion in projects awarded before 2009.
• Fund infusion by NHAI in stalled projects where the physical progress is 50% and
the concessionaire is facing shortage of funds.

Bank of India) has also issued circular for providing long term debt finance matching
the concession period without classifying the exposure as restructured.

Departments and State Governments, etc., hosted on the Portal. Both these portals, also, discuss the

of the view that even the national capital is far-far away from a good public road transport system, the
Committee recommends that instead of allowing private aggregaters to ply taxi on the roads, they should
be roped in to ply buses in major cities. (Para 119)
Reply of the Government
189. Public transport System is the responsibility of the respective State Government. It is for the
respective State Government to decide to allow private aggregators to ply buses in major cities. However,
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways will consider the recommendation of the Committee to allow
Private aggregators to ply private buses in major cities by issuing advisory to States/UTs.
Further Recommendations/Observations
190. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
191. The Committee wants to know the status of Development of Bus Terminals and Multi Modal
Transit Terminal. The Committee feels that since the Ministry is a major stakeholder it has to play
proactive role in the project. (Para 121)
Reply of the Government
192. Delhi Integrated Multi Model Transit System Ltd. (DIMTS) have been appointed as the Project
Development Consultant and an agreement has been signed between MoRTH and DIMTS Ltd. to prepare
the standard Project Reference Documents. DIMTS is in the process of finalization of Project Reference
Documents.
Further Recommendations/Observations
193. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
194. The Committee observes that the fund to be allocated to State PWDs is quite a big amount, but
the Committee would also like to know whether these money has been utilised by the State in full or got
the project underhand completed in a prescribed time-frame. The Committee wants that the Ministry
should keep the check and balance on States while giving the fund and getting the utilisation certificate
of the work done periodically. (Para 123)

30
Reply of the Government
195. Total fund of `13717.40 crore was allocated to States/UTs for development of National Highways
under National Highways(Original) and Permanent Bridge Fee Fund Schemes during the year 2016-17.
The payment under the scheme is made by Regional Pay and Accounts Offices (National Highways) after
examination and passing the bills from contractors by Regional Officers of the Ministry under Direct
Payment Procedure(DPP). Hence, Utilisation Certificates for these payment is not required.
196. Fund for development of State Roads are released to States/UTs as “Grant-in-Aid for Creating of
Capital Assets”. Projects for development of State Roads under the Central Road Fund Scheme, implemented
by the State PWDs, are accorded Administrative Approval (AA) by the Ministry as per the extant policy.
Technical Sanction(TS) and Financial concurrence(FS) are given by States. As per the extant policy, one
third of the allocation for the financial year for the State is released for utilisation against sanctioned
works and this amount is maintained as a reserve by replenishing expenditure from subsequent releases.
Further releases of funds during the financial year are made to State based on the utilisation certificates
(UCs) furnished by them.
197. The Ministry while releasing funds to the States based on UCs, etc., duly reviews progress of
works, expenditure incurred on them, etc.
Further Recommendations/Observations
198. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
199. The Committee is of the view that the traffic of vehicles in Delhi is increasing at alarming pace
(registration of 10 lakhs vehicles approx. in 2016, bringing the number of vehicles in Delhi close to 1
crore). The Committee appreciates that the Ministry has taken many steps to decongest the traffic but
in practice it will take a long time to decongest the road for smooth traffic in Delhi. The Committee
further thinks that the Ministry has a major role to play in improving the traffic scenario in Delhi. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry should play proactive role in co-ordination with the Government
of Delhi to ease the problem faced by the people in negotiating with the large traffic on the road.
(Para 129)
Reply of the Government
200. For ease out of outgoing and gross through traffic coming from outside of Delhi, the NHAI has
taken up construction of about 135 km. long Eastern Peripheral Expressway (EPE). This work is likely
to be completed by this year end. Further, Government of Haryana is also constructing about 135 km.
Western Peripheral Expressway (WPE), which is in continuity of EPE. Both these roads will be a new
Ring Road for about 270 km. around Delhi. All the traffic, which is not bound to Delhi and going to
other places will use this road and this will ease out the traffic in Delhi.
201. On the NH-24, NHAI has started the widening work to the 14-lane NH as a part of Delhi-Meerut
Expressway. The work has been started. On the NH-1, NHAI has started the 8-laning NH work from
Mukaraba Chowk to Delhi border.

31
202. All these NH development work will be helpful to sort out of traffic congestion in and around
Delhi.
Further Recommendations/Observations
203. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
204. The Committee is concerned about the increasing number of vehicle and vehicular pollution
caused by them in Delhi. The Committee knows that the Government of Delhi from time-to-time, has
taken steps on the directions of Honorable Courts, to check pollution but the problems of pollution in
Delhi is far from over. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should find out the solution for
vehicular pollution on the roads of Delhi. (Para 132)
Reply of the Government
205. The National Green Tribunal vide its order, dated 18.07.2016 and 20.7.2016 in O.A. 21 of 2014,
Vardhaman Kaushik V/s Union of India has directed that diesel vehicles older than 10 years to be
deregistered in NCR of Delhi. In compliance to the orders of NGT, de-registration of diesel vehicles more
than 10 years old is being carried out by the respective State Government. The proposal to introduce
‘Vehicle Fleet Modernization Programme’ to enable the replacement of Old Vehicles is under consideration.
This will ensure phasing out of older polluting vehicles and enable their replacement with fuel efficient
and environment friendly vehicles. The concept note on ‘Vehicle Fleet Modernization Programme’ to
enable the replacement of Old Heavy and Medium Commercial Vehicles as they contribute the maximum
of vehicular pollution was placed on Ministry’s official website for information and comments from
concerned Ministries and Departments and other stakeholders. The matter has been placed before the
Committee of Secretaries for their recommendations.
206. To reduce vehicular pollution across the country, Government has taken proactive steps to promote
environment friendly vehicles which are innovative, ushering in proactive use of natural resources. Bharat
Stage IV Fuel Norms have been applicable since the year 2010 in Delhi and NCR and certain cities. The
set norms have been mandated in phase-wise manners across the country. The Government has notified
G.S.R. 643(E), dated 19/08/2015 for introduction of BS-IV fuel throughout the country by the year 2017.
Furthermore, steps have been taken by notifying alternate fuels like ethanol, biogas, electric hybrid etc.
by amending the Central Motor Vehicle Rules. Ministry has issued GSR 889(E) dated 16th September,
2016 for introduction of BS VI, mandating mass emission standard for BS-VI throughout the country
w.e.f. from 1st, April 2020.
Further Recommendations/Observations
207. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
208. The Committee expresses its dismay over the inability of the Government of Delhi for not submitting
proposals for the funds to maintain the roads in Delhi from the Central Road Fund. The Committee wants

32
to know the reasons for non-utilization of funds. The Committee knows the condition of many roads in
Delhi which is in bad shape. The Committee strongly recommends the Ministry to convey the displeasure
of the Committee to the Government of Delhi for non-submission of proposals for construction/maintaining
the roads in Delhi. (Para 133)
Reply of the Government
209. The Ministry released ` 5.54 crore to the Government of NCT of Delhi during Financial year
2016-17 towards one third of the allocation for the State for the year to be maintained as reserve by
adjusting unutilized funds available with the State out of previous releases made. No further utilization
certificates (UCs) have been received from the Government of NCT of Delhi.
Further Recommendations/Observations
210. The Committee notes that the condition of roads in Delhi is poor but the Government is
not utilizing even 1/3rd of the allocated fund and the Union Ministry is a mute spectator. The
Committee recommends that the Government should take proactive measures to ensure that
NCT of Delhi is maintaining the roads properly. The Committee further recommends that the
Ministry should take up the matter with the Government of NCT of Delhi regarding the status
of utilization of funds at the earliest.
Recommendation/Observation
211. The Committee observes the facts given by the Ministry on treatment of accident victims. The
Ministry also during its deliberations with the Committee enlightened that recently they have taken
various steps to help the accident victims. The Committee came to know that the Ministry is planning
to link the ambulance service with the local hospitals so that optimal utilization could be made. The
Committee has already recommended in the recently presented report on the Motor Vehicle (Amendment)
Bill, 2016 for treating the accident victims in golden hour and not harassing the good Samaritans who
help the accident victims in the time of need. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry may
take up the issue of treatment of accident victims with its State counterpart for timely and free treatment.
(Para 137)
Reply of the Government
212. The recommendation of Committee has been noted for compliance.
Further Recommendations/Observations
213. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
214. The Committee insists on giving wide publicity on following the traffic rules, causes of accidents
its repercussions and treatment in emergency. (Para 140)
Reply of the Government
215. Recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance. However, it is stated that the
Ministry has been undertaking various publicity measures through print and electronic media including

33
following the traffic rules, causes of accidents its repercussions and treatment in emergency will also
be included in publicity campaigns.
Further Recommendations/Observations
216. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
217. The Committee observes that an amount of 
` 200 crore was allocated for Training and Research
in B.E. 2016-17, which was reduced at R.E. stage. Now, in 2017-18 the Ministry has been allocated `250
crore for the purpose. The Committee wants to know the reason why there is fluctuation in the allocation
of budget. The Committee feels that the training is an important part of the driving vehicles and this
aspect should not be ignored for the sake of saving fund because a less skilled driver brings lives of
others in danger while driving on the road. The Committee is of the view that during the time of renewal
of license the driver should undergo a refresher training as the modern vehicle has undergone many
changes. The Committee feels that the country still lacks good training schools and the Committee
recommends that the Ministry should assist the States in opening more Driving Schools.
(Para 148)
Reply of the Government
218. During 2016-17, ` 200 crore was allocated for the different schemes administered by Transport
Wing of Ministry of Road Transport and Highways viz, schemes relating to road safety, National Data
Base network, Inspection and Certification Centre, Improving and Strengthening of Pubic Transport
System, and not only for Training and Research. Under some of the scheme under road safety, financial
assistance are provided to States for setting up of Institute of Driving and Training Research (IDTR),
Inspection and Certification Centre, etc. Further installment is released after receipt of achieving the
milestone and receipt of Utilization Certificate (UC) along with supporting papers. Since, some of the
States did not provide (UC), the budgetary outlay was reduced at RE stage. During, 2017 -18, the
Government has decided to provide financial assistance of State Road Transport Undertaking (SRTU) for
improving their training infrastructure so that they could impart training. Accordingly, budgetary allocation
has been enhanced from ` 200 crore to ` 250 crore.
219. Further, the recommendation of the Committee to assist States to open the more Driving School
has been noted for compliance. The Ministry is in process to extend the scheme under which financial
assistance are provided to States to open the Driving Schools beyond Twelfth Five-Year Plan.
Further Recommendations/Observations
220. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
221. The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry has taken initiatives to adopt Swachchta action
plan wherever its activities or schemes are going on. (Para 151)

34
Reply of the Government
222. The Ministry has prepared Swachhta Action Plan (SAP). As per this, NHAI shall construct 1,488
toilets (ladies and gents) and Solid Waste Management (SWM) at 372 toll plazas. NHAI has already
constructed 480 toilets (120 toll plazas); work in progress for 520 toilets (130 toll plazas). Ministry
intends to develop ATM cum Toilet complex underneath flyovers/foot-over-bridges and SWM along NHs.
Public awareness campaign was launched. A separate budget head has been created for SAP in
2017-18 (BE) with an outlay of ` 91 crore.
Further Recommendations/Observations
223. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
224. The Committee is surprised to know that very few States have been given breath analyzer. The
Committee would like to know the details of fund to be allocated for breath analyzer for other States
and for cities especially Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Bengaluru, where number of vehicles are large and
the cases of drunken driving is rampant. The Committee thinks that road engineering is instrumental in
checking road accidents. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should form teams to find out the
accident prone sites, fault in its designing and its correction. (Para 159)
Reply of the Government
225. The Ministry is implementing a scheme for providing road safety equipment to States/ UTs for
enforcement. On the basis of requirements received from States during the year 2016-17, financial
assistance was provided to the States of J&K, Sikkim, Punjab and West Bengal. Ministry is inviting
proposals from States/UTs for providing financial assistance for purchase of Breath Analyzers.
226. Ministry established an exclusive Road Safety Engineering Cell and developed guidelines for
identification and rectification of black spots, Road Safety Audits, Road Safety Engineering works on
State Roads under CRF etc. These are circulated to all States/UTs.
227. So far 789 black spots are identified on National Highways based on fatalities in 2011, 2012, 2013
and 2014. Out of these, 150 spots are on PWD NH stretches, 501 are with NHAI and balance 138 are
on State Roads. Of the above spots, 96 spots are already rectified and 215 are on ongoing development
projects, 106 are sanctioned for rectification and balance are in different pre-construction stages. 10%
of allocations under CRF have been earmarked for Road Safety Engineering works on state roads under
CRF amendment rules 2016. Guidelines for implementing these rules have also been issued by the
Ministry.
228. Road Safety Audits are part of all EPC/BOT projects on NHs. Standalone Road Safety audits have
been sanctioned on 400 km. of NHs and more Road Safety audits are in bidding stage in about more
than 3000 km. Road safety improvements at selected critical locations have been sanctioned under Road
Safety Annual Plan at a cost of ` 255 crore. Crash barriers have been sanctioned in a length of about
143 km. at a cost of ` 87 crore in hilly terrain on NHs. Capacity building activities through formal and

35
informal training workshops on Road Safety Engineering are organized where more than 1000 engineers
have participated.
229. In the light of the above, it may be seen that systems have already been kept in place for checking
road accidents through engineering measures.
Further Recommendations/Observations
230. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
231. The Committee feels that an effective co-ordination mechanism among the Ministry of Culture,
Ministries of Tourism, Civil Aviation and Road Transport and Highways is needed in order to ensure that
the places of tourist and cultural importance are integrated seamlessly with well connected roads and
airports and are provided with required facilities like budget hotels, taxis, souvenir shops, restaurants etc.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways may co-
ordinate in formulating an action plan with the above said Ministries in this regard and that the Ministry
of Tourism may be made the nodal Ministry for this purpose. (Para 160)
Reply of the Government
232. For seamless movement of Tourist vehicles this Ministry has published a draft notification on
18.05.2016 and uploaded on the website of this Ministry for the comments of the stakeholders. In the
meantime, a meeting was held on 10.08.2016 under the chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister ( RT&H) with
Hon’ble Minister for Transport, Government of Kerala. Government of Kerala raised apprehension
regarding loss of revenue after implementation of the All India Authorization for Tourist Bus Permit Rules,
2016. In this regard, Hon’ble Minister (RT&H) directed that this matter involves the interests of the
States. Therefore, it may be put up before the Group of Transport Ministers of States for consideration
and recommendation. The matter is under consideration with the Group of Ministers.
233. Ministry of Tourism has taken up the matter of reviving airstrips, increased air connectivity to
major and potential tourist destinations, opening of new airstrips, requirement of airports at world
heritage sites and other important tourist destinations which are strategically located near tourist sites
with the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
234. Rail being the most preferred mode of transport for domestic tourists, amenities in trains as well
as at railway stations have to be improved substantially for better tourist experience. Both Ministry of
Railways and Ministry of Tourism have agreed to collaborate for the joint upgradation of 24 railway
stations in the country.
235. Under the Swadesh Darshan and Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Augmentation Drive
(PRASAD) Schemes, the component of development of approach and last mile connectivity are eligible
for Central Financial Assistance to ensure improvement of road connectivity leading to tourist sites/
destinations.
Further Recommendations/Observations
236. The Committee notes the reply.

(b) Dredging: The 12th plan envisaged to increase the drafts to at least 14 meters in all ports
by the end of 12th plan period and achieve 17 meters in Hub-Ports. 10 of the Major Ports

(c) Productivity and Dwell Time: As emphasized in the 12th Plan, successful attempts have
already been initiated for closely working with Customs Department to reduce the dwell
time for containers in Ports and CFSs. Also, Direct Port Delivery facility, under the accredited
client programme has been extended by JNPT.
(d) Containerization and Hinterland Connectivity.: The share of Containerized traffic during
2016-17 was 19.23%. The container handling capacity of Major Ports increased from
138.88 Million Tonnes during 2011-12 to 183.81 Million Tonnes during 2016-17 with a

containerized cargo in ports with a view to capturing a higher share of international trade.

for Major and non-Major Ports.
(e) Private Sector Participation: In the 12th Plan, the need for working out PPP model for
infrastructure Port development Project was stressed. Active steps have been taken to fully
utilize the potential, resources and professionalism of the private sector. These include
standardization of biding documents, transparent bidding process for selection of PPP

These steps have resulted in several port PPP projects coming up in the 12 Major Ports.
At present, a total of 38 PPP projects are operational and 20 more PPP projects are under
implementation/construction.
(f) Development of Non Major Ports: The share of capacity creation at the Indian Ports is
constantly increasing. It has increased from 39% during 2011-12 to 43% during 2016-17.
The increase is due to number of private ports coming up particularly in the States of
Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra etc.

from 2012 onwards. It has doubled in the five year period to reach 5.063 BTKM in 2016-

91. The Committee is happy to note that the Cochin Shipyard has been strong in financial performance
during the current financial year. The Committee hopes that the targets will be attained at the end of
the Financial Y ear. (Para 72)
Reply of the Government
92. The observation of the Committee has been noted
Further Recommendation/Observation
93. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
94. The Committee notes that the Indian ship yards are less sophisticated and lacking world class
standards of equipment and manpower. Similarly low cost loans are not easily available for expansion
of the shipyard. The Committee recommends the following to support the ship building industry in the
country:

15
(i) The Government of India should take necessary steps to upgrade the current technology
used by the shipyards with the modern technology available in worldwide;
(ii) Periodic refreshment training of the existing employees may be conducted on regular basis
to familiarize with the latest technology;
(iii) Low cost loans may be raised from the overseas markets; and
(iv) Tax incentives to the yards as well as subsidies to the buyers may be expanded to attract
more buyers from Indian Market. (Para 73)
Reply of the Government
95. Government has been implementing a shipbuilding subsidy scheme to all the India Shipyards
including private sector shipyards. Many Indian shipyards borrowed funds and invested in new capacity
addition.
(i) Taking into account the need to expand infrastructure and promote growth and upgrade the
current technology it has been decided to execute two large projects namely (i) Construction
of large Dry Dock ( ` 1799 crores) and (ii) setting up a state of the art ship repair facility
(` 970 crores).
(ii) The employees are regularly trained to re-skill them for better and improved productivity.
Skill development of the employees is an ongoing activity in the yard.
(iii) For executing the two large projects namely (i) construction of large Dry Dock ( `1799
crores) and (ii) setting up a state of the art ship repair facility ( ` 970 crores). Funds were
not forthcoming from other sources and, therefore, CSL proposes to raise resources partly
by way of fresh issue of shares (IPO) and the balance by way of loans.
(iv) The import of capital goods for shipbuilding continues to attract customs duty. The shipyards
are subjected to corporate tax of 30%. CSL had made representations to Ministry of Finance
through pre budget memorandum to consider a lower rate.
Further Recommendation/Observation
96. The Committee notes the reply furnished by the Ministry of Shipping. The Committee
desires to know the impact of GST on the ship building sector.
Recommendation/Observation
97. The Committee has noted the assurances given by the Secretary, Shipping and recommends that
the Cochin Shipyard should not be privatized or disinvested as it is functioning well under the Govt. of
India control. (Para 75)
Reply of the Government
98. The recommendation has been noted for compliance. Presently, there is going to be a public issue
only to raise money to invest in the two large projects namely (i) construction of large Dry Dock
(`1799 crores) and (ii) setting up a state of the art ship repair facility ( ` 970 crores).

16
Further Recommendation/Observation
99. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee conveys its apprehension that CSL may
die due to lack of shipbuilding orders and the public issue of the CSL shares may subsequently
lead to getting the management control of CSL into private hands. The Committee recommends
that the Government should ensure that the management and operations of CSL remain with
the Central Government only.
SHIPPING CORPORATION OF INDIA LIMITED
Recommendation/Observation
100. The Committee notes the financial performance of SCI during the last 3 years. The Committee
further notes that the SCI has now recovered from its losses and is continuously making profit for the
last 3 years. The Committee desired to know the reasons why the income has shown declining trend in
the first half of the Financial Year 2016-17. (Para 80)
Reply of the Government
101. Majority of SCI’s fleet consists of Tankers and Bulk Carriers and the freight rates are based on
global market indices. The global tanker and dry bulk market indices both displayed a fall during the
referred period. Baltic Dirty Tanker Index (BDTI) fell from 833 to 625 and the Baltic Clean Tanker Index
(BCTI) fell from 495 to 352.
During the same period the TD3 (VLCC route index) fell from WS 88.18 to WS 38.85 and the
TD8 (Aframax route index) fell from WS 129.44 to WS 65. The clean route index TC1 fell from WS
104 to WS 54.69. The bulk market continued to be subdued well below the OPEX of the vessels.
102. The associated fall in earnings due to the declining market indices contributed to the drop in
revenues. In addition, revenues were reduced due to scheduled dry docking of the vessels.
Further Recommendation/Observation
103. The Committee notes the reply and understands that the global market indices are
determining the profits of the Shipping Corporation of India. The Committee recommends that
the Shipping Corporation of India should concentrate in the inland water transport also which
has a wide scope in the country.
Recommendation/Observation
104. The Committee also notes the ongoing fleet acquisition plans of SCI. The Committee recommends
that since the financial performances of the SCI has now improved to a certain extent, it may think about
more vessel acquisitions in the near future if the International market conditions remain viable.
(Para 81 )
Reply of the Government
105. SCI has envisaged 1 no. Resale MPSV, 1 no. Second hand VLGC size LPG carrier and 2 nos.
second hand Suezmax tankers in the current Annual Plan 2017-18. SCI’s strategy is currently to expedite

17
the above second hand acquisitions to augment existing tonnage to enhance cargo coverage and generate
immediate revenues. SCI will keep scouting the market continually for attractive second hand tonnage
and striking deals at favorable terms.
Further Recommendation/Observation
106. The Committee notes the reply.
NATIONAL WATERWAYS
Recommendation/Observation
107. The Committee notes that the IWAI is proposed to undertake fairway development and maintenance
of 8 National Waterways with an allocation of 
` 303 crore during 2017-18. The Committee also notes
that permission has been granted by the Ministry of Shipping to raise ` 1000 crore through bonds as
Extra Budgetary Resources and loan from World Bank. The Committee may be appraised about the
details of funds to be raised through bonds, IEBR and loan from World Bank. (Para 87)
Reply of the Government
108. Approved BE for the year 2017-18 under the Head “Grants to IWAI for creation of capital Assets”
is ` 102 crores. For North East Region (NER), an amount of ` 93 crore has been approved.
109. IW AI has raised ` 340 crore, out of the `1000 crore approved to be raised as Extra Budgetary
Resources (EBRs) during 2016-17.
110. The terms and conditions for the proposed loan of US $ 375.00 million for implementation of the
Jal Marg Vikas Project were finalized with the World Bank on 15.03.2017.
111. The Board of Executive Directors of the World Bank has approved the sanction of loan on
12.04.2017. The PIB has recommended the JMVP for approval at its meeting held on 06.03.2017. After
placing the JMVP for consideration and approval of the Cabinet Committee of Economic Affairs, a
request would be made to the Ministry of Finance for part release of the amount of loan by the World
Bank.
Further Recommendation/Observation
112. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee desires that development works of the
National Waterways should not face any fund shortage. The Jal Marg Vikas Project should be
implemented without any further delay.
Recommendation/Observation
113. Cargo movement through Inland Waterways is the most economical and environment friendly mode
of transport. The Committee notes that the growth of cargo movement through the IWT mode has not
picked up the required momentum. The Committee recommends that all the basic infrastructure requirements
such as navigation channel with sufficient depth and width, day and night navigational aids, terminals
for berthing of vessel and equipment’s for loading and unloading of cargo, etc. should be provided in
all the operational waterways for smooth cargo handling. The Committee also recommends that incentives
should be given to those goods carried by waterway mode. (Para 91)

18
Reply of the Government
114. The recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee have been noted. Accordingly,
under the Jal Marg Vikas Project, three multimodal terminals at Varanasi, Sahibganj and Haldia with road
and rail are to be constructed. These terminals will have state of the art mechanized cargo handling
facilities for quick loading and unloading of cargo. A new navigational lock at Farakka is under construction
with modern technology to facilitate movement of vessels much faster than the time being taken through
the existing lock.
115. Similar facilities wherever required based on the cargo availability and feasibility of the waterway,
will be developed in future.
Further Recommendation/Observation
116. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee, however, noticed that IWAI is focusing
only on very few projects all these years and there are no initiatives regarding development and
operation of many viable waterways in the country. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
apart from sticking on the Varanasi, Sahibganj and Haldia, focus is required on other waterways
projects also.
Recommendation/Observation
117. The Committee recommends that cargo movement through the water mode need to be entertained
in all the viable stretches so that the development of nation’s waterways may get a tremendous boost.
(Para 92)
Reply of the Government
118. IWAI has held consultations with various stake holders at Kolkata, Patna, Guwahati and Kochi to
explain the environmental benefits and reduction of costs in cargo movement through IWT and the steps
being taken by the Government to develop it as a more sustainable supplementary mode of transport.
IWAI has received commitments for movement of 9.5 million MT of cargo on NW-1.
Further Recommendation/Observation
119. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
120. The Committee notes that the pace of progress of works in the various National Waterways
development are not up to the mark. The Committee recommends that the IWAI should pursue getting
various environment clearances from the concerned authorities so that the proposed works may go on
smoothly. (Para 93)
Reply of the Government
121. The recommendations of the Committee have been noted. Action is being taken to get clearances
wherever required for the development of viable National Waterways.

19

122. The Committee notes the reply and recommends that further development made in the
matter may be furnished to the Committee.

123. The Committee notes that the initial studies and preparation of DPRs of 92 most viable Nations
