Reply of the Government
124. The recomm endation of the Committee has been noted. The Ministry of Finance allocates funds
to the Ministry of Shipping, out of which a portion is allocated for development of NWs. To provide
certainty for funding development of NWs, through an institutional mechanism, a proposal to allocate
2.5% of the Central Road Fund for the purpose, has been suggested by the Ministry of Shipping.
Further Recommendation/Observation
125. The Committee notes the reply.
PROMOTION OF CRUISE SHIPPING
Recommendation/Observation
126. The Committee notes that some Major Ports have started giving incentives to cruise ship visiting
their ports. The Committee recommends that apart from incentives, the ports may develop good passenger
amenities at the ports and also good passenger relations. (Para 97)
Reply of the Government
127. Apart from extending the incentives to cruise vessels, cruise passengers amenities are being
provided at all the five major ports that receive cruise vessels i.e. Mumbai, Mormugao, New Mangalore,
Cochin and Chennai have cruise berths.
128. A new modern cruise terminal building has been constructed at Murmugao Port and has started
operations in December, 2016. It has an area of about 1650 Sq. mtrs. Ample space is provided for car/
tour bus coach parking, Customs, e-visa, immigration, security, baggage handling, sorting, identification
procedures waiting / departure halls etc. Other than the above principle functions, the Cruise terminal
building also includes one cafeteria / snack, lounge, duty free shop, business centre, space for office
areas, dedicated counter for tourist information and hotel and travel reservations etc.
129. Mumbai Port Trust (MbPT) has an international cruise terminal with approx. 2500 sq. m. covered
centrally air conditioned hall. Passenger facilities provided at the terminal include custom and immigration
checking points, handicrafts and curio stalls, duty free shops, currency exchange facility etc. Further,
MbPT has taken the initiative for further development/upgradation of cruise terminal.
130. Chennai Port has modernized its Cruise Terminal to international standards at a cost of ` 17.24
crores with financial assistance from Government of India (Ministry of Tourism). This terminal has been

20
provided with all passengers’ amenities like escalator. A new passenger cruise terminal has been built in
Chennai with similar modern facilities for the cruise passengers.
131. New Mangalore has a full-fledged cruise terminal with all facilities like immigration, banking
service, facilitation centres, duty free shop and boutique. It has also constructed a cruise passenger
lounge near the berth with an area of 2150 sq. mtrs where all facilities like money exchange, ATM, locker
room, medical officers rooms, cafeteria and conference hall has been provided.
132. An international cruise terminal is functional at Cochin Port with an air conditioned space of 1500
sq. mtrs with single window clearance facility for customs and immigration. A proposal is under
consideration for upgradation of the existing terminal with the assistance of Ministry of Tourism.
133. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for cruise vessels has been operationalized in April, 2016
to facilitate passenger handling at the port.
Further Recommendation/Observation
134. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee desires that similar facilities at all the
viable major ports may be arranged for attracting more cruise ships and tourists to the Country.
Recommendation/Observation
135. The Committee also recommends that river cruise tourism may be popularized so that waterways
tourism may generate more income. The Ministry of Shipping should coordinate with Ministry of Tourism
in their domestic campaign so that the river cruise tourism may get a boost in the coming years.
(Para 98)
Reply of the Government
136. River cruise/ tourism has been a regular feature on National Waterways-1 & 2. Various cruise
operators viz. M/s Heritage River Cruises Pvt. Ltd., M/s Vivada Inland Waterways and M/s Assam Bengal
Navigation Company operate their cruise vessels on NW-1 and Sunderbans waterways. M/s Assam-
Bengal Navigation Company and M/s Far Horizon Company, operate cruise services on NW-2. River
tourism on NW-3 is already popular among domestic and foreign tourists. IWAI provides necessary
infrastructure like fairway, navigational aids and berthing facilities at desired locations for safe and
smooth sailing of cruise vessels.
137. A Working Group comprising of representative from M/o Tourism, Inland Waterways Authority
of India (IWAI), tour operators and cruise operators was constituted to examine the modalities of cruise
tours connecting religious places and other related issues. The Working Group has identified 5 Tourist
Circuits on National Waterways (NW-1) namely Allahabad, Varanasi, Patna, Bhagalpur and Kolkata Circuits
and 3 circuits on National Waterways II (NW-2) namely, Guwahati, Tejpur and Neemati Circuits respectively.
138. Various cruise operators operate their cruise vessels on NW-1 and NW-2. River tourism on
National Waterway-3 is already popular among domestic foreign tourists. IWAI provides necessary
infrastructure like fairway, navigational aids and berthing facilities at desired locations for safe and
smooth sailing of cruise vessels. Wherever the ports are in the vicinity of the national waterways,

21
dedicated inland water transport berths are being planned to evacuate the cargo direct from mothership
to hinterland through National Waterways connected with those ports.
Further Recommendation/Observation
139. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee recommends that river cruise tourism
may be popularized in other parts of the Country also.
Recommendation/Observation
140. The Committee would like to point out that as per the latest economic survey, India’s internal trade
has a much higher dimension than its international trade. The Committee therefore desires that there
should be a holistic coordinated approach needed for handling of trade within the country as well as
towards openings to the external trade. The Committee therefore recommends that the Government should
adopt a strategy for seamless flow of traffic especially through the National and coastal waterways.
(Para 99)
Reply of the Government
141. The recommendations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. Wherever the ports are
in the vicinity of the national waterways, dedicated inland water transport berths are being planned to
evacuate the cargo direct from mothership to hinterland through national waterways connected with
those ports.
142. Wherever national waterways are connected with the ports, such as NW-1 with Kolkata and Haldia
Ports; NW-3 with Kochi Port; NW-4 with Kakinada and Krishnapatnam Ports; and, NW-5 with Dhamra
and Paradip Ports, IW AI has already taken steps to ensure seamless flow of traffic from ports to
hinterland through national waterways. However, integration of coastal shipping with national waterways
to ensure seamless flow of traffic requires further examination since the category of vessel-worthiness
is quite different from navigation in inland waterways from the navigation in coastal waterways.
Further Recommendation/Observation
143. The Committee notes the reply.

144. The Committee also recommends that the Government would formulate a coordinated policy for
container size, dimensions and such aspects related to container traffic. (Para 100)
Reply of the Government
145. The containers are transported not only within the country but also from one country to another
country on ships. The container size and dimensions are decided by International Standards for freight

• Classification,
• Dimensions,

• Specifications,
• Test methods
• Handling and securing of containers,
• Container equipment,
• Coding, identification and marking, and data exchange (CEDEX)

system. The Committee recommends that a high powered inter-ministerial group may be constituted to
take policy decisions on internal trade and a high powered regulator for managing the entire area of
logistics of container. (Para 101)

148. The trade related issues including logistics are dealt by Department of Commerce. They have
earlier scheduled a meeting to consider the setting up of a Logistic Division in Directorate General of

proposed to be housed in DGFT, it is learnt, will coordinate on all trade related logistic issues.

149. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee may be apprised about the progress made

coordinated and integrated system for handling goods for Railways, Highways, Coastal Shipping Inland
waterways etc. may be worked out. (Para 102)

inland transport by rail for containers. Insofar as coordinated and integrated system for handling goods
for railways, highways, coastal shipping, inland waterways, etc, there are a large number of Multimodal
Transport Operators in the private sector. About 1267 multimodal transport operators are registered with
Directorate General of Shipping.
Further Recommendation/Observation
152. The Committee notes the reply.

Recommendation/Observation
153. The Committee notes that a lot of pollutants are dumped into the seas and waterways by the vessels
in the form of sewages, oil leakages etc. The Committee recommends that Ministry of Shipping may take
up the matter under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan seriously and necessary control measures may be put
in place to prevent pollution. (Para 103)
Reply of the Government
154. The recommendations of the Committee have been noted. Adequate provisions are being planned
to treat pollutants of ships and terminals through STPs. Necessary provisions have been kept in the
amendments proposed to the Inland Vessels Act 1917, to contain sewage, oil leakages and other effluents
likely to be generated through navigation on inland waterways. The draft Bill is under examination by
the Ministry of Law & Justice and is likely to be placed before both the Houses of the Parliament during
Monsoon Session of this year. Once the Bill is enacted, Inland Vessel Rules will be framed which will
be enforced by all the State Governments. As regards a pilot project to control pollution in waterways,
suggestion will be considered after the Inland Vessel Rules are framed based on the new Inland Waterways
Act 2017, likely to be passed by the Parliament in the monsoon session of 2017".
155. India is a party to International Convention on Prevention of Pollution at sea by ships (MARPOL
73/78) and other relevant convention applicable for prevention of marine pollution incidents. National
Legislation is in place to control and prevent pollution incidient caused by ships registered under Merchant
Shipping Act, 1958 and foreign flag vessels visiting Indian Ports. National laws/rules give the effect of
International Convection through the provisions made in Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, towards mitigation,
containment/control, removal or combat of oil spillage, whether accidental or otherwise. The Merchant
Shipping Prevention of Pollution Rule and formulation of contingency plan give effect to international
convention in order to take action consequent to any spillage incident whether accidental or otherwise,
the same can be dealt with.
156. Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP) and Shipboard Marine Pollution Emergency Plan
(SMPEP) or Vessels Response Plan or Garbage Management Plan or other plans, as applicable, are
maintained on board the ships to prevent and contain oil pollution incidents.
157. Indian and foreign flag ships are inspected at Indian ports under Flag State and Port State control
regime, so as to make sure that preventive measures on ships are in conformity to relevant international
convention.
158. National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan is being maintained to undertake oil spill prevention
and control measures. Lesson learnt are shared among the authorities/stakeholders and to update the plan
periodically.
159. The authorities in the major ports co-ordinate with the other local action groups as per requirements.
All major ports have been notified to have oil/garbage reception facilities as required by the Convention.
160. Accordingly, the pollution incidents are handled and control measures are taken to prevent pollution
under the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan on these set mechanisms.

161. The Committee notes the reply.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and
Culture, having been authorized by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this Two
Hundred and Fifty Fourth Report on “Action Taken Replies by the Ministry of Culture on the observations/
recommendations as contained in its Two Hundred and Forty Fifth Report on Demands for Grants (2017-18)
of the Ministry of Culture”.
2. The Two Hundred and Fifty Fifth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented on the 17
th March, 2017 to the Parliament.
3. The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its Two Hundred
and Forty Fifth Report was received from the Ministry of Culture on 27 th July, 2017.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on the 18 th December, 2017.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
recommendations/observations as contained in its Two Hundred and Forty Fifth Report on
Demands for Grants (2017-18) of the Ministry of Culture which was presented to both the Houses
of Parliament on 17 th March, 2017.
2. Action Taken Replies were received from the Government on 27 th July, 2017, in respect of all the
recommendations/observations contained in the Report. The replies have been categorized as follows:–
(i) Recommendations/Observations that have been accepted by the Government:
Paragraph Nos.: 7, 16, 38 , 57, 92, 95, 98, 106, and 113 Total: 9
(ii) Recommendations/Observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the
Government replies:
Paragraph Nos.: 28 and 31 Total: 2
(iii) Recommendations/Observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been
accepted by the Committee:
Paragraph Nos. : 22, 25, 34, 42, 51, 77, 86, 89, 110, 117 and 121 T otal: 11
(iv) Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still
awaited.
Paragraph Nos: 10, 19, 45, 48, 65, 68, 80 and 101 Total: 8
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of those recommendations/observations
which have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished at the earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of Action
Taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee contained in the Two
Hundred and Forty Fifth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry and recommendations/observations of
the Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs:
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation for 2017-18 is about 10.04% more than the budgetary
provisions at RE 2016-17. The Committee is surprised to note that the Ministry had to face a budgetary
reduction at RE stage in the previous financial year. The Committee would like to know the reasons for the
same.
(Para 10)
Reply of the Government
6. As against total budgetary provision of  ` 2500.00 crore at Budget Estimates (BE) 2016-17 which was
reduced to ` 2488.63 crore at Revised Estimates (RE) stage 2016-17, the budget for 2017-18 for Ministry
of Culture has been pegged at  ` 2738.47 crore. Ministry of Finance has not intimated any reason for the
reduction in Annual Plan allocation at RE stage during 2016-17. However, the Ministry will make efforts to
seek an additional allocation at RE stage during the current financial year 2017-18.

2
Further Recommendations/Observations
7. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
8. The Committee notes that the shortfall in budgetary allocation for 2017-18 is to the tune of
 ` 828.24
crore and that the Ministry of Finance has not intimated any reason for this reduction. Keeping in view the
crucial role played by culture in the Nation’s overall development and growth, the Committee is of the
considered view that with the present allocation, especially on the Capital side, it would be difficult to run
the existing schemes and other activities undertaken by the Ministry. Therefore, the Committee recommends
that the Ministry should actively pursue the matter of increasing the allocation at the RE stage in the current
financial year 2017-18, with the Ministry of Finance.
(Para 13)
Reply of the Government
9. The Ministry will take up the issue for providing additional funds with Ministry of Finance at RE stage
in the current financial year 2017-18.
Further Recommendations/Observations
10. The Committee may be apprised of the outcome thereof.
Recommendation/Observation
11. The Committee takes note of the expenditure made by the Ministry of Culture under the Plan and Non
Plan heads. At the same time, the Committee observes that under the Plan head for the financial years
2015-16 and 2016-17, better planning and supervision could have definitely improved the pace of utilization
and for achievement of set target. The Committee hopes that optimum pace of expenditure would be maintained
in future.
(Para 17)
Reply of the Government
12. The Ministry will continue to make all out efforts for optimizing the utilization of allocated funds
during the year 2017-18.
Further Recommendations/Observations
13. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
14. In this regard, the Committee impresses upon the Ministry that every possible step should be taken to
ensure that the stipulated outputs are achieved on time.
(Para 19)
Reply of the Government
15. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. The Ministry has prepared the output/outcome
targets under all schemes which are being monitored by the Ministry as well as NITI Aayog. Moreover,
Ministry signs Memorandum of Understandings (MoUs) with its organizations in which specific targets of

3
work are assigned. The achievements against the targets are monitored on regular basis at the appropriate
level.
Further Recommendations/Observations
16. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
17. The Committee recommends that an Inquiry Committee may be constituted to look into the facts and
circumstances which led to the delay in construction of the Institute of Archaeology. Based on the findings,
action may be taken against those officials found guilty and a report in this regard may be submitted to the
Committee. The Committee strongly recommends that effective and periodic monitoring of the various
Organizations under the Ministry should be done in order to avoid such delays.
(Para 22)
Reply of the Government
18. Ministry of Culture had in November, 2013 called for a thorough inquiry into the cancellation of plot
allotted by Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority (GNIDA) to Archaeological Survey of India
(ASI) for setting up of Institute of Archaeology and to fix responsibility of the officers responsible for the
same. Accordingly, a thorough examination of the progression of this proposal was conducted and a detailed
factual report was submitted chronologically by ASI to the Ministry of Culture for consideration and further
directions. The factual report in this regard was considered in the Ministry at the level of Hon’ble Culture
Minister. Thereafter, the matter with regard to restoration of the plot was taken up at the level of Secretary
(Culture) with the Govt. of U.P. and CEO, GNIDA. After vigorously pursuing the case, the plot has been
restored to ASI after fulfilling the conditions laid down by GNIDA. Further action for construction of the
building for Institute of Archaeology has been initiated after obtaining the approval of the Delegated Investment
Board (DIB). The work is being executed by National Buildings Construction Corporation (NBCC) and as
per the schedule of construction, the work is likely to be completed by July, 2019. The Project Monitoring
Committee is also constituted to monitor the progress of the projects. Further, periodic review meetings are
taken by the higher authorities in the Ministry to monitor the various organizations and MoUs signed by the
Ministry with them.
Further Recommendations/Observations
19. The Committee may be apprised about the progress of construction of the Institute of
Archaeology along with the names of the officers responsible for monitoring the construction. The
Committee further recommends that the Ministry should ensure that target is achieved within the
stipulated time.
Recommendation/Observation
20. The Committee welcomes the initiative taken to construct boundary walls for ASI protected monuments.
The Committee hopes that this will go a long way in preventing encroachment of monuments. The Committee
desires that a roadmap may be drawn for the construction of boundary walls for all the ASI protected
monuments and that existing timelines may be strictly adhered to. The Committee may be informed of the
progress made in the matter.
(Para 27)

4
Reply of the Government
21. The work for construction of boundary walls and toilet blocks at ASI protected monuments has been
assigned to Telecommunications Consultants India Limited (TCIL) and Water and Power Consultancy Services
(WAPCOS), the Government of India undertakings. Most of the estimates for construction of boundary
walls have been approved for which tenders have been initiated by the concerned agencies and the work is
in progress at some sites. The work order for some of the sites have been issued. M/s. TCIL & W APCOS
shall be instructed to ensure the time line of work orders.
Further Recommendations/Observations
22. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should take necessary measures to
expedite the work and ensure that progress of work is not stalled at any stage. The Committee may
be apprised of the achievements in physical terms.
Recommendation/Observation
23. The Committee is unhappy to note the non-implementation of e-Governance in ASI. The Committee is
of the view that in this era of rapid advancement in technology, it is essential that e-Governance is adopted
in a vital Organization like ASI. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take proactive steps to
ensure that e-Governance is implemented in ASI. The Committee may be apprised of the action taken in this
regard.
(Para 29)
Reply of the Government
24. The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has given all necessary approval with regard to development/
design of necessary software for implementation of e-governance in ASI.
Further Recommendations/Observations
25. The Committee is unhappy to note that the Ministry of Culture and ASI has not given any
details of the e-governance projects they are planning to implement. The Committee notes that the
authorities have taken some initiatives only after this Committee has come down heavily on the
inaction of the ASI to implement e-governance initiatives. The Committee recommends that the
Ministry should follow up the progress of development of necessary software for implementation of
e-governance in ASI and ensure that the implementation of e-governance in ASI is expedited. The
Committee may be apprised about the details and progress of implementation of e-governance
projects.
Recommendation/Observation
26. The Committee observes that e-ticketing enables the visitors to plan their visit to the monuments in
advance and help them to avoid the hassle of waiting at the ticket counters. Therefore, the Committee
desires that the facility of e-ticketing may be introduced in all ASI protected monuments.
(Para 31)
Reply of the Government
27. The online e-ticketing facility has already been introduced in all centrally protected ticketed monuments
of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

30. With regard to ‘Swatchh Paryatan Mobile App’, the responsibility of ASI is to redress the issue raised

31. The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation/Observation
32. The Committee welcomes the initiatives taken under Adarsh Smarak and desires that such improved
facilities may be provided in all the ASI monuments in a phased manner.
(Para 35)
Reply of the Government
33. With regard to the recommendation of the Committee contained in para 35, the suggestion and
observations suggested by the Committee are welcome. In this regard, it is pertinent to mention that in
spite of 25 Adarsh Monuments, ASI has already identified 75 monuments and Sites as Adarsh Monument
in second phase where tourist amenities such as drinking water, cafeteria, wi-fi, souvenir shop, Audio
Video centre and facilities for disabled may be provided. Out of the 100 Adarsh monuments 56 monuments
are ticketed while 44 monuments are not-ticketed. With regard to suggestions made by the Committee, it
is to mention that all ASI protected monuments and sites are not frequently visited by the tourists. Most
of the protected monuments in ASI are not being visited even by a single tourist. Therefore, the extension
of the facilities for all monuments in phased manner as suggested by the Committee does not seem
feasible as well as economical. In this regard it is proposed that the Circle Offices of ASI may be directed
to identify at least 5 monuments under their jurisdiction for upgrading amenities as suggested by the
Committee.

34. The Committee recommends that a feasibility study may be conducted by ASI on identifying
the Monuments which have the potential to be declared as Adarsh Monuments and the results of

Recommendation/Observation
39. The Ministry, in its written reply, has stated that nine and twenty-eight Demolition Orders have been
issued by the Archaeological Survey of India so far for the removal of unauthorized construction within the
prohibited/regulated areas of Zaffar Mahal and Qutub complex respectively.
(Para 38)
40. The Committee desires that ASI should ensure that the demolition orders are executed timely and that
the encroachments are removed.
(Para 39)
Reply of the Government
41. Demolition orders are being issued properly as and when cases of encroachments are reported. However,
the field officers of ASI may please be directed to keep regular visit and take appropriate response/ action
against the person as per provisions of The Ancient Monument and Archaeological Sites and Remains
(AMASR) Act, 1958 and Rules, 1959 and the eviction of unauthorized property for Public Premises (Eviction
of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971.
Further Recommendations/Observations
42. The Committee is not convinced by the reply of the Ministry. The Committee desires that the
Ministry should ensure that the field officers of ASI take appropriate action against the encroachers.
The Committee would like to know the number of encroachment eviction orders issued during the

43. In response to a pointed query as to whether legal opinion has been received from the Ministry of Law

(Para 41)
Reply of the Government

Circle level is being considered to expedite the cases with regard to encroachment and illegal/unauthorized

Recommendation/Observation
46. The Committee emphasizes the need for greater co-ordination between ASI and the State Governments
in the matter of prevention and removal of encroachments at the monuments. The Committee impresses
upon the Ministry to persuade the State Governments to form State level Co-ordination Committees for
prevention and removal of encroachments at the monuments. The Committee also recommends that a

(Para 42)
Reply of the Government
47. It is proposed that the SA’s/Dy. SA’s of Circles/Mini Circles would be directed to co-ordinate with

issues.

48. The Committee may be informed of the outcome thereof.

49. The Committee notes that the Ministry and ASI, New Delhi has stock of information on removal of
encroachment of only three circles. This shows the lackadaisical attitude of the Ministry and ASI towards

51. The Committee notes with utter dismay that even after six months the Government has not
submitted any quarterly report on encroachment to the Committee. It seems that the

Recommendation/Observation
58. The Committee observes that if its own organizations are unable to provide space for regional centre
of NSD at Kolkata, the Ministry should explore other possibilities such as requesting the State Government
to provide land/accommodation. The Committee desires that the Ministry may take necessary steps to
ensure that the regional centres of National School of Drama are set up at each of the places at the earliest
by doing the needful in this regard.
(Para 51)
Reply of the Government
59. It had been decided to open five Regional Centres of the National School of Drama (NSD) across the
country, viz. one each at Kolkata, Mumbai/ Goa, J&K and North-East Region besides upgrading the existing
Regional Resource Centre (RRC), Bengaluru to a full-fledged Centre. The land / accommodation for the
purpose was to be provided by the concerned State Governments. Accordingly all State Governments were
requested to provide land.
60. Only Karnataka Government has, however, provided accommodation as well as land for the purpose
where one year Diploma Course is already in operation.
In so far as Centre at Mumbai is concerned, NSD is in search of accommodation that may be suitable
for operationalizing the Centre. For this purpose, an advertisement has been published in the leading
Newspapers. As soon as suitable accommodation is found, steps will be taken to open the NSD’s Centre
there expeditiously.
61. NSD is following up the proposal with the State of Jammu &Kashmir and NE States to take a decision
at the earliest to provide a land / accommodation for the purpose of opening Regional Centre.
62. In so far as opening of Centre at Kolkata is concerned, as per the observations made by the Committee,
all Cultural Institutions under Ministry of Culture at Kolkata were requested to explore the possibilities for
providing accommodation to National School of Drama for starting a Regional Centre at Kolkata until suitable
land is made available to NSD by the State Government. However, the said organizations have indicated their
inability to provide accommodation for the purpose of opening of the NSD at Kolkata.
63. As per the observation of the Committee, matter is also being taken up with the State Government of
West Bengal for providing a land for opening of NSD at Kolkata.
64. Further, a meeting of Committee on Government Assurances, Lok Sabha was held on 08.05.2017 at
Leh to discuss the matter pertaining to assurance given to the Parliament on the subject. NSD has apprised
the Committee that a proposal to grant status of National Importance to the National School of Drama is
under consideration. Once the proposal to confer the status of National Importance is approved, the NSD
will be able to grant degrees / diplomas to the students who undertake the studies in the NSD and its regional
centres.
Further Recommendations/Observations
65. The Committee may be apprised in detail about the steps taken and the communication
undertaken between the Government of India and Government of West Bengal on providing land
for NSD at Kolkata. The Committee may be apprised of the progress made in this regard.

Recommendation/Observation
66. The Committee has observed that the outreach of the Central Akademis are not upto the mark to
preserve and promote a variety of culture and cultural activities existing at State level. Only the State level
Akademis can grapple with the issue and find solutions at the local level. The Committee is happy to note
that the Ministry of Culture is focusing some attention to the State Akademies which are in a poor financial
condition. The Committee desires that the proposals may be approved in a time bound manner so that the
Ministry of Finance may be requested to provide the requisite funds in time.
(Para 53)
Reply of the Government
67. Matter has been taken up with all three Akademies i.e. Sahitya Akademi, Sangeet Natak Akademi and
Lalit Kala Akademi of this Ministry. These Akademies have been requested to provide their comments along
with the proposal for providing the financial assistance to the State Akademies. A concrete proposal /
Scheme on the basis of the comments of these Akademies would be prepared and approved from the
concerned authorities and only thereafter a proposal will be moved to Ministry of Finance for providing the
requisite funds to be given to State Akademies. Reminders have also been issued to these Akademies on
16.05.2017 and 01.06.2017. Further vide this Ministry’s letter dated 13.07.2017, alongwith the information
already called for, all the three Akademies are again requested to furnish the details of the existing State
Akademies, their activities as also to apprise the Ministry as to how plan assistance could be provided to the
State Akademies by the Central Akademies.
Further Recommendations/Observations
68. The Committee notes that the Akademis are not responding to the communication of the
Ministry of Culture for a submission of proposals to provide financial assistance to State Akademis.
It is not clear why the Ministry needs the approval of Akademis to provide financial assistance to
the State Akademis. It seems that the Government is taking umbrage in the inaction of the Central
Akademis to provide assistance to State Akademis. The Committee, therefore, further recommends
that the Ministry should take initiative to assist the State Akademis. The Committee may be apprised
about the steps taken in this regard.
Recommendation/Observation
69. The Committee notes that the functioning of Asiatic Society has been deteriorated to a greater extent
and the society is embroiled in so many controversies including cases of sexual harassment. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry should take up a stronger measure to clean up the organization. The Committee
notes that the Asiatic Society, Kolkata is not responding to settle the audit paras. The Committee takes
serious note of the fact and observes that strict and effective monitoring should be done by the Ministry of
the Organizations coming under its control and that accountability should be ensured of the loss of public

the LIC took the responsibility to disburse the pension, all the beneficiaries were segregated in three groups
with three vesting dates i.e. 1
st April, 1st Oct. and 1st Jan. i.e. the dates from which Expert Committee, which
met on three occasions, recommended the pension to certain number of beneficiaries. However, for easier
administration/monitoring and efficient disbursal of pension to the beneficiaries, it was felt appropriate that
instead of piecemeal disbursement, pension to all the beneficiaries will be disbursed till March, 2017 and
then clubbed together from 1
st April, 2017 onwards. The Ministry held meetings with the LIC in which it has
been mutually decided that from 2017-18 the vesting date will be one only i.e. 1 st April. Accordingly, funds
will be demanded by LIC only once in the beginning of the financial year and the Ministry will release whole

observations/recommendations as contained in its Two Hundred Forty Eighth Report on Demands
for Grants (2017-18) of the Ministry of Tourism which was presented to both the Houses of
Parliament on 17 th March, 2017.

Hundred and Forty Eighth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry and recommendations/observations
of the Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs:
Recommendation/Observation
5. The Committee observes that the 12th Five Year Plan outlay for tourism development in the country
was ` 22800 crore. Out of it, the major chunk of allocation of ` 9450 crore was for development of
destinations and circuits. From the data provided by the Ministry of Tourism, the total allocations made all
these five years was only ` 5479.03 crore out of which the spending up to 31 st January, 2017 is ` 4644.89
crore. This comes to 20.37% of the 12th Plan outlay, whereas the total allocation itself was very insufficient
as compared to the outlay, which was only 24%. The Committee is very disappointed to note these figures
and desires to know the details of the reasons why such huge difference occurred in allocations to the tourism
sector during 12th Five Year Plan in the country.

(a) The share of India’s Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) in International Tourist Arrivals in the
world in 2016 was 0.7%. However, the International Tourist Arrivals comprises of 2 components
namely FTAs and Arrivals of Nationals Residing Abroad. Recently, Ministry of Tourism has
started collecting the data of Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) Arrivals. The number of International
Tourist Arrivals (FTAs + NRI Arrivals) during 2016 was 14.57 million. Accordingly, share of
India in International Tourist Arrivals of the world has also improved to 1.18% in 2016.
(b) The Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of the number of Domestic Tourist Visits (DTVs)
to different States/Union Territories (UTs) in India from 2011 to 2016 was 13.29% which is
above the stipulated target of Growth Rate of 12.16%.
(c) The Foreign Tourist Arrivals in 2016 were 8.80 million as against targeted 11.24 million. Foreign

Darshan scheme and funds have been sanctioned for development of above components under
various projects park under the scheme.
(d) Ministry of Tourism in collaboration with Ministry of Railways has identified 26 railway stations
for joint development of tourist amenities based on the popularity of stations from the tourism
point of view and has sanctioned an amount of `63.80 Crore for the Joint Development of
tourist amenities at 12 Railway Stations across the country. In addition, Ministry of Tourism had
mooted the idea of having glass top coaches on picturesque routes for an enhanced experience
to tourists. Ministry of Tourism has released `12.00 Crore for the manufacture of three glass
top coaches at the cost of `4.00 Crore per coach. One of the coaches has been deployed on the
Vishakpatanam–ArakuV alley Route.

(a) Ministry of Tourism has released Centralized Media Campaign Globally as well as in important
source markets of Asian and African Continent during the period of 12th Five Year Plan.

various tourist generating markets including East Europe, Middle East, ASEAN and African
Region by way of launching marketing campaigns, publicity campaigns, participating in travel
and tourism related fairs and festivals and helping the local travel – trade for promoting tourism
to India. Niche tourism products available in the country are also being zealously promoted by
Overseas Offices.
(c) Ministry of Tourism has taken the following steps for developing and promoting new tourism
products:
(i) Guidelines for promotion of Golf Tourism released in December 2010
(ii) Guidelines for promotion of Medical and Wellness Tourism released
(iii) Guidelines for promotion of Polo Tourism released
(iv) Basic Minimum Standards for Adventure Tourism released. Adventure Tourism Task Force
formed in December 2016.
(v) Cruise Tourism Task Force formed on 24th November 2015

(vi) National Medical and Wellness Tourism Board formed on 5th October 2015 under
chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister (Tourism) to provide dedicated institutional framework
to forward the cause of Medical Tourism, Wellness Tourism and Ayurveda Tourism and
any other format of Indian System of medicine covered by AYUSH.
(vii) Sustainable Tourism Criteria for India (STCI) for the accommodation, tour operators and
backwaters, lakes and rivers sectors launched in August 2014. MoU signed with Eco-

(a) During the 12 th Five Year Pan Period, Ministry has released Social Awareness Campaign “Ätithi
Devo Bhava” on TV/Radio and Outdoor Medium.
(b) Ministry of Tourism undertakes Swachhta Pakhwadas at various tourist destinations across the
country with the active involvement of the Ministry’s Offices located in various States and other
States/UTs Govts. Major cleanliness drives were carried out at India Gate, Jantar Mantar,
Nizamuddin Dargah, Red Fort, Qutab Minar, Mehrauli Archaeological Park, Sai Mandir, Purana
Quila, Lotus Temple and Laxmi Narayan Mandir during 2016-17.
(c) With the objective of promoting a sense of competition among the State and UT Governments to
achieve high standards of cleanliness in the tourist destinations falling under their jurisdiction,
Ministry of Tourism has decided to institute a National Swachhta Award from the Year 2016.

19 with a budget outlay of `43.20 Crores. The programmes under the SAP consists of
construction of toilets of world class standard, facilities for garbage collection system, solid
waste management system, etc. at selected tourist destinations. SAP also provides creating
awareness regarding cleanliness and training programs for various stakeholders, students, cadets
of NCC, NSS etc.

pilot basis at 25 locations of Adarsh monuments protected by Archaeological Survey of India
(ASI). A Nodal Officer at each of the 25 monuments has to ensure clearing of the garbage
reported and send an SMS to the complainant that his/her complaint has been attended to
successfully.

PRASAD Schemes and the Ministry is focusing on its development in the identified circuits.

toilets and on principals of universal access.

(a) Ministry of Tourism has taken several measures to ensure the safety and security of tourists
including foreign tourists:

Helpline on the toll free number 1800111363 or on a short code 1363 in 12 Languages
including 10 international languages and in Hindi & English in February 2016, for domestic
and foreign tourists to provide support service in terms of information relating to Travel in
India and also offers appropriate guidance to tourists in distress while travelling in India.
(ii) Ministry of Tourism has launched an initiative of presenting pre-loaded SIM Cards at the
Indira Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi and Cochin Airport to foreign tourists
arriving in India on e-Visa with the objective of providing instant connectivity.

tourism industry for Safe and Honourable Tourism with the objectives to encourage tourism
activities to be undertaken with respect to basic rights like dignity, safety and freedom
from exploitation of both tourists and local residents, in particular women and children.

to deploy Tourist Police in the States/Union Territories. At present, a total number of 14

(a) Adventure Tourism: Ministry of Tourism has formed a Task Force on Adventure Tourism to
draw up short term and long terms goals and strategies for the promotion of Adventure Tourism.
Ministry of Tourism had launched a two-year campaign “777 Days of the Himalayas” during
2013-2015 to centre stage the Indian Himalayas on the World Tourism Map. As part of the
campaign a TVC on Indian Himalayas and a Map of Indian Himalayas was produced. Ministry
of Tourism subsidized 50% of the Peak Fee charged by Indian Mountaineering Foundation from
climbing expeditions during the campaign.

8
(b) MICE: Ministry of Tourism actively supports the India Conventions Promotion Bureau in its
efforts for the promotion of MICE industry. Ministry of Tourism is marketing India’s MICE
capabilities by participating in trade fairs exclusively related to MICE like IMEX in Frankfurt and
Las Vegas.
(c) Cruise Tourism: Ministry of Tourism in collaboration with Ministry of Shipping has set up a
Task Force for promoting cruise tourism. The Task Force formulated Standard Operating
Procedure (SOP) and has appointed a consultant for preparation of an Action Plan for development
of Cruise Tourism in India. Ministry of Tourism has provided financial assistance to the ports of
Mumbai, Marmugao, Cochin and Chennai for developing dedicated terminals and facilities for

Medical Tourism, Wellness Tourism and Yoga, Ayurveda Tourism and other forms of Indian
system of medicine. Medical Visa rules have been streamlined and e-Visa facility can be availed
by visitors arriving for medical purpose.
(e) Wellness Tourism: India is promoted as a Wellness Tourism destination through Incredible India
campaigns. The National Medical and Wellness Tourism Board encourages accreditation of
wellness centres and the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Services
have released accreditation standards for AYUSH hospitals, Panchkarma clinics and wellness
centres.
(f) Golf Tourism: Ministry has released guidelines for promotion of Golf Tourism which includes
extending support to domestic and international Golf Tournaments to highlight India as a Golf
destination. Setting up of Golf Courses are eligible for financial assistance under the LRG Scheme.
Ministry also participates in Golf Tourism Trade Shows for promoting India as a Golf Tourism
Destination.
(g) Polo Tourism: Ministry of Tourism has released guidelines for support of International Polo
Tournaments held under the aegis of the Indian Polo Association.
(h) Spiritual/ Pilgrimage Tourism: The ‘National Mission on Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual
Augmentation Drive’ (PRASAD) has been launched by the Ministry of Tourism with the objective
of holistic development of identified pilgrimage destinations. 25 destinations have been identified
for development under the PRASAD scheme.

(a) The 2nd Tourism Satellite Account of India (TSAI) has been prepared for the reference year

prepared for the same reference year. The process of preparation of 3rd TSAI and 2nd R-TSAs

(b) A study was conducted in the markets of Turkey, South Korea, South Africa, Germany, Japan
& Russia to gauge the perception of tourists (past as well as prospective) about tourism in India

10
which could help in undertaking targeted marketing activities in the potential source markets.
The target respondents of the study included travellers (past and intending travellers to India and
other countries) and various service providers. According to the findings from the study, the
Indian cities most frequently visited by the travellers were Delhi, Mumbai, Goa and Agra. The
main reasons for choosing India as a tourist destination by past travellers were India’s culture,
Heritage and Scenic Tourist Spots. Among the intending travellers, primary attractions of India/
motivation for visiting India were found to be Scenic Tourist Spots, Monuments, Forts &
palaces, Museums and Variety of Food on offer.

Recommendation/Observation
11. The Committee notes the confidence shown by the Secretary, Tourism that by the end of the financial
year they would be able to spend the revised allocation of ` 1599.03 crore during 2016-17. The Committee,
however, notes that under the Head Assistance to Central Agencies for Tourism Infrastructure even 50% of
the allocation out of the 
` 70 crore has not been made so far. This trend can be seen also in the restructured
scheme of Overseas Promotion and Publicity including MDA where, out of the r evised allocation of
` 223.00 crore, the amount spent so far is ` 91.26 crore only. In case of North East Region, all the heads are
showing zero spending. The Committee is constrained to understand how the Ministry of Tourism is able to
spend the entire allocation within a period of two months time as claimed by the Secretary, Tourism. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should be more pragmatic in their approach in
implementing the schemes and spending of allocation so that the sanctions could be utilized systematically
without much hassle in the closing end of the Financial Year.
(Para 16)
Reply of the Government

spent ` 161.44 crore out of the Revised Estimates Limit of ` 1599.03 crore i.e. 97.64% of RE limit. The
Ministry has taken note of the recommendations of the Committee and suitable monitoring mechanism has
been built into the two flagship programme of Ministry of Tourism viz. Swadesh Darshan and PRASAD to
monitor the flow of expenditure and progress of works by the implementing agencies. Further, Secretary
(Tourism) takes weekly meeting to monitor progress of expenditure and its utilization of various schemes of
the Ministry.
Further Recommendation/Observation
13. The Committee notes the reply.

14. The Committee would like to know the reasons why the Ministry of Tourism could not spend the
entire allocation during 2016-17.
(Para 17)
Reply of the Government
15. The Ministry of Tourism had spent ` 1561.44 crore out of the Revised Estimates Limit of ` 1599.03
crore i.e. 97.64% of RE limit could be utilized by this Ministry. The minor variation between allocation and
expenditure is due to various factors such as pendency of utilization certificate, non – receipt of proposals
at right time from State Governments, etc.
Further Recommendation/Observation
16. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee is unhappy with the reply of the Ministry as
the reasons are vague and evasive. The Committee advises that lacunae such as administration etc.

I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and
Culture, having been authorized by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby present this Two
Hundred and Fifty Sixth Report on "Issues related to improving consumers' satisfaction of airlines".
2. The Committee heard the views of the Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation; Director-General,
DGCA; Director-General, Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS); Chairman, Airports Authority of
India and CMDs/CEOs of Air Asia, IndiGo and Go Air on the subject in its meeting held on 20th
November, 2017. The Committee heard the CMDs/CEOs of Spicejet, Jet Airways, Air India Ltd. and
Vistara in its meeting held on 27th November, 2017. The Committee again heard the Secretary, Ministry
of Civil Aviation; Director-General, DGCA; Director-General, Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS);
Chairman, Airports Authority of India in its meeting held on 4th December, 2017.
3. The Committee wishes to express its thanks to the officers of Ministry of Civil Aviation; DGCA;
Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS); Airports Authority of India; CMDs/CEOs of Air Asia, IndiGo,
Go Air, Spicejet, Jet Airways, Air India Ltd. and Vistara for placing before the Committee, the material
and information desired in connection with the subject and for clarifying the points raised by the

4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on the 2nd January, 2018.
