22. The Committee understands that this task is multi-pronged and will require the assistance
of various Ministries and Departments at both the State and the Centre. Hence, the Committee
recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should take the onus of coordinating with various
Ministries and Departments including the Ministry of Railways to ensure the smooth progress
and set a time- bound completion date for each project. Infrastructure gaps need to be identified
and action mobilized.
EFFICIENT UTILISATION OF FUNDS
23. The Committee notes that the development of the Buddhist Circuit since its conceptualization in the
year 1985 has moved at a snail’s pace. While funds have not been scarce, it is lacking in its implementation.
The Loan Agreement signed by the Government of India with Japan International Cooperation Agency
[JICA] in 2005 was for the implementation of Phase II of the ‘Baudh Paripath Project’  at a total cost of
approximately 396 crores. After inspection of some of the project sites in July 2012, the JICA conveyed
that the ground realities had changed since the signing of the Loan Agreement in 2005 and that the
continuation of the project would not be possible since implementation of the proposal would have enhanced
adverse impact on environment and society and the project would require compliance under a different
category. The project was subsequently dropped in 2012. The above incident is an example of the lack of
planning, coordination and implementation in the Circuit. Lost opportunities such as these are highly
detrimental to the development of the Buddhist Circuit in India.
24. The Committee was informed that the Ministry of Tourism did not have a separate budgetary
allocation for the development of Buddhist Circuit. The Ministry, in 2014-15, launched the ‘Swadesh
Darshan Scheme’. Under the Scheme, Buddhist Circuit is one of the fifteen thematic Circuits identified
for development in the country. The Ministry has sanctioned a total of `361.97 crores during the years
2016-2018, for the development of the Buddhist Circuit across the States of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar
Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh (the sites in Odisha are under consideration). However, out of
the amount mentioned, only `72.4 crore has been released between the period of 2016-18 (refer to table
in para 30). The Committee notes that the Circuit has also benefitted from the funding provided by the
Word Bank (International Finance Corporation). However, the results have been quite disappointing.

7
25. The Ministry, in its reply to a specific query on total amount of funds received from the World Bank
and the amount utilised so far, informed the Committee that the Ministry of Tourism, Government of
India, the Department of Tourism of the Governments of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh and the International
Finance Corporation (World Bank Group) together worked on the project of formulating a strategy for
up-gradation of Buddhist sites in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. The work on project is over and the strategy
formulated by the IFC “Investing in the Buddhist Circuit – 2014-2018” was launched in July 2014. The
total cost of project was ` 4.50 crore of which the share of the Ministry of Tourism was 50%, IFC 40%
and the States of Bihar and UP were 5% each.
26. The Committee notes that the reply of the Ministry does not mention the amount utilised so
far. The Committee may be apprised of the amount of funds released till date, amounts utilised
etc. in the Action Taken Report.
27.  As evinced from the table below, taken from the Demands for Grants No. 85 (2018-19) of the
Ministry of Tourism, the Ministry has a total budget of `2150crore, of which an amount of `1100 crore
has been allocated to the Swadesh Darshan Scheme and an amount of `150crore has been allotted to the
PRASHAD Scheme. Furthermore, it has been noted that a meagre amount of 0.01 crore has been allocated
towards the development of the Buddhist Circuit as a whole. The Buddhist Circuit is one of the most
promising Circuits with a huge potential for development. Buddhist sites are rich in traditions
and places of spiritual significance and are thus revered by millions of people around the world.
The Committee observes that ````` 0.01 crore translates to a meagre amount of ````` 1 lakh towards the
development of the Buddhist Circuit as a whole. The Committee feels that this token amount
allocation is grossly inadequate for the development of the Buddhist Circuit. The Committee is
disappointed to state that this token sum allocation is highly impractical and is evidence of the
lackadaisical attitude towards the development of the Buddhist Circuit as a vibrant and viable
tourist destination worthy of investment and the respect it deserves.

28. In this regard, the Committee observes that the full potential of the Buddhist Circuit is yet
to be exploited by the stakeholders. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry of
Tourism must pursue the development of the Buddhist Circuit with a renewed vigor and zeal.
29. The Ministry of Tourism, in reply to a specific query on whether the Ministry of Tourism hired
independent consultants or agencies for the monitoring, evaluation and audit of all Circuits and if there are
any mechanism in place to ensure the timely completion of projects undertaken under the various Circuits,
especially the Buddhist Circuit, informed the Committee that the implementation of projects sanctioned
under the Swadesh Darshan scheme are monitored rigorously by the Ministry of Tourism. The Central
Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee chaired by Secretary (Tourism) and Mission Directorate chaired
by the Joint Secretary (Tourism) reviews the progress of project implementation on periodic basis. The
Ministry also holds regional workshops, Video Conference and review meetings with the States and UTs
to review the progress of the projects. At working level, Swadesh Darshan Division along with Programme
Management Consultants and Domestic offices of Ministry monitors the projects for Cost, Quality and
Schedule. The Ministry has also developed an on-line monitoring portal to monitor the real time physical
and financial progress of the projects.
30. As per revised scheme guidelines of the Swadesh Darshan scheme, 5% of the project cost will be
paid to the implementing agency after successful O&M of Toilet, TFC, Cafeteria facilities for one year as

10
certified by an independent agency. Since projects sanctioned under the scheme have started completing
from this year, the Ministry is in the process of appointment of agency.
31. The target market of the Buddhist Circuit is primarily international tourists from East,
South and South-East Asia. These countries have wide and varied cultures from that of India but
are bound by our connect with Buddhism. The Committee, therefore, feels that it is insufficient
to place the Circuit under the Swadesh Darshan Division as its needs are different from those of
most domestic destinations. The Committee recommends that a separate, efficient mechanism
must be set in place, as it is evident that the one at present is not adequate to meet the needs and
requirements of the Buddhist Circuit. The Committee reiterates that the development of Buddhist
Circuit is integral to the development of tourism in India.
32. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Tourism must constitute an inter-
State-Ministerial Committee at the Central level to look into the disbursal and proper allocation
of the funds that have been set aside. It is also desired that a time-line may be set for the
completion of each phase and periodical updates may be sent to the constituted Committee in
order to ensure that the projects are completed.
33. The Ministry of Tourism, in reply to a specific query on whether there is any form of Monetary
Stabilisation Fund for the Buddhist Circuit, informed the Committee that the Ministry under its existing
schemes does not have provision to provide Monetary Stabilisation fund to Tour Operators to deal with
the issue of seasonality. However, the Ministry of Tourism under the Marketing Development Assistance
(MDA) Scheme provides financial assistance to approved stakeholders and Tourism Departments of
States/Union Territories for undertaking tourism promotion activities in overseas markets, including Sales-
cum-Study Tours, Participation in Travel Fairs/Exhibitions and Production of Publicity Material.
34. The Committee feels that it is important to understand that the Buddhist Circuit is largely
seasonal owing to the weather conditions. The winter season ranging from November to March is
the ideal travelling season. The seasonality of the Circuit is not conducive to a sustained growth
and the sites wear a deserted look during the off-season. This seasonality extends to rail and
flight services as well. In order to sustain tourism, the Committee recommends that an off-
season stabilization fund may be formulated to attract more tourists to make it viable for
businesses.
LACK OF CENTRE -STATE COORDINATION
35. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism had previously proposed a ‘Buddhist Circuit
Steering Committee’ to overlook and coordinate the different aspects of the development of the Buddhist
Circuit. However, there have been no further updates in this regard. The Committee in this regard, feels
that until there is coordination between the Ministry of Tourism, State and different Ministries both at the
Centre and State level, the Buddhist Circuit cannot achieve its full potential. There needs to be an ease of
access and direct communication between the Ministry and the concerned Departments with minimal red
tape.
36. The Ministry of Tourism, in response to a specific query on implementation of the Buddhist Circuit
Steering Committee and why the National Task Force (to be integrated State-wise and Department-wise)
has not been set up yet and the reasons for the same, informed the Committee that a National Advisory
Committee on Buddhist Circuit has been formed under the chairmanship of Hon ble Minister of Tourism.

11
The Committee has members from Government, Private Sector and Academicians working in this sector.
The Committee works as a think tank for development of Buddhist Circuit in the country.
37. The Committee is of the opinion that the lack of coordination and communication between
the various stakeholders has been a key factor towards the lack of success of the Buddhist Circuit,
despite the long gestation period and the availability of funds. Seamless inter-State coordination
is integral to the success of the Circuit. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry
should put into action the previously proposed ‘Buddhist Circuit Steering Committee’. This will
go a long way in ensuring the proper and timely development of the Circuit.
38. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should coordinate with
various stakeholders and ensure that project targets are set. The Committee also desires that
there must be greater communication with those at the local level in terms of project development
to ensure that projects recommended are feasible. Once funding has been granted, care must be
taken to ensure that the target completion date is set and all stakeholders including the
administration at the local level, are active participants in the development and maintenance of
the sites.
