with a task to chalk out solutions for delays being faced in the projects of the Ministry, 
in coordination with the stakeholders. This Cell may further analyze the impact these 
delays cause in terms of increase in expenditure incurred by the Ministry, loss caused in 
terms of GDP which would have been generated had the projects stayed on course etc. 
so as to portray a clear picture of the actual negative impact of delays in road 
infrastructure pro jects on the overall Indian economy. The Cell may be tasked to 
provide long -term solutions to the major issues faced in the road projects of the 
Ministry.  
(Para 178) 
WORK FINANCED FROM PERMANENT BRIDGE FEE FUND (PBFF) 
  The Committee hopes that the reduct ion in toll collection caused by the policy 
decision of the Ministry exempting tolling of projects costing less than Rs. 100 crore will 
not cause shortfall in the funding of NH works of the concerned States. The Committee 
recommends that the shortfall face d, if any, by the State Governments because of the 
policy decision, may be taken care of by the Ministry so as to avoid any delays in the 
ongoing projects under PBFF.  
(Para 180) 
STATE PWD AND BORDER ROAD ORGANIZATION (BRO) 
  The Committee would like to know the reason for huge variations in the 
percentage of funds allocated for Maintenance & Repairs in the various States and the 

83 
 
implications of the same, on the quality of road maintenance in the respective States. 
The Committee desires that a study may be undertaken to evaluate the quality of roads 
developed by State PWDs vis-à-vis NHAI and create a quality index. Such an index 
would push the State PWDs to make efforts to improve the quality of their Highways, 
enabling the Mini stry to motivate the low performing States for higher allocation of 
funds for Maintenance & Repairs of Highways.  
(Para 182) 
ROAD SAFETY 
  The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Ministry/NHAI to allow users 
to report an accident through the smart phone application NHAI Sukhad Yatra. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry/NHAI should tie up with the National 
Emergency Number 112 to provide its emergency services in case of accidents since an 
average road user cannot be expected to remember diffe rent phone numbers for 
accidents happening on a National Highway or on a local road. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry should look into addressing the issues being faced by the 
users with regard to the NHAI Sukhad Yatra application and take remedial steps.  
(Para 186) 
  The Committee notes that while the total number of road accidents has been 
decreasing since 2015, the number of fatal road accidents is increasing every year. The 
Committee would like the Ministry to evolve monitoring mechanisms for  adherence of 
road safety standards at each stage of road construction and maintenance.  
(Para 188) 
  The Committee feels that one of the major reasons behind road accidents is the 
poor condition of roads. Presence of potholes can prove to be fatal, even m ore so in the 
rainy season. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may make provisions for 
speedy redressal of safety concerns on National Highways. The Committee feels that 
given the vast stretches of National Highways in the country, allowing road us ers to 
report potholes, lack of lighting, and other safety concerns through the use of 
smartphone application would be very helpful to receive information on such issues, 
along with pinpoint location. The Ministry/NHAI may then forward the complaints 
received to the concessionaire, responsible for the maintenance of the concerned road. 
User feedback may also be sought on resolution of the reported issue. The Committee 
desires that such solutions may be implemented and sufficient fund be provided for that 
purpose.  
(Para 189) 
  The Committee recommends that the Ministry may seek higher fund allocation 
for Road Safety, Maintenance & Repairs of Roads and Driver Training Programmes 
for effective measures to be taken to minimize the road traffic injuries and deat hs, 
which causes irreparable loss of human lives.  

84 
 
(Para 190) 
  The Committee recommends that the safety of road travelers is paramount in 
each stage of construction and maintenance of road highways under the Ministry. The 
Committee further recommends that the Ministry may look into the feasibility of 
provision for lan ding of helicopters at designated spots on the National Highways so 
that quick response is enabled in case of road accidents.  
(Para 191) 
  The Committee recommends that the Ministry may set up a portal in order to 
upload the proceedings of the District Ro ad Safety Committee to ensure transparency 
and accountability of the same. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry 
may consider broadening the mandate of the Road Safety Committee to cover issues 
regarding road safety on all roads including rural roads, State PWD roads and National 
Highways since the Committee finds that the State Governments are often lax in their 
approach to ensure safety on roads.  
(Para 192) 
  The Committee recommends that road stretches where fatal accidents take place 
due t o bad condition of road or poor road design, sign boards may be put up as a 
precautionary measure and necessary remedial action may be taken. The Committee 
desires that the Ministry may furnish status reports on the action taken regarding such 
black spots.  
(Para 193) 
SAFETY OF WOMEN IN PUBLIC TRANSPORT SYSTEM 
   The Committee is distressed to note that only miniscule expenditure has been 
made in two schemes, while zero amount has been spent on the two other schemes of the 
Ministry. The Committee feels that  Indian roads are still unsafe for women especially 
those who travel alone and those who have to travel at night hours. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry may proactively take up the matter with the concerned 
State Governments and resolve the issue s which have stalled the execution of these 
projects.  
(Para 196) 
TRAINING AND RESEARCH 
  The Committee hopes that the Ministry is able to optimally utilize the higher 
funds allocated for Research, Training, Studies and Other Road Safety Schemes.  
(Para 201) 
  The Committee further recommends that the Ministry may make efforts to cover 
the entire country under its driver training programmes, in the light of the poor driving 

85 
 
habits of the average road user across the country. The Committee desires that the  
Ministry may explore the possibility of utilizing the MPLADS funds to carry out the 
driver training programmes in the respective constituencies of Members of Parliament.  
(Para 202) 
  The Committee appreciates the initiatives being taken by the Ministry t o bolster 
research and training in the Road Sector in India.  
(Para 206) 
CO-ORDINATION WITH STATE GOVERNMENTS 
  The Committee recommends that the Ministry should provide budgetary 
support to the State Government to bolster their public transport system, in  addition to 
the existing scheme of financial assistance to States/UTs for implementation of IT 
related projects. The Committee feels that pollution -hit States like Delhi, Haryana, 
Uttar Pradesh and Punjab should be given more funds to improve their public  
transportation systems and thus, possibly, put a check on the worsening pollution 
situation in these States.  
(Para 208) 
  The Committee feels that many of the projects of the Ministry face problems due 
to delayed action on the part of State Governments. The Committee recommends that 
the existing mechanism to coordinate with State Governments may be reviewed and 
revamped in order to improve the coordination between the Ministry and the State 
Governments.  
(Para 209) 
NEED FOR BETTER CO-ORDINATION BETWEEN MINISTRIES 
  The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministries of Civil Aviation, Shipping, 
Road Transport & Highways, Culture, Tourism, Railways  are not only inter -related 
and interconnected but also have a common objective to improve connectivity and 
better amenities for the benefit of tourists, travellers and faster movement of freight 
within the country. The Committee, therefore, feels that there is a pressing need for 
having an effective co-ordination mechanism among these Ministries so that the polic ies 
and guidelines being formulated by them are executed seamlessly and can supplement 
each other in achieving these objectives. This will not only increase effectiveness and 
efficiency, but will also help in utilization of funds and skilled manpower to th e 
maximum possible extent. Therefore, the Committee recommends that an easy -to-use 
interface should be made available which allows hassle -free communication and co -
ordination amongst them. A hotline number which is common to all these Ministries, 
may be es tablished so that whenever emergency arises, there can be effective and 
prompt coordination among these Ministries and issues in hand can be resolved at the 
earliest.  

86 
 
(Para 210) 
EARMARKING OF OBLIGATED ALLOCATIONS FOR SCHEDULED CASTE SUB 
PLAN (SCSP) AND TRIBAL SUB PLAN (TSP) 
 The Committee agrees with the Ministry‟s view that monitoring the beneficiaries 
especially on demographical distribution is not feasible in case of linear projects like 
National Highways. The Committee recommends that NITI Aayog may c onsider the 
request of the Ministry with regard to seeking exemption from mandatory earmarking 
of funds under SCSP. The Committee desires that the Ministry may furnish the 
updated status regarding the request it made to NITI Aayog.  
(Para 212) 
STAFFING IN NHAI 
  The Committee notes that NHAI shoulders the responsibility to implement a 
large portion of the projects of the Ministry and NHAI has been managing these 
 
sanctioned strength of 1890 posts. The Committee strongly recommends that the 
Ministry should look into the impact of the vacancies on the working of NHAI and take 
urgent measures to fill up vacancies existing in NHAI.  
(Para 215) 
MISCELLANEOUS 
CAG Report on Hyderabad-Bengaluru Toll Road 
  The Committee desires that it may be apprised of the response given by the 
Escrow Bank as to why it is not accepting the requests of the Ministry to recover the 
damages in this matter and whether legal action can be taken against them for the same. 
The Committee further recommends that the Ministry may take proactive measures to 
ensure that similar such cases do not recur in future.  
(Para 218) 
Curbing excessive usage of horns 
  The Committee feels that the average Indian road user is habituated to honking 
excessively which in turn contributes a lot to the noise pollution in big cities. Further, 
the Committee notes that the rules and laws are in place regarding fitting of loud hor ns 
on vehicles, but the same are not being implemented effectively. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry may run promotional campaigns, especially on social 
media to promote responsible usage of horns. The same idea may also be advocated 
through the Driver Training Center Programme of the Ministry.  
(Para 223) 
Timely clearance of payments to contractors 
onerous  responsibilities  with  inadequate  manpower  of   1081  personnel  i.e., 57.2%  of  its

87 
 
  The Committee appreciates the development of the „GATI‟ portal and hopes that 
the issues raised by the contractors/concessionaires/user fee collecti ng agencies and 
consultants are addressed on time. The Committee would like the Ministry to provide a 
platform to the contractors to report their feedback/grievances to the higher authorities.  
(Para 225) 
  The Committee recommends that the Ministry may lo ok into the feasibility of 
increasing the number of project milestones, especially in case of projects costing large 
amounts of money, as this will enable the release of payments to contractors in smaller 
instalments and reduce the need for contractors to finance huge amount of money from 
the lending institutions for long durations.  
(Para 226) 
Public Project Monitoring Facility 
  The Committee feels that the general public has the right to know about the 
details and exact status of an ongoing road project as the same would establish 
accountability and transparency in the road projects. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry may develop an easily accessible online portal wherein, 
inter alia, details, present status, progress achieved in the project and contact details of 
the officer(s) responsible for ensuring the quality of the project, may be uploaded and 
updated on a regular basis. This would allow road users and general public to register 
their grievances regarding the quality of construction/maintenance work.  
(Para 228) 
Promotion of Electric Vehicles in the country 
  The Committee feels that exemption to battery operated/electric vehicles from 
payment of registration fees would encourage more people to buy electric vehicles and 
would also address pollution levels across the country. The Committee desires that it 
may be apprised of the status of the same.  
(Para 230) 
  With the growing acceptance of electric vehicles in the country, the Committee 
feels that the Ministry should look into the issue of lack of noises in electric vehicles‟ 
engine by way of provision of an inbuilt mechanism to emit sound to alert pedestr ians 
and other vehicles. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may come up with 
rules/regulations prescribing certain minimum threshold of electronic noise which 
should be emitted by these vehicles so as to alert pedestrians and other vehicles.  
(Para 231) 
  The Committee feels that the traffic data available with the Ministry of Road 
Transport and Highways would be helpful for the Department of Heavy Industry in 
finalizing the locations of the charging stations for the electric vehicles, planned to be set 

88 
 
up across the country and therefore, recommends that the Ministry may coordinate 
with the Department of Heavy Industry in this regard.  
(Para 232) 
Installation of Electronic Weighing Bridges at Toll Booths 
  The Committee recommends that the Ministry may install Electronic Weighing 
Bridges at Toll Booths in order to put a curb on rampant overloading of trucks in the 
country. The Committee feels that doing so would prevent damage to the roads and 
bridges, besides improving road safety. The Committee rec ommends that the Ministry 
may explore whether the Electronic Weighing system can be tied up with the Electronic 
Toll Collection system wherein a vehicle can be identified with the help of the FASTag 
and if it is found to be overloaded, a challan is generated then and there for the vehicle.  
(Para 233) 
Coordination with Local Police Departments 
  The Committee observes that checking of documents by policemen often leads to 
slowing down of traffic and sometimes even leads to accidents when high speed vehicles 
fail to notice a vehicle that has been stopped for document checking by the police. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry may designate spots on the Highways, in 
consultation with the State police department, where the police could ask the vehicles to 
stop for checking of documents and/or vehicle. Provisions for the same could be 
incorporated at the design stage itself, wherever possible.  
(Para 234) 
Issuance of Fitness Certificate from anywhere in the country 
  The Committee feels that it is not always feasible for vehicle owners to travel to 
the city/State that they are registered in, in o rder to renew their fitness certificate, more 
so in case of long -haul truck drivers. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the 
Ministry should come up with a mechanism to permit vehicle owners to obtain fitness 
certificates for their vehicles from anyw here in the country by visiting their nearest 
local office.  
(Para 235) 
Core group on Safety and Security 
  The Committee emphasizes the need for a combined robust security framework 
to ensure safety and security in sectors of Civil Aviation, Road Transpor t & Highways, 
Shipping, Tourism and Railways. The Committee desires that in order to facilitate 
effective and periodic coordination among the concerned Ministries and agencies, a core 
group comprising officers at the level of Joint Secretary of the Ministr ies of Civil 
Aviation, Road Transport & Highways, Shipping, Tourism, Railways, Commissioner of 
Railway Safety and Petroleum may be set up to meet on monthly basis to chalk out 

89 
 
ways and means for addressing safety and security concerns in these sectors and ensure 
that international best practices are followed. This core group should be headed by 
Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation. In order to upgrade to international standards, 
the services of consultants (both domestic and international) who are experts in the 
respective fields and have domain knowledge, may be engaged for preparing Reports so 
that they can be implemented. This core group may serve as a think-tank and formulate 
guidelines and directions to improve safety and security standards in these se ctors. The 
Committee would like the Ministry to furnish the monthly Reports and status of 
implementation of its decisions, to the Committee.  
(Para 236) 
Pending road projects in Telangana 
  The Committee desires that Telangana  being a newly formed State, priority 
should be given to execution of pending road projects in both Telangana and Andhra 
Pradesh.  
(Para 237) 
The Committee desires that the Ministry may furnish reasons behind the delay 
in allocation of NH number to the newly announced National Highway from Hyderabad 
junction of ORR at Gowrelly to junction at Kothagudem on NH -30, via Valigonda-
Thorrur-Nellikudur-Mahabubabad-Yellandu in the Telangana State. The Committee 
notes that no maintenance activity has been done in respect of this road ever since it was 
declared as National Highway. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may take 
effective measures to resolve these issues at the earliest.  
(Para 238) 
Four-laning of National Highway connecting Thanjavur-Vikravandi 
  The Committee notes that the four -laning of National Highway connecting 
Thanjavur-Vikravandi is not progressing well and desires that the same may be 
speeded up by way of intensive monitoring, and NH -63 connecting Thanjavur to 
Nagapattinam may be expedited.  
(Para 239) 
Development of Sabarimala National Highway 
  The Committee observes that no funds have been earmarked for the 
development of Sabarimala Natonal Highway (NH -183A) and is of the view that since 
lakhs of devotees visit the shrine of Sarbarimala,  this project must be accorded priority 
and should be taken up without any delay and the hindrance coming in the way of 
development of this Highway should be sorted out in consultation with the State 
Government of Kerala.  
(Para 240)

 India has a long coastline of about 7517 km, spread on the western and eastern shelves of 
the mainland and also along the islands. Hence, Shipping plays a pivotal role in the economic 
development of the country. India has 13 Major Ports and about 200 Minor Ports. Approximately 
95% of the country‟s trade by volume and 68% by value is moved through maritime transport. 
Therefore, development of Major & Minor Ports and harbours, human resource and finance, 
maritime safety issues, training and skill development need to be strengthened. The Ministry of 
Shipping has been entrusted with the responsibility to formulate various policies and 
programmes on these issues and implement them in an effective and efficient manner.

6. The Committee notes that as against the projected demand of Rs 3328.70 crores for 
the Ministry for FY 2020 -21, an allocation of Rs 1800.00 crores has been made, leaving a 
shortfall of Rs 1528.70 crores. In comparison to the RE 2019 -20 stage allocation of Rs 
1523.40 crores, the increase in BE 2020-21 is of Rs 276.60 crores only, which, in the opinion 
of the Committee, is inadequate and will be eaten up by inf lation. The Committee gathers 
from the information made available to it that Maritime Transport is a critical 
infrastructure for economic development of the country and approximately 95% of the 
country‟s trade by volume and 68% by value is moved through Ma ritime transport and 
Shipping continues to remain unchallenged as the world‟s most efficient means of 
transportation. 
 

 
 
5 
 
7. The Ministry of Shipping which has drawn ambitious program for Port 
infrastructure development and capacity augmentation will become h andicapped because 
of the budgetary cuts which will jeopardize the targeted outcomes. The Committee takes 
note of the fiscal constraints faced by Ministry of Finance due to moderation in economic 
growth and the impact of global slowdown. Still , while seeking a balance between public 
good and need for containing fiscal deficit, the Committee would advocate higher 
budgetary provisions in favour of  Sagarmala Scheme and Kolkata Port Trust at the RE 
2020-21 stage. The Committee recommends that when the growth mo mentum is revived 
and the additional resources become available as a result of revenue buoyancy, the 
allocation for the Ministry should be increased further.   
8.       The Committee observes that there is a huge gap between the projected demand and 
the sa nctioned budget for the Ministry for the FY 2020 -21. As against the projected 
demand of Rs. 3328.70 crores, the Ministry has been provided with Rs. 1800.00 crores only. 
Obviously, such huge variation is suggestive of the shortcomings in the budgetary planning. 
The Committee would urge upon the Ministry to exercise due diligence in the budget 
formulation with proper planning and assessment , taking into account its needs and the 
capacity to deliver the functions assigned to it. 
9. The Committee notes that against the projected demand of Rs 350.00 crores for 
development of Major Ports, the allocation in BE 2020 -21 has been reduced to nil which is 
far below Rs. 107.00 crores in BE 2019 -20. The Committee would like to be apprised of the 
reasons behind the same. Similarly, the Committee fails to comprehend that no allocation 
has been made for Sagarmala Development Company Limited (SDCL), against projected 
demand of Rs. 250.00 crores despit e the fact that  SDCL was formed to provide equity 
support for the project Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) set up by the Ports / State / Central 
Ministries and formulate plans and policies for projects under Sagarmala Programme. The 
Committee apprehends tha t the prime objective of SDCL would get diluted with no funds 
allocated therein. The Committee would like a detailed note with justifications for nil 
allocation under the head “Sagarmala Development Company”.

67. Some of the main problems before the shipbuilding industry are as follows: 
(i)   Lack of economies of scale due to small order -book and due to lack of     dedicated 
domestic shipbuilding orders. 
(ii)  Lack of cheaper and long term flexible financing support from the domestic banking 
system for infrastructure investment and modernization. 
(iii)  Lack of access to cheaper working capital (including that available globally) due to 
restrictive External Commercial Borrowing norms. 
(iv)  Lack of competitive and domestic ancillary industry in the domestic industry due to 
small size and scale of the domestic shipbuilding industry thereby depending more 
on imports of shipbuilding components and equipment as well as reducing 
bargaining power on procurement of inputs. 

 
 
27 
 
(v)  Lack of capital infusion in the sector due to subdued investor confidence and 
pessimistic domestic outlook. 
68.    The following steps have been taken by Ministry of Shipping to promote shipbuilding 
industry:- 
(i)  Financial Assis tance Policy on Shipbuilding: To promote shipbuilding in Indian 
shipyards and to provide them a level playing field vis-a-vis foreign shipyards, the 
Union Cabinet had on December 9, 2015 approved New Shipbuilding Financial 
Assistance policy for Indian ship yards for contracts signed during a ten year period, 
viz. 2016 -2026 with budgetary projections of Rs. 4,000 crores for this period. 
Financial assistance is being granted @ 20% of contract price, fair price and actual 
receipts by the shipyard for the vessel  which is being delivered, whichever is least. 
Financial assistance is released after delivery of vessels. The rate of financial 
assistance will be reduced by 3% after every 3 years. 
(ii)    Right of Refusal to Indian Shipyards: The Union Cabinet has on 09 .12.2015 
approved that all government departments or agencies including CPSUs have to 
provide Right of First Refusal to Indian shipyards while procuring or repairing 
vessels meant for governmental or own use till 2025 after which only Indian 
shipyards would build and repair such vessels for above mentioned organizations.  
(iii)  Grant of Infrastructure Status: The Department of Economic Affairs has notified the 
inclusion of standalone „Shipyards‟ in the Harmonized Master List of 
Infrastructure Sub -sectors o n 13.04.2016. With this inclusion, shipyards will be 
able to avail flexible structuring of long term project loans, long term funding from 
Infrastructure Funds at lower rates of interest and for a longer tenure equivalent to 
the economic life of their asse ts, relaxed ECB norms, issuance of infrastructure 
bonds for meeting working capital requirements. 
69. The Secretary, Ministry of Shipping, while deposing before the Committee on the 
Demand for Grants (2020-21), stated:- 
“We have a scheme for shipbuilding t hrough the shipyards where the private shipyards 
are also eligible to build ships and where the Government of India provides some 
percentage as subsidy. The amount of subsidy is fixed as per the time-limit.” 
70. The Committee finds that the shipbuilding industry is facing certain financial and 
infrastructural bottlenecks which tend to push back the progress of Shipping industry. 
India has meager contribution of 1 percent in terms of its share in global shipbuildin g 
sector. In a bid to give major push to shipbuilding industry, the Government has unleashed 
a slew of initiatives like formulation of Financial Assistance Policy on shipbuilding in 2015, 
provisions of Government departments including Central Public Sector  Undertakings 

 
 
28 
 
giving right of first refusal to Indian shipyards while procuring or repairing vessels for 
Governmental or its own use and grant of infrastructure status to Indian shipbuilding 
industry. Smaller countries like Vietnam and Philippines are ahea d of India in terms of 
shipbuilding. The Committee observes that a vibrant shipbuilding industry contributes to 
national GDP by way of employment generation and creation of business opportunities and 
shipbuilding and  therefore, can contribute immensely to the vision of making India a 5 
Trillion Dollar economy. It is , therefore, imperative for the Government to encourage the 
indigenous shipbuilding ecosystem. The Committee is also of the opinion that shipbuilding 
is a capital int ensive infrastructure industry and therefore, PPP is the way forward. The 
Committee also recommends that the Ministry must revisit its strategies to enhance the 
country‟s global competitiveness in manufacturing of warships and also to build ship 
equipments for Merchant Shipping.

ships at sea; (ii) prevention of marine pollution; and (iii) mandatory regulations of the 
International Maritime Organizations for effective implementation including promotion of 
maritime education and training, examination & certification of seafarers a nd supervision of 
other subordinate offices for their effective functioning etc.

International Oil Pollution Prevention (IOPP) Surveys -The Classification Societies 
(ROs) are also responsible for survey and certification for Oil Pollution under the various 
Annexes of MARPOL 73/38 Convention.

possess a certif icate called Continuous Discharge Certificate (CDC) to be able to work on an

KOLKATA PORT TRUST 
115. To a query whether the Kolkata Port Trust is being granted maintenance dredging 
subsidy over the years in terms of the decision of the Government, the Ministry has clarified that 
Major Ports are meeting their dredging expenditure through their Internal & Extra Budgetary 
Resources (IEBR). The internal resources are generated through port services such as pilotage, 
berth hire, storage, lease rentals etc. As regards Kolkata Port Trust, subsidy for dredging and 
river maintenance in the river Hooghly should not  be considered in isolation but viewed in the 
overall context of the national interest. 
 
116. Kolkata Port Trust established Dredger and Despatch Service and Department of Chief 
Hydraulic Engineer for undertaking dredging works and maintenance of the river  channel to 
counter the menace of siltation.  Based on the reports of several expert committees the Union 
Cabinet approved 80% river dredging subsidy from 01.04.1976.  This system of providing 
dredging subsidy is being continued and Government of India app roved dredging subsidy of 
Rs.998.08 cr. to Kolkata Port Trust for the period from 2016-17 to 2019-20. 
 
117. Further, cargo traffic has been showing a consistent growth for the last five years and the 
operating surplus of Kolkata Port Trust has improved fro m Rs.384.70 cr. in 2014 -15 to 
Rs.897.51 cr. in 2018 -19.  However, holding the Kolkata Port Trust entirely responsible for 
funding the dredging and river conservation requirements for maintenance of the 232 km channel 
may not be in the public interest.  The  river channel is vital for the existence of the port and only 
with the availability of adequate draft can the Kolkata Port justify its sustainable existence. 
 
118. The Committee notes that due to extensive use of Ganga water and bank and bed 
erosion in the upstream states, the Hooghly estuary underwent substantial changes and the 
silt that used to be flushed out into the Bay of Bengal through this river channel started to 
be deposited due to reduction in the volume of river water.  It is, therefore, essent ial that 
the existing system of subsidy for dredging and river conservancy works of the Kolkata 

 
 
46 
 
Port Trust should be cautiously monitored and progress be evaluated at regular intervals 
of time. 
 
NEED FOR COORDINATION BETWEEN MINISTRIES 
119. The Committee i s of the opinion that the Ministries of Civil Aviation, Shipping, 
Road Transport & Highways, Culture, Tourism and  Railways  are not only inter -related 
and interconnected, but also share a common objective to improve connectivity and better 
amenities for th e benefit of tourists, travellers and faster movement of freight within the 
country. The Committee, therefore, feels that there is a pressing need for having an 
effective co -ordination mechanism among these Ministries so that the policies and 
guidelines be ing formulated by them are executed seamlessly and can supplement each 
other in achieving these objectives. This will not only increase effectiveness and efficiency, 
but will also help in utilization of funds and skilled manpower to the maximum possible 
extent. Therefore, the Committee recommends that an easy -to-use interface should be 
made available which allows hassle -free communication and co -ordination amongst them. 
A hotline number which is common to all these Ministries, may be established so that 
whenever emergency arises, there can be effective and prompt coordination among these 
Ministries and issues in hand can be resolved at the earliest. The above said Ministries 
should work together in this regard and the Ministry of Tourism may be made the noda l 
Ministry for this purpose. 
 
CORE GROUP ON SAFETY AND SECURITY 
120.  The Committee emphasizes the need for a combined robust security framework to 
ensure safety and security in sectors of Civil Aviation, Road Transport &  Highways, 
Shipping, Tourism and Railways. The Committee desires that in order to facilitate effective 
and periodic coordination among the concerned Ministries and agencies, a core group 
comprising officers at the level of Joint Secretary of the Ministries  of Civil Aviation, Road 
Transport & Highways, Shipping, Tourism, Railways, Commissioner of Railway Safety 
and Petroleum may be set up to meet on monthly basis to chalk out ways and means for 
addressing safety and security concerns in these sectors and ens ure that international best

Aviation. In order to upgrade to international standards, the services of consultants (both

121. The Committee takes note of the fact that the East Coast Canal in the Balasore 
district of Odisha has been declared as the NW -5 and the vast agricultural land on both 
sides of the canal depends on the drainage of water during heavy rain in the rainy season. 

 
 
47 
 
During summer season , rabi crops used to be irrigated from this canal. Further, it notes 
that due to negligence of authorities, growth of wild shrubs and grass makes the little water 
available, poisonous and it dysfunctions the lift irrigation pumps during summers. They 
also act as a blockade for drainage of water during rainy season, making the area  marshy, 
waterlogged and breeding ground for snakes. Therefore, the Committee desires that the 
Ministry should clean the canal from wild shrubs and let the water flow to and fro so that 
sufficient water is available for irrigation during the summer season.  The Committee 
further recommends that water gates at Bhograi lock should be maintained and regular 
dredging of the canal should be undertaken by constructing proper embankments to 
maintain fertility and safety in the East Coast Canal.

          (Para: 6) 
 The Ministry of Shipping which has drawn ambitious progra m for Port 
infrastructure development and capacity augmentation will become handicapped because 
of the budgetary cuts which will jeopardize the targeted outcomes. The Committee takes 
note of the fiscal constraints faced by Ministry of Finance due to modera tion in economic 
growth and the impact of global slowdown. Still , while seeking a balance between public 
good and need for containing fiscal deficit, the Committee would advocate higher 
budgetary provisions in favour of  Sagarmala Scheme and Kolkata Port Tr ust at the RE 
2020-21 stage. The Committee recommends that when the growth momentum is revived 
and the additional resources become available as a result of revenue buoyancy, the 
allocation for the Ministry should be increased further.  
(Para: 7) 
       The Committee observes that there is a huge gap between the projected demand and 
the sanctioned budget for the Ministry for the FY 2020 -21. As against the projected 
demand of Rs. 3328.70 crores, the Ministry has been provided with Rs. 1800.00 crores only. 
Obviously, such huge variation is suggestive of the shortcomings in the budgetary planning. 
The Committee would urge upon the Ministry to exercise due diligence in the budget 
formulation with proper planning and assessment , taking into account its needs and t he 
capacity to deliver the functions assigned to it.         
(Para: 8) 
 The Committee notes that against the projected demand of Rs 350.00 crores for 
development of Major Ports, the allocation in BE 2020 -21 has been reduced to nil which is 

 
 
49 
 
far below Rs. 107.00 crores in BE 2019-20. The Committee would like to be apprised of the 
reasons behind the same. Similarly, the Committee fails to comprehend that no allocation 
has been made for Sagarmala Development Company Limited (SDCL), against projected 
demand of  Rs. 250.00 crores despite the fact that  SDCL was formed to provide equity 
support for the project Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) set up by the Ports / State / Central 
Ministries and formulate plans and policies for projects under Sagarmala Programme. The 
Committee apprehends that the prime objective of SDCL would get diluted with no funds 
allocated therein. The Committee would like a detailed note with justifications for nil 
allocation under the head “Sagarmala Development Company”.       
 (Para: 9) 
SALIENT FEATURES OF DEMANDS FOR GRANTS 2020-21    
 The Committee takes note of the reply from the Ministry regarding developing new 
project MIS tool for Sagarmala Programme and National Maritime Heritage Complex at 
Lothal. The Committee applauds the Ministry fo r the efforts, but feels that main emphasis 
should be laid on completion of ongoing and stalled projects under the said programme. 
There should be regular monitoring of funds at each level of work and Committee should 
be apprised of the progress made in this regard.        
 (Para: 11) 
ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2019-20  
 The scrutiny of Annexure I reveals  significant variation between Budget Estimates, 
Revised Estimates and Actual Expenditure under various heads during the financial year 
2019-20. For instance,  Rs 150.00 crores and Rs 200.00 crores allocated at the stage of BE 
2019-20 under the heads “Saga rmala Schemes and Projects” and “Other Schemes under 
Sagarmala” respectively were reduced to Rs 98.26 crores and Rs 32.60 crores at the RE 
stage and the actual expenditure incurred till 31.01.2020 is only Rs 60.79 crores and Rs 
32.60 crores respectively. S imilarly, against RE 2019 -20 of Rs 42.43 crores, which was a 
reduction from BE of Rs 97.00 crores for the head “Assistance to Ship Building, Research 
and Development”, the Ministry has been able to incur an expenditure of only a meager Rs 
18.43 crores till 31.01.2020.  
                 (Para: 15) 
 Rs. 450.00 crores was allocated under the head “Grants to Inland Water Transport 
Authority of India”, which was reduced to Rs 236.51 crores at RE stage and the Ministry 
has spent Rs 192.20 crores till 31.01.2020. Since, as per the norms stipulated by the 
Ministry of Finance, there is a ceiling of 25% on expenditure in the last quarter and it 
should not be more than 10% of the BE in the month of March, the Committee apprehends 
substantial underutilization of the budgeted fund under the above heads.   
            (Para: 16) 
 The Committee expresses its displeasure at this significant variation between Budget 
Estimates and Revised Estimates which is indicative of serious shortcoming in the 
budgetary planning and monito ring of utilization of the budgeted funds. The Committee, 

 
 
50 
 
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should take corrective measures to arrest such an 
erratic trend of projection of fund requirements and be more prudent in their Budget 
formulation and make their estimates only after proper assessment and planning.          
  (Para: 17) 
 The Committee notes that a sum of Rs 380.00 crores was proposed in BE 2019 -20 
under the head “Director General of Lighthouses and Lightships”, which was steeply 
revised upward to Rs 413.00 crores  at the RE 2019 -20 stage. The Ministry has spent Rs 
278.00 crores till 31.01.2020, leaving 32.45% for expenditure in the last two months of the 
current fiscal year. Since the remaining expenditure would have to be squeezed in the last 
two months of the current financial year, the Committee apprehends the occurrence of 
saving under this head. The Committee also notes that the allocation of Rs 60.00 crores 
under the Capital head of the scheme was reduced to Rs 43.78 crores  at the RE 2019 -20 
stage, which points to the fact that development oriented activities under the scheme have 
been curtailed. The Committee, while strongly disapproving such variations between BE, 
RE and Actual expenditure for „Director General of Lighthouses and Lightshi ps‟ urges the 
Ministry to avoid such ritualistic allocations which remain on paper only. The  Committee 
also recommends that the Ministry should pay special attention and take proactive steps to 
avoid the occurrence of savings under the scheme because a res ource constrained country 
like India cannot afford to keep a vast chunk of its financial resources locked up and 
surrendered towards the end of financial year. The Committee desires to be kept apprised 
of the quantum of savings under the above scheme for 2019-20.  
                    (Para: 18) 
PORT CAPACITY- ADDITION WORK 
 The Committee observes that in Major Ports productivity in terms of ship turn -
around time, waiting time and average output ship berthday continues to be modest when 
compared with global standards and performance of Ports in developed maritime 
countries. Since globalization, rapid adoption of technology and competitiveness are critical 
objectives to the exporters and importers in India, modernization of Major Ports is critical 
to the succe ss of their supply chain objectives. It is in this context that, the capacity 
addition at five Ports, namely, Deendayal Port Trust, Mormugao Port Trust, V.O. 
Chidambaranar Port Trust, Cochin Port Trust and Visakhapatnam Port Trust assumes 
added significanc e. The Committee desires that the progress of implementation of these 
projects should be monitored regularly and that proper guidelines should be issued for 
their timely completion. The Committee also desires to know whether traffic flows at the 
above Ports have shown any correlation with the GDP subsequent to the capacity addition 
during 2019-20.       
    (Para: 20) 
The Committee observes that the parameter of average Turn -around time does not 
indicate how efficient a Port is. One commonly used parameter which is used to assess a 
Port‟s internal efficiency is the quantum of cargo that the Port handles per day (i.e. ou tput 
ship per berthday). The Committee desires to be apprised of the output per ship berthday 

 
 
51 
 
of the above Ports subsequent to the improvement of average Turn -around time and also 
the reasons for little or no improvement in the average Turn -around time in other Major 
Ports.            
  (Para: 23) 
The Committee notes that a number of PPP projects involving capacity addition are 
under implementation. The Committee observes that the count ry's international trade is 
growing fast which warrants creation of adequate Port infrastructure and capacity. Since 
projects are capital intensive, the resources required to build the Port infrastructure are 
much larger and therefore , public investment has to be supplemented in private sector 
investment in Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode. The Committee desires to be 
apprised as to what extent PPPs have been able to augment resource availability and also 
minimize time overrun and cost escalation in construction of Port projects. The Committee 
also desires to know whet her the Model Concession Agreement of 2008 has succeeded in 
obviating the problems faced in execution of PPP projects and make the investment in Port 
sector attractive.   
 (Para: 25) 
CARGO HANDLING CAPACITY 
 The Committee finds that despite adequate alloca tion of funds towards the 
development and modernization of Major Ports, the cargo handling capacity has not shown 
proportionate improvements and that there remains a big difference in cargo handling 
performance between the Indian Major Ports and Port of Si ngapore. The Committee is of 
the opinion that introduction of major technological changes in the Indian Major Ports can 
provide stimulus for cargo handling.  
            (Para: 27) 
 The Committee also recommends that uneconomic practices coming in the way of 
efficient operations should be identified and reviewed to bring down the cost of cargo 
handling at the Major Ports.       
 (Para: 28) 
AVERAGE OUTPUT SHIP BERTHDAY 
 On comparison of the above figures of 2019 -20 with data of 2018 -19, it has been 
noticed that there was improvement only in 6 ports viz., Haldia, Visakhapatnam, Cochin, 
Mormugao, Mumbai and JNPT.  However, in Ports of Kolkata, Paradip, Kamarajar, 
Chennai, V.O. Chidambaranar, New Mangalore and Deendayal, the average Output Per 
Ship Berthday is even less than that of 2018 -19. The Committee desires that the Ministry 
should look into the reasons for the decrease in average Output Per Ship Berthday of 7 
Ports mentioned above and take remedial measures.    
    (Para: 30) 
TRAFFIC HANDLING AT MAJOR PORTS 
 The Committee notes that only seven Major Ports were able to register positive 
growth in traffic handling parameter, while the remaining Major Ports were in the 

 
 
52 
 
negative. The Committee is of the view that the Ports which ha ve showed negative growth , 
except MoPT, were among the top performers in 2017 -18 in terms of traffic growth. This 
performance does not match with huge funding from Government for various Port 
enhancement programmes and schemes especially designed for Major Ports.  
      (Para: 33) 
 The Committee desires to know whether the negative growth of the traffic handled 
at the 6 Ports is a result of competition from minor Ports due to their growth rates and 
huge capacity addition through private sector. The Committe e also desires to be apprised 
of the remedial measures taken to arrest this trend.  
            (Para: 34) 
PERFORMANCE OF PORTS 
  The Committee observes that the parameters of Average Turn -around time 
and Average Output Per Ship Berthday are not much in vogue in international Ports in 
terms of international best practices. One such parameter widely used internationally is 
“average moves per crane hour”. With the advent of full scale containerization of general 
cargo, Ports have witnessed paradigm shift in  terms of commissioning of container 
terminals. The Committee  would, therefore, like the Ministry to apply the yardstick of 
“Average moves per crane hour” to measure the performance of the Major Ports. The 
Committee desires to be kept apprised in this regard. 
         (Para: 36) 
MODERNIZATION OF PORTS 
 The Committee recommends that the Ministry should recalibrate its policies and 
strategies to keep pace with the growing EXIM Trade and equipped the Ports with 
adequate capacity to handle various types of carg o.  Special focus is required for creation 
of additional capacity at Major Ports through infrastructure development projects and 
introduction of modern technology. The Ministry should formulate policies and schemes 
aiming at mechanization of operations and  introduction of modern technique for cargo 
handling particularly in dry bulk cargo to improve performance of the Major Ports. 
Modernization of Port administration should also be undertaken. The Committee also 
observes that tremendous scope exists in the M ajor Ports to modernize existing 
conventional berths and to convert some of them to dedicated or multipurpose terminals.  
                 (Para: 41) 
 The Committee takes note of the initiatives taken for modernization of Minor Ports 
and recommends that specialized Minor Ports should also be developed as an integral part 
of the overall Port system.   
    (Para: 42) 
CONNECTIVITY TO PORTS 
 Lack of rail and road networks has emerged as a major constraint for the Major 
Ports. The Committee observes that connectivity projects are capital intensive and have 
substantial gestation period as they become economically viable over long  periods of time. 
The Committee would, therefore, like to know the financial model for implementation of 

 
 
53 
 
the rail -road connectivit y projects including sources of their funding and the extent to 
which such models are viable in India. The Committee is dismayed to note that the 
Ministry has extended timelines for execution of almost three -fourth of the number of 
projects whereas the emp hasis should have been on timely and speedy completion of 
connectivity projects. The Ministry should also focus on implementing connectivity 
projects to link Minor Ports to metropolitan cities and State capitals. Processes for all 
necessary clearances shou ld be initiated well in advance to avoid undue bottlenecks and 
clearance issues.      
        (Para: 44) 
 The Committee desires to be updated on the progress made towards route 
rationalization for Visakhapatnam and Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) connecti vity to 
Deendayal Port.       
   (Para: 46) 
 Taking cognizance of the fact that a number of projects for widening and upgrading 
the roads and interlinking them are under implementation, the Committee recommends 
that a dedicated monitoring mechanism be put in place to ensure completion of these 
projects within the approved cost and designated timeline. The Committee desires to be 
kept apprised of the measures taken in this regard.  
         (Para: 48) 
SAGARMALA  
 The Committee expresses it s deep concern that an amount of Rs. 150.00 crores was 
allocated in BE 2019 -20 for Sagarmala Projects/ Schemes which got reduced to Rs 98.26 
crores at the RE 2019 -20 stage because many projects approved under this scheme could 
not be funded due to statutory  clearances. This speaks of very poor planning and fiscal 
discipline as the budgeted funds have been kept locked up for want of approvals. The

 The Committ ee notes the reply of the Ministry and desires to know whether the

 The Committee desires the Ministry to review the requirement of funds and based 
on the progress under the ongoing project and newly sanctioned projects, a nd explore the 
possibility of getting budgetary assistance from the Ministry of Finance or Viability Gap 
Funding (VGP).   
     (Para: 57)

 The Committee desires that steps should be taken to reduce the operational cost/ 
overhead expenditure of DCI. The Ministry, in coordination with DCI, should focus on 

 
 
54 
 
reduction in Dry -dock timelines and the expenditure on fuel by adopting remedial 
measures and deploy dredgers along the same coast to reduce the expenditure on voyages 
etc.     
     (Para: 60) 
DREDGING ACTIVITIES 
 The Committee would like the Ministry to identify the reasons for high expenditure 
on capital dredging at Major Ports such as Mumbai  Port Trust, VoCPT, Paradip Port

             (Para: 62) 
 The Committee desires to know whether DCI has entered into joint v entures with

capacity to meet the dredging requirements of the country and if not, what is the share of 
DCI in the total dredging.     
        (Para: 63) 
SETHUSAMUDRAM CORPORATION LIMITED 
 The Committee observes that this project is a vital link to Gulf region which is a 
very productive corridor from India‟s econom ic point of view. The Committee  would, 
therefore, like the Ministry to take all possible steps to expedite adjudication in the matter.  
         (Para: 65) 
SHIP BUILDING INDUSTRY 
 The Committee finds that the shipbuilding industry is facing certain financial and 
infrastructural bottlenecks whi ch tend to push back the progress of Shipping industry. 
India has meager contribution of 1 percent in terms of its share in global shipbuilding 
sector. In a bid to give major push to shipbuilding industry, the Government has unleashed 
a slew of initiatives like formulation of Financial Assistance Policy on shipbuilding in 2015, 
provisions of Government departments including Central Public Sector Undertakings 
giving right of first refusal to Indian shipyards while procuring or repairing vessels for 
Governmental or its own use and grant of infrastructure status to Indian shipbuilding 
industry. Smaller countries like Vietnam and Philippines are ahead of India in terms of 
shipbuilding. The Committee observes that a vibrant shipbuilding industry contributes to 
national GDP by way of employment generation and creation of business opportunities and 
shipbuilding and  therefore, can contribute immensely to the vision of making India a 5 
Trillion Dollar economy. It is , therefore, imperative for the Government to encoura ge the 
indigenous shipbuilding ecosystem. The Committee is also of the opinion that shipbuilding 
is a capital in tensive infrastructure industry  and therefore, PPP is the way forward. The 
Committee also recommends that the Ministry must revisit its strategi es to enhance the 

 
 
55 
 
country‟s global competitiveness in manufacturing of warships and also to build ship 
equipments for Merchant Shipping.          
(Para: 70) 
SHIP BUILDING FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE POLICY FOR INDIAN SHIPYARDS 
 The Committee is deeply concerned that some of the Indian ships which had been 
provided with shipbuilding subsidy/ financial assistance under the Financial Assistance 
Policy have become NPAs and are undergoing insolvency proceedings in the National 
Company Law Tribunal. The Committee would like the Ministry to take effective steps to 
clear pendency of cases in the NCLT and dispose them in a specified time frame by 
rigorously pursuing the cases with NCLT so that the interest of the Government could be 
safeguarded.   
                                 (Para: 73) 
 The Committee also expects the Ministry to expedite the formulation of guidelines 
for the disbursal of subsidy to shipyards. The Committee desires that the Ministry should 
look into the reasons as to wh y sufficient proposals were not received and take remedial 
steps. The Committee desires to be kept apprised in this regard.  
      (Para: 74)

 The Committee applauds the efforts of Directorate General of Shipping and would 
expect the DGS to formulate policies and activities aiming to harness the potential of 
Shipping sector in coordination with the Ministry. The Committee desires that with the 
advancement of the information technology, it is imperative for the Directorate Gen eral of 
Shipping to move towards paperless regime so as to reduce the cost and increase 
transparency. Welcoming the initiative of DGS in digitalizing its 99 odd functions, there is 
still scope of dedicated measures for effective implementation of a definit e IT plan in a 
given time-frame. The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the progress made in this 
regard. The Committee also observes that many of the existing operations and maintenance 
procedures have their origin in decades past and therefore, need to be revised and updated. 
The Committee expects the Ministry to spell out its policy stance in this regard.    
      (Para: 80)

 The Committee underlines the role of lighthouses and lightships in terms of 
indication of dangerous shoals, sandbanks, rocks etc. to obtain a Line of Position and to 
indicate Landfalls, Headlands, entrance to estuaries/ Ports etc. The Committee notes from 
the information made available to it that the funding pattern of the Directorate General of 
Lighthouses and Lightships is based on cost recovery system and that the Directorate does 
not burden the taxpayers as all expenditure on management and development is met out of 
the revenue collected by levy of light dues. The Committee desires to be apprised of the

Ministry.                  (Para: 82) 

 
 
56 
 
 The Committee notes that a tota l of 23 projects have been undertaken during 2020 -
21. The Committee recommends the Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships to 
chalk out an action plan for implementation of these projects in a time bound manner.            
     (Para: 83)

 The Committee notes that SCI has reported a net loss of Rs. 122.00 crores in the FY

liabilities and whether its cash flow is adequate to meet the company‟s debt liabilities. The

offload its holdings in SCI.  
           (Para: 87) 
INLAND WATERWAYS AUTHORITY OF INDIA 
 The Committee observes that Port traffic in the country is largely carried by 
railways and road transport with pipelines carrying some crude oil and petroleum 
products. IWT which is widely recognized as a fuel efficient, environment friendly and cost 
effective mode, especially for bulk goods , has largely  remained underdeveloped. Since  
Indian Ports are facing problem of connectivity through rail and road, it is imperative that 
IWT is exploited to the fullest ex tent possible. The Committee is, therefore, pleased to note 
that the Ministry of Shipping is implementing the JMVP for capacity augmentation of 
navigation on NW -1 at an estimated cost of Rs. 5369.18 crores in March 2023. The 
Committee recommends that a dedicated monitoring mechanism be put in place to ensure 
that the targeted outcomes are achieved within the prescribed timeline.  
                (Para: 91) 
 The Committee would like the Ministry to share with it the details of the projects 
those have become fully operational and the targeted date of completion of the remaining 
projects.

 The Committee desires to know whether the above projects have witn essed any cost 
escalation and the details of funding pattern of these projects.    
            (Para: 96) 
INDIAN MARITIME UNIVERSITY 
 The Committee desires an explanation from Indian Maritime University (IMU) for 
an unutilized fund of Rs. 336.16 crores found to be parked in various banks of   Indian 
Maritime University by the special Audit conducted by the Pr. CCA.    
                  (Para: 100) 
 The Committee observes that the Indian Port sector has undergone substantial 
technological developments duri ng the last 10 years to match with world class standards. 
With the changes in the Port scenario and introduction of high capacity Port equipment, 
there is a need to redefine job description for each level as the strength of manpower has

with an International Institute to carry out a training need analysis for such segment of

 The Committee appreciates the efforts of the Ministry in carrying out skill

recommend that the Ministry should conduct studies to work out annual manpower

augment the supply of required manpower to cater to India‟s needs , being the 16 th largest

high quality training imparted to maritime person nel in India, which has facilitated India

 The Committee would like to know the efficacy of measures taken in promoting

 The Committee observes that cruise tourism in India is a niche product to attract

in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism, should expedite appropriate policy measures 
and joint action plan for developing India‟s largely untapped and hitherto small cruise

 The Committee welcomes the construction of the New Dry Dock within the premises

ship repair at the Cochin Shipyard may be granted deemed export status.    
             (Para: 112) 
 The Committee desires to be kept updated on the progress made towards 
implementation of this program.

KOLKATA PORT TRUST 
 The Committee notes that due to extensive use of Ganga water and bank and bed 
erosion in the upstream states, the Hooghly estuary underwent substantial changes and the 

 
 
58 
 
silt that used to be flushed out into the Bay of Bengal through this river channel started to

NEED FOR COORDINATION BETWEEN MINISTRIES 
  
The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministries of Civil Aviation, Shipping, 
Road Transport &  Highways, Culture, Tourism and  Railways  are not only inter -related 
and interconnected, but also share a common objective to improve connectivity and better 
amenities for the benefit of tourists, travellers and faster movement of freight within the 
country. The Committee, therefore, fe els that there is a pressing need for having an 
effective co -ordination mechanism among these Ministries so that the policies and 
guidelines being formulated by them are executed seamlessly and can supplement each 
other in achieving these objectives. This will not only increase effectiveness and efficiency, 
but will also help in utilization of funds and skilled manpower to the maximum possible 
extent. Therefore, the Committee recommends that an easy -to-use interface should be 
made available which allows has sle-free communication and co -ordination amongst them. 
A hotline number which is common to all these Ministries, may be established so that 
whenever emergency arises, there can be effective and prompt coordination among these 
Ministries and issues in hand can be resolved at the earliest. The above said Ministries 
should work together in this regard and the Ministry of Tourism may be made the nodal 
Ministry for this purpose.   
            (Para: 119) 
CORE GROUP ON SAFETY AND SECURITY 
 
The Committee emphasizes the need for a combined robust security framework to 
ensure safety and security in sectors of Civil Aviation, Road Transport & Highways, 
Shipping, Tourism and Railways. The Committee desires that in order to facilitate effective 
and periodic coordination among the concerned Ministries and agencies, a core group 
comprising officers at the level of Joint Secretary of the Ministries of Civil Aviation, Road 
Transport & Highways, Shipping, Tourism, Railways, Commissioner of Railway Safet y 
and Petroleum may be set up to meet on monthly basis to chalk out ways and means for 
addressing safety and security concerns in these sectors and ensure that international best 
practices are followed. This core group should be headed by Secretary, Minist ry of Civil 
Aviation. In order to upgrade to international standards, the services of consultants (both 
domestic and international) who are experts in the respective fields and have domain 
knowledge, may be engaged for preparing Reports so that they can be  implemented. This 
core group may serve as a think -tank and formulate guidelines and directions to improve 
safety and security standards in these sectors. The Committee would like the Ministry to 

 
 
59 
 
furnish the monthly Reports and status of implementation of its decisions, to the 
Committee.

MISCELLANEOUS 
 The Committee takes note of the fact that the East Coast Canal in the Balasore 
district of Odisha has been declared as the NW -5 and the vast agricultural land on both 
sides of the canal dep ends on the drainage of water during heavy rain in the rainy season. 
During summer season , rabi crops used to be irrigated from this canal. Further, it notes 
that due to negligence of authorities, growth of wild shrubs and grass makes the little water 
available, poisonous and it dysfunctions the lift irrigation pumps during summers. They 
also act as a blockade for drainage of water during rainy season, making the area marshy, 
waterlogged and breeding ground for snakes. Therefore, the Committee desires t hat the 
Ministry should clean the canal from wild shrubs and let the water flow to and fro so that 
sufficient water is available for irrigation during the summer season. The Committee 
further recommends that water gates at Bhograi lock should be maintained  and regular 
dredging of the canal should be undertaken by constructing proper embankments to 
maintain fertility and safety in the East Coast Canal.

9. The Committee reassembled at 2:00 P.M. after lunch.  
10. The Chairman welcomed the Secretary, Ministry of Shipping and other senior 
officials from the Ministry to the meeting. Highlighting the vital role of Shipping industry in 
strengthening country‟s export and import trade, he sought to know the future action plans of 
the Ministry on shipbuilding, containerization and marine safety. The Chairman then 
requested the Secretary to make a presentation on the Demands for Grants (2020 -21) of the 
Ministry. 
11. In his presentation, the Secretary apprised the Committee a bout the budgetary 
allocations and expenditure in the last 3 years, alongwith an overview of the Gross and Extra 
budgetary details for 2020 -21. He elaborated upon the capacity and traffic handled at major 
Indian Ports during the last five years. He further  shared the key achievements of Ports in 
2019-20 such as improvement in efficiency parameters, one time settlement scheme and 
upgraded Port Community System. He also apprised the Committee about the current status 
and achievements of ship-building and ship recycling industry. The Secretary also briefed the 
Committee about the expenditure figures for 2018 -19 and 2019-20, alongwith the reasons for 
increased spending in 2019 -20. He submitted that all Ports are now financially sustainable 
and can take care of t heir expenses and developmental needs. He mentioned a scheme for 
shipbuilding through shipyards where the private shipyards are also eligible to build ships. He 
informed that new legislations on the Inland Vessels Act, the Merchant Shipping Act and the 
Indian Ports Act will be introduced as old legislations have become outdated. 
12. He then furnished the details of projects under Sagarmala Scheme alongwith their 
implementation cost and funds utilized till date. He mentioned about the training and skill 
development programs held in Centre of Excellence in Maritime and Shipbuilding and Multi 
Skill Development Centres in JNPT and Chennai Port Trust. He also informed the Committee 
about the projects relating to Inland Waterway Transport such as Jal Marg Vikas Pr oject and 
development of National Waterways. He concluded by mentioning the details of the 
upcoming projects at Major Ports in the year 2020-21 and under Sagarmala Programme.  
13. Members of the Committee raised various queries some of which were replied t o by 
the Secretary. The Chairman then directed that written replies to the queries which remained 
unanswered may be sent to the Secretariat within a week.

been categorized as follows:-
