2 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
MINISTRY 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
1. The Committee recommends that the State Government, Ministry of Tourism and the 
various other stakeholders must endeavor to remove the negative publicity in the press by finding 
innovative means to engage with the world at large via the social media. In this age of You Tube 
and social platforms  like Instagram and Snapchat, social media influencers may be engaged 
to promote a more positive image of the State. Furthermore, the Committee recommends that the 
State Government must engage with ASSOCHAM, CII and FICCI to invite and encourage 
companies to host meetings and visits in the region. The Committee fe els that websites of the 
Ministry of Tourism and its various arms should be made interactive and user -friendly. Mobile 
applications and social networking sites like Facebook, Twitter, Snapchat, Instagram, etc. should 
be harnessed as a quick and cost effective medium for tourism marketing. 
(Para 36) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1.  The Ministry of Tourism launched the new Incredible India website on 14 th June 
2018.  The website showcases India as a holistic destination, revolving around major 
experiences, such as, spirituality, heritage, adventure, culture, yoga, wellness and more. The 
website follows the trends and technologies of international standards  with an aim to project 
India as a “must-visit” destination, among its overseas travelers. 
 
1.2. The Ministry of Tourism proactively leverages the potential of Social Media in marketing 
and promotion of India, both in the domestic as well as in the oversea s markets.  The Ministry, 
currently maintains accounts in leading social media platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, 
Instagram, LinkenIn, YouTube, Vimeo and Periscope.  Since, May 2016, a professional social 
media agency has been appointed to manage the soc ial media activities on Ministry’s social 
media handles.  A large number of posts/tweets/messages are regularly posted/tweeted on 
various facets of India including Jammu & Kashmir with a view to provide wide publicity about 
various destinations in India.   
 
1.3. The Ministry of Tourism has  guidelines for extending Financial Support to Commerce, 
Trade and Industry Organizations for organizing Tourism and Tourism Related Events.   
These organizations include ASSOCHAM, CII, FICCI, etc. The Tourism related events include 
Seminars, Symposia, Conferences, Conventions, Lectures, Competitions focusing on Tourism or 
Tourism related subjects and any other event which has the potential of promoting tourism 
within the country. 
1.4. The Ministry of Tourism, through i ts Hospitality Scheme invites Key Influencers 
including leading international Bloggers/ Instagrammers to visit India to promote India including 
Jammu & Kashmir among their followers.  The Ministry also undertakes campaigns on social 
media channels to furth er enhance visibility of tourist destinations and products in India, 
including J&K in the overseas markets. 
 

3 
 
SAFETY OF TOURISTS 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. Safe and secure travel is always the top priority for travelers. The Committee feels 
that security of tourists must be given top priority. The Committee was informed by the Tour and 
travel operators and Hoteliers that the travel bans imposed by various Governments, both 
international and domestic , on travel to the State create an air of negativ ity in the region. The 
Committee, during its visit to Srinagar, observed that the situation was more peaceful than  what 
was reported in the news and media. The Committee feels that this is a matter which must be 
broached with caution as it involves issues of national security.                    (Para 42) 
 
3. The popularity of the region as a 'dham' pilgrimage site is offset by large crowds 
travelling on foot. Often, the elderly, women and children have to be carried on indigenous 
palanquins which are neith er sturdy nor reliable. The result is a chaotic situation of unregulated 
crowds which cause regular stampedes which leave many injured and prove fatal for  others.                                             
(Para 43) 
 
4. The Committee, in this regard, recommends that the State Government must work on 
crowd management in coordination with the concerned temple authorities, to formulate a plan to 
regulate the crowds in the area. Furthermore, the State Government of J&K must work to ensure 
the provision of regulated assistance, in order to prevent overcrowding by vendors.                             
(Para 44) 
 
5. The Committee recommends that the State Government must endeavour to establish 
an evacuation plan and procedure, with signage and instructions at re gular intervals, to help and 
evacuate the tourists in the event of a stampede or a natural  calamity.                                                                                            
(Para 45) 
Reply of the Ministry  
5.1.  Various measures have been taken to ensure safety and security of tourists in the 
country including the State of J&K.  MoT takes up the issue of Safety & Security time to time 
with the concerned authorities to minimize the air of negativity created by vari ous media reports 
and news.  
  
5.2. MoT has taken up the issue with the State Govt of J&K in order to formulate a plan 
to regulate the crowd in the area and to ensure the provision of regulated assistance in order to 
prevent overcrowding by vendors. 
 
 
ECOLOGICAL SUSTAINABILITY 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
6.  The Committee was informed by the stakeholders that J&K has been declared a 
fragile Eco Zone. The Committee notes that pollution and waste management are problems being 
faced by the J & K Government.                    (Para 49) 
 
7. The Committee recommends that the State Government of Jammu & Kashmir must 

4 
 
envisage a Solid Waste treatment plant in Srinagar and other prominent tourist destinations. The 
State must work to clean up the Dal Lake, Nigeen Lake and develop the Wular Lake.  Solar 
Energy must be encouraged in the region and green initiatives must be undertaken. The 
Committee recommends that the State should draw up an action plan on how to maintain 
cleanliness and develop and maintain an ecolo gically–friendly and ecologically –viable form of 
tourism in the region.                                                                                      (Para 50) 
 
 
Reply by the Ministry 
7.1.  As per input received from the Govt. of J&K Solid Waste Man agement Plants have 
been/are being installed at various tourist destinations in the region to overcome the problem of 
Solid Waste Management created due to influx of tourists.  For the purpose of implementation of 
Pollution Control Board norms have been ma de mandatory for Hoteliers/Guest House 
Owners/Houseboats Owners for establishment of Sewerage Treatment Plant (STP) with capacity 
of 19 rooms and above.  Bio -digesters are being installed on each House Boat through Housing 
& Urban Development Departments  as per the recommendations of Committee of Experts 
(CoE) constituted by the Hon’ble High Court, J&K in the PIL 159/2002.  Besides, 
Polythene/plastic items have been banned in the region.  Furthermore, the tourist destinations 
have been pedestrized to promote Eco-Tourism in the region. 
 
    7.2.  In order to regulate the construction of Hotels/Guest Houses all the construction 
have been brought under the mandate/rules/regulations of BOCA (Building Operation 
Construction Authority). A Government Order No. 193-TSM of 2018 dated 19-06-2018 has been 
issued in respect of Ladakh region to ensure that no haphazard construction takes place. 
 
7.3.  Furthermore, the Department of Tourism does not create any such infrastructure 
which creates environmental problem at tourist destination in Tourism sector and due care is 
being taken to provide Eco -friendly infrastructure at various Tourist Resorts in private sector as 
well. 
 
 7.4. The measures taken by the Directorate of Tourism, Kashmir are: 
 
1.   Bio-digester toilets have been installed at Charchinari Dal Lake. 
2.  Battery Operated Vehicles (BOV) have been/are being procured for operation at 
Tourist Resorts for facilitation of tourists. 
3.  Tourism Department registers and renews the licenses of Hotels/Guest Houses, 
subject to NOC from the Pollution Control Board.  The pollution control board is 
mandated with taking punitive action against the delinquents and periodical 
instructions are being conducted to Hotels by the prescribed authority to check the 
violation of garbage dumping (if any) and in case any stake holder is found guilty, 
the matter is brought to the notice of concerned Departme nt besides, withholding 
of renewal of Registration certificate of the unit. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
8. The Committee feels that special efforts should be taken to highlight famous lakes of 
the State in order to promote them as important tourist destinations as a part of eco-tourism in the 

5 
 
State. Steps should be taken to preserve and enhance their beauty by undertaking development in 
an integrated manner. Moreover, Lakes and Waterways Development Authority (LWDA) must 
ensure that wastes generated by houseboats are not dumped into the lakes. Furthermore, 
emphasis should be placed on the introduction of an effe ctive Waste Management Treatment 
System.                                                                                                             (Para 52) 
 
Reply by the Ministry 
8.1.  The Govt. of J&K  has informed that t he water bodies especially Dal  Lake/Nigeen 
Lake are being taken care of/ maintained by the separate Department i.e. lakes and Waterways 
Development authority (LAWDA).  As per the directions  of Hon’ble High Court J&K, the 
Tourism Department is also undertaking various measures for cons ervation of famous Dal 
Lake/Nigeen lake. Besides, the Government has created a separate development authority viz. 
Wullar Manasbal Development Authority (WMDA) to protect and conserve the ecology of these 
lakes and its surroundings. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  

6 
 
CHAPTER-II 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT 
DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY 
 
DISTRIBUTION OF FUNDS 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee was informed by the Ministry of Tourism about the various policies 
which have been introduced to provide funding towards the development of Swadesh Darshan 
for integrated development of tourism based theme circuits and PRASHAD in Jammu & 
Kashmir. It was stated that there have been limited allocation of funds under the Swadesh 
Darshan Scheme. However, given its status, the State has been allocated special funds under 
Prime Minister Development Plan (2016). 
(Para 10) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1.  There is no separate allocation of funds under the Prime Minister Development Plan 
2015.  The Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure at the time of announcement of 
package, vide letter dated 11.7.2016 had conveyed that different components of Recon struction 
Plan are allocated to respective line Ministries and are to be implemented by them out of their 
own Budget. The component of Reconstruction Plan of Ministry of Tourism (MOT) may be 
implemented through MoT’s Budget. If necessary, MoT may seek suit able augmentation of 
Budget at supplementary stage. Accordingly, the projects under PMDP are taken up for 
implementation under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme. In 2016 -17, the MoF at RE stage made 
provision of additional Rs. 200 Crores under SD scheme to meet the requirements for PMDP and 
PMs Bihar package. After that no additional funds were allocated by the MoF for the PMDP to 
the Ministry of Tourism. The Ministry has taken up the matter of additional funds with the MoF.  
 
SEASONALITY 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee understands that the seasonality of the region along with the other 
variables may contribute to delay in completion of Project in the region.  The Committee is of 
the view that the time table followed by the Ministry of Finance towards funding various 
activities in the region may not be conductive to peculiarities of the region.  The Committee 
therefore recommended that the Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
and other stakeholders may impress upon the Ministry o f Finance to chalk out a plan to ensure a 
more sustainable and efficient way of releasing funds to J&K and other similar affected States. 
(Para 16) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1. Release of funds for projects approved under the Schemes of Ministry of Tourism is 
as per the provisions of the respective Scheme Guidelines.  The Scheme Guidelines have 
adequate provisions for timely release of funds for smooth implementation of the proje cts for 
Scheme undertaken by the Ministry of Tourism and there is hardly any occasion when projects 
are held up due to the pattern of release of funds.  
 

7 
 
CONNECTIVITY 
(i) Air  
3. The Committee is pleased to note that the airports at Leh  and Srinagar have been 
upgraded and made functional. The Association of Tour, Travel and Hotel operators of the State 
informed the Committee that the exorbitant price of air tickets is a major dampener. Escalating 
airfares of ‘low cost’ carriers during th e peak season are a major deterrent to increasing footfall 
in the region. The airfares are equivalent to that of the nearby foreign destinations and given the 
sensitivity of the region, tourists would prefer to visit nearby foreign destinations at the same  
airfare rather than visit J&K. 
(Para 17) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
3.1.  Ministry of Tourism has taken up the matter with Ministry of Civil Aviation 
(MoCA) on the said observation earlier and M/o Civil Aviation had informed that, at present, 
airfares are not controlled by the Government. Airlines offer fares on various levels which are 
driven by demand and market forces and as the demand goes up the seats on lower fare levels get 
filled. This is a global practice in the aviation industry. Pricing forms the strategic framework, 
day-to-day tactical changes  in pricing  respond to demand/supply and market dynamics  works 
through the Inventory Management process.   
 
3.2.  Airlines are free to fix the reasonable tariff under the provision under the provision 
of Aircraft rules 1937 having regard to all relevant factors, and the generally prevailing tariff. Air 
fares are not fixed by the Government as they are determined by th e interplay of market forces. 
Airlines remain compliant to the regulatory provisions of Sub -Rule 2 of rule 135 as long as the 
fare charged by them does exceed the fare established and displayed on their website.  
 
3.3.  The domestic airline pricing runs in multiple levels (bucket or RBD) which is in line 
with the practice followed globally. The lower fare in the fare bucket is available for advance 
booking much earlier. As time lapses and date of journey approaches closer, the fare in higher 
side of fare bu cket is made available as per the respective airline policy. In order to identify the 
fare and conditions of travel on passenger tickets, airlines world over follow IATA Resolution 
728  which contains information on various booking classes referred to as R eservation Booking 
Designator(RBD). The RBD is the code used in reservation transactions to identify the booking 
class.  
 
    SAFETY OF TOURISTS 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
4. The Committee is pleased to note that the State Government has implemented 
Tourism Police in the State. The Committee recommends that the Tourism Police must be 
trained regularly and must undergo sensitization training to deal with the large number of tourists 
arriving from different countries, cultures and languages. The Committ ee desires that the Tourist 
Police may also be encouraged to learn foreign languages in order to better serve foreign tourists 
in the region. 
(Para 46) 

8 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
4.1. It is to be mentioned that Ministry of Home Affairs had forwarded a concept paper 
on Tourist Police as discussed during the DsGP and IsGP Conference held in 2015. Further, as 
desired by Ministry of Home Affairs,  a list of 25 tourist sites which may be taken as pilot project 
for formation of a separate police unit in the States/UTs and training module, as given by IITTM 
for imparting training vide OM TT/84/2018 dated 12.12.2018, has been forwarded to them. Now, 
Ministry of Home Affairs has circulated a lett er to all the Chief Secretaries of all state 
Governments/UT Administrations asking for the training to be imparted. It may now be seen that 
necessary action with respect to formation of Tourist Police and imparting training to them has 
already been taken u p by Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Tourism. The follow up 
action is to be taken by the State Governments. 
 
 
NEED FOR GREATER CENTRE- STATE COORDINATION 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
5.  The development of J&K has been integral to the overall devel opment policy for the 
nation. In this regard, the Committee was informed that the Prime Minister’s Reconstruction 
Package (PMRP) was instituted as early as 2004 and a great deal of money was sanctioned under 
different kind of projects which included a proj ect for rural tourism, tourism authorities and one 
for the Circuits amongst others. The Committee was further informed that the package also 
included compensation for businesses destroyed/damaged by the floods in 2014. 
 
(Para 56) 
6. The Committee was also informed that under the Product/Infrastructure 
Development of Destinations and Circuits, the Ministry of Tourism extended Central Financial 
Assistance to the State Governments/Union Territory administrations for tourism projects 
identified in consultation with them for the improvement of existing tourism products and also 
for developing new ones. Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Product/Infrastructure 
Development for Destinations and Circuits, 100% Central assistance is given  for development of 
Destinations/Circuits, including mega projects, to world standard and also for Rural Tourism 
infrastructure development. The Ministry of Tourism provides financial assistance up to Rs. 5.00 
crore for the development of destinations and R s.8.00 crore for circuits. The upper limit of 
financial assistance has been increased to Rs.25 crore and Rs.50 crore for development of 
identified mega destinations and circuits respectively, under the schemes to promote rural 
tourism in the country. The t hrust is for development of tourism infrastructure at the identified 
rural tourism sites so that socio -economic benefits percolate down to the rural community. A 
maximum of Rs.50.00 lakhs is sanctioned for each project under this scheme for development of  
tourism related infrastructure. The Committee was informed that the scheme had been 
restructured under the PRASHAD and Swadesh Darshan.  
(Para 57)

27. The Committee observed during its visit to Jammu and Kashmir that the State 
requires further input in terms of improving upon tourist facilities in the region. The tourist 
destinations must be equipped with safe drinking water stations, clean and hygieni c washrooms, 
rest stop, car stops etc. The Committee recommends that tourist facilities proposed under the 
Swadesh Darshan scheme must be completed at the earliest. Furthermore, the Committee 
recommends that the State Government must put in place a system to ensure that these tourist 
amenities, once operational, are well maintained and at par with global standards. The creation of 
adequate and suitable infrastructure in terms of accommodation, transport, communication links 
etc. and other essential amenities are the foundation for the success of tourism in the State. 
(Para 39) 
 
28.  The Committee recommends that in order to improve the maintenance of existing 
tourist destinations, adoption/management/sponsorship programs should be promoted so as to 
create a sense of ownership in the minds of locals and corporate alike, for monuments, religious 
sites and tourist destinations. 
(Para 40) 
Reply of the Ministry 
28.1. The Ministry lays special emphasis on timely execution/completion of work and 
simultaneous establishment of O&M (Operation & Maintenance) mechanism for the projects 
sanctioned under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme. The Ministry regularly holds review meeting 
with the State Government to monitor the timely implementation of projects sanctioned in the 

22 
 
State. The State in the meeting held on 25 th February 2019 had assured to bring the projects to 
timely completion and to plan for O & M of assets created.  
 
28.2. For proper O&M of the assets created under the scheme the Ministry has revised the 
guidelines of the Swadesh Darshan Scheme and now 5% of the project cost will be paid to the 
implementing agency after successful O&M of Toilet, TFC, Cafeteria facilities for  one year as 
certified by an independent agency. 
Further Recommendation 
28.3. The Committee suggests that in addition to provision of  Toilets, TFCs, 
Cafeteria, etc., under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme, the Ministry should ensure sufficient 
number of drinking water stations, rest stops, car stops, refreshment centres in the tourist 
destinations of the State in tandem with tourist footfall in the State. The Committee also 
suggests that in order to provide such facilities at faster pace, the works may be outsourced 
on need basis for adoption/sponsorship  of the tourist sites  by agencies for better  
maintenance. 
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
29. During the visit of the Committee to Srinagar, it was informed that there was an 
urgent need to introduce a Laser Show on the Dal Lake and restart the Sound and Light Show at 
Shalimar Gardens. The Committee may be apprised of the status of implementation o f the Sound 
and Light Show at Dal Lake. The Committee feels that these facilities may definitely attract 
more tourists while serving to narrate the story of Kashmir. The Committee recommends that the 
Ministry of Tourism should extend financial support to t he Government of J & K to restart the 
above mentioned projects. 
(Para 41) 
 
Reply of the Ministry 
29.1. The Ministry under the project Integrated Development of Tourism Infrastructure 
projects in the State of Jammu & Kashmir under Himalayan Circuit of Swadesh Darshan Scheme 
sanctioned in June 2016 has developed Sound and Light Show with water fountains at Sher-i-
Kashmir International Conference Centre (SKICC) Ghats. Work on this component is complete. 
Further Recommendation 
29.2. The reply of the Ministry does not address the recommendation.  The 
Committee seeks a categorical reply on introduction of a Laser Show on Dal Lake and 
resumption of Sound and Light Show in Shalimar Gardens in the State. 
 
SAFETY ALERTS 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
30.  The Committee notes that the region is prone to natural calamities and feels that the 
State must be better equipped to handle situations in the event of calamities, both natural and 
man–made. 
(Para 47) 
31. In this regard, the Committee strongly feels that the State Government must work 

23 
 
towards ensuring the safety of tourists in the region. The Committee recommends that the State 
Government must work to ensure that its volunteers, Tourist Police and State Police are regularly 
trained by the National Disaster Relief Force (NDRF) in the evacuation and rescue of civilians. 
The Committee further recommends that the State Government must work to coordinate regular 
joint exercises with the volunteers, Army and the NDRF in preparation for any eventualities. 
(Para 48) 
Reply by the Ministry 
31.1. The matter has been taken up with the State Government of Jammu and Kashmir in 
order to ensure that its volunteers, Tourist Police and State Police are regularly trained by the  
National Disaster Relief Force (NDRF) in the evacuation and rescue of civilians.  
Further Recommendation 
31.2.  The Committee recommends that units of disaster management teams should 
be deployed at appropriate places in order to safeguard the to urists from natural 
calamities. 
 
ECOLOGICAL SUSTAINABILITY 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
32.  The Committee feels that the State Government needs to regulate the houseboat 
operations on the Dal Lake keeping in mind its carrying capacity and introduce special incentives 
to start houseboat operations in areas other than Dal and Nageen Lakes. 
(Para 51) 
Reply by the Ministry 
32.1. The Govt. of J&K has informed that they have constituted a Committee of Experts 
(CoE) to monitor and recommend various measures of conservation of Dal Lake.  The 
Committee of Experts has recommended that the Department of Tourism shall find out the 
optimum carrying capacity of Lake in terms of House Boats and till such time  the 
issuance/renewal of licenses in favour of House Boat owners be put on hold.  The Department 
has accordingly requested Kashmir University for report in the matter.  Preliminary concept note 
has been received from Director, Centre of Research & Developm ent (CoRD), Kashmir 
University and the research work has been initiated. 
 
32.2. The State Government is of the view that in case the incentive scheme is revalidated 
and subsequently extended to the areas other than Dal & Nigeen Lake, it will definitely boost the 
Tourism Sector. 
Further Recommendation 
32.3.   The Committee desires to be apprised of the findings of Kashmir University on 
the optimum carrying capacity of Dal Lake in terms of House Boats  and the action taken 
thereon.  The Committee also reiterates that an early action on regulation of house boats in 
the Dal Lake and introduction of house boats in areas other than Dal and Nageen Lakes 
may be taken on a priority basis. 
 
GOODS AND SERVICES TAX 
 
Recommendation/Observation 

24 
 
33. The sensitive nature of Jammu & Kashmir must be taken into consideration during 
the development of tourism in the region. The implementation of GST on tourism in the region 
would have manifold effects, mostly negative on the economy of the region. The Comm ittee was 
informed by the stakeholders that sourcing of products and materials is an issue. Unlike other 
States, the residents of Jammu & Kashmir and its business owners spend huge amounts of money 
on procuring essentials, most of which have to be flown in , which increases their capital 
expenditure. Most wholesale traders insist on payment in cash which is a major issue, as the 
support from the Government must be processed via the Public Financial Management System 
(PFMS) payment system which insists on digital transactions. 
(Para 53) 
34. Furthermore, the Committee was informed that small business owners for small scale 
hotels, bed and breakfasts and home stays cannot list their properties on various travel 
intermediary websites as there is a levy of an 18 percent of GST, which cuts across the little 
profit that they might make, making their venture unsustainable. 
(Para 54) 
 
35. In this regard, the Committee recommends that the implementation of GST on 
tourism related activities in the State must be reconsid ered. It must be done in a cautious and 
phased manner in order to ensure that the delicate state of tourism in the region is not adversely 
affected. Furthermore, the Committee suggests that the Ministry of Tourism must initiate 
dialogues with the Ministry of Finance in order to formulate a policy  wherein tourism in the 
region can be supported and developed over a period by giving tax sops for a given time period 
and to be leaned off slowly, in order to ensure the sustained development of the region. 
(Para 55) 
Reply of the Ministry 
35.1. This issue has been taken up with Ministry of Finance for further taking up with GST 
Council (Annexure -C). 
Further Recommendation 
35.2. The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Ministry would continue to 
follow up the matter with the Ministry of Finance.

REPORT 
The Report of the Department -Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, 
Tourism and Culture deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on the 
observations/ recommendations as contained in its Two Hundred and Seventy Sixth Report on 
Demands for Grants (2020 -21) of Ministry of Civil Aviation pres ented to both the Houses of 
Parliament on 12th March, 2020. 
2. The Action Taken Replies were received from the Ministry on 10th June, 2020, in respect 
of all the observations/recommendations contained in the 276 th Report. The replies have been 
categorized as follows:-

Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) 
Recommendation/ Observation 
1. The Committee notes that RCS has given the Indian aviation industry a huge fillip. This 
Scheme has made air travel more affordable and also the connectivity to remote and hilly 
regions of the country has improved. The Comm ittee notes that availability of funds and high 
cost of operations are the major constraints under the Scheme. The Committee finds that out of 
688 valid routes awarded, only 256 routes have commenced operations, which constitute only 
37% of the awarded rou tes. Despite the fact that the Ministry frequently conducts bidding for 
RCS routes and awards routes, desired progress has not taken place. Given the tremendous 
enthusiastic response from the stakeholders including the passengers and significant change 
noticed in the economic activity of the connected routes with current level of 37% routes, there  
is a huge potential in terms of connectivity and the resultant economic prosperity under the 
Scheme. The Committee, therefore , desires that concerted efforts sho uld be made to 
operationalize all the awarded routes at the earliest. The Committee also desires that periodic 
evaluation of the Scheme be conducted to address the constraints of the issues in 
implementation. 
 
Reply of the Government 
(Recommendation at Para 16.5 of 276th Report) 
1.1. Out of the 688 valid routes awarded, 268 RCS routes have been commenced so far. The 
Selected Airline Operators (SAOs) are obligated to commence RCS flight operations on a RCS - 
route, as part of individual route -proposal or a network proposal within a period of six months 
from the issuance of Letter of Award or within two months from the readiness of airport, 
whichever is later, unless any extension is granted by the Implementing Agency. 
1.2. There is also a mechanism to revi ew the performance of Selected A irline Operators 
(SAO) for RCS routes. RCS -UDAN is regularly monitored for successful implementation. In 
case of wilful default by a Selected Airline Operator (SAO), cancellatio n of routes are done by 
forfeiting the Performance Guarantee/Proposal Security and the routes are offered for rebidding 
in subsequent rounds of bidding. 
1.3. MoCA has therefore been making all possible efforts to operationalize awarded routes 
at the earliest.

Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) facilities in India 
 
Recommendation/ Observation 
11. The Committee is aware of the huge potential that India has, in offering MRO facilities 
in its soil. It is a sad fact that India could not fully exploit the opportunities available in this 
sector. MRO, being a sunrise industry, and with our huge technical  and skill base, by creating a 
congenial environment, India can easily meet the requirements of the sector. By giving boost to 
this sector, new employment opportunities can be created for our fresh engineering students.  
The Committee, therefore, strongly feels that the Ministry should give adequate and immediate 
focus on the issues faced in the MRO sector and chalk out strategic measures to make positive 
interventions in order to ensure that India becomes a key player in offering MRO facilities. This 
will also help in achieving the Prime Minister’s vision of attaining 5 trillion dollar economy. 
(Para 30.1) 
Reply of the Government 

8  
11.1. The Government has taken up further improvements in policy, taxation and regulatory 
regime. The roadmap h as been developed in consultation with MRO industry for realizing self -
sufficiency in this vital and strategic aviation segment, which includes upgrading the 
demonstrated airframe capacity and setting up component and engine MROs in India. Reciprocal 
acceptance of air safety certificates between Indian and overseas regulators has also been taken 
up. Convergence between Defence sector and the civil MROs would be established to create 
economies of scale and maintenance costs for airlines would be brought down  including through 
rationalisation of royalty charged for MROs at airports. 
11.2. The implementation of the roadmap would act as a catalyst for future growth towards a 
well-developed Indian MRO ecosystem which will help in leveraging India‗s engineering 
advantage, a step towards achieving higher self -reliance in airline operations and Make-in- India. 
It will also help nurture R&D besides creating MRO training infrastructure, skills development, 
and churning out more jobs for the youth of India.  Commensurate with the airlines‘  fleet growth 
over time, the size of India aviation MRO is estimated by industry to grow annually from an 
estimated Rs. 13,500 crore in 2019 -20 to Rs. 21,600 crore in the  next five years, with domestic 
MRO contributing a higher proportion of about Rs. 5,000 crore. 
11.3. In pursuance of the roadmap, the tax regime for MROs has been substantially 
rationalized as below: 
(a) Import Duty has been exempted on Special Tools and Equipment for MRO. 
(b) Customs duty waived that applied to spares only for Airlines extended to MRO. 
(c) Aircraft brought into country for MRO allowed to stay from 1 month to 6 months 
without penalties. 
(d) Spares purchased for MRO can be consumed upto 36 months (up from 12 months) 
from time of landing in India. 
(e) GST on Domestic MRO reduced from 18% to 5% w.e.f. 1st April, 2020. 
(f) Sub-contracted transactions to domestic MRO by foreign MRO now treated  as 
exports with zero-rated GST w.e.f. 1st April, 2020.

12.2. (a) Growth of air cargo is  critical for industries such as e -commerce, pharmaceuticals,

and high -value goods, including gems and jewellery and fashion garments, where

compared to hardly any growth the preceding years. India‗s air cargo growth exceeded 
global growth during this period. During FY 2018-19, total air cargo handled reached to 
3.57 million MT comprising domestic air cargo of 1.36 million and international air 
cargo of 2.20 million MT. Domestic and international cargo grew annually by 12.1% 
and 2.6%, respectively. Indian air express and courier industry is one of the fast est 
growing markets globally. Growth is estimated at 17% CAGR during the last five years. 
Entry of e-commerce giants in air cargo business is expected to give further impetus to 
its growth. 
(c) Government has taken several initiatives to sustain the growth impetus in air cargo by 
way of cost reduction, efficiency improvement and better inter -ministerial coordination, 
and to bring the country‗s logistics on a par with global standards. These include, inter 
alia, the following: 
 
A. Infrastructure Creation/ Upgradation: 
(i) 23 Common User Domestic Cargo Terminals (CUDCTs) and 20 International Cargo 
Terminals (CUTs) made operational by Airport Authority of India (AAI) through its 
wholly-owned subsidiary, the AAI Cargo Logistics and Allied Services Ltd. (AAICLAS). 
Both d omestic and international cargo terminals are also developed and operated at JV 
airports (Bengaluru, Cochin, Delhi, Hyderabad and Mumbai). 
(ii) AAICLAS has taken up a time -bound programme for developing air cargo facilities 
(including X -Ray machines) at unserve d airports and upgrading existing facilities at 
underserved airports as per commercial and other considerations. 
(iii) Cold Storage and perishable cargo handling facilities have been upgraded / developed at 
major airports. The segregated agro and other perishabl es facility, the 'Export Cold Zone', 
launched by MIAL (Mumbai International Airport Ltd.) on 20 February 2020 is world's 
largest airport-based temperature-controlled facility and a global first of its kind. 
(iv) Air Freight Station (off -airport common user faci lity) at Chennai is in operation. Delhi‗s 
first AFS is in readiness to be launched after obtaining security clearance. 
(v) For promoting multimodal synergies between air and road transportation in particular, 
multimodal logistics parks are being encouraged to help decongest airports and reduce 
logistics costs and air cargo processing time. 
B. Implementation of the provisions of the air cargo policy 
(i) Airport, including cargo terminals, and cold chain facilities and warehouses, have been 
included in Harmonised List of Infrastructure. 

10  
(ii) Free period for air cargo clearance has been reduced from 72 hours to within 48 hours 
across all major airports. 
(iii) Service Level Standards have been set for entire air cargo ecosystem. 
(iv) Progressively, air cargo dwell time on imports has been reduced from 72 hours to 52 hours 
by December 2017 and to 39 hours by December 2018 as per data maintained by IATA. 
Dwell time on export cargo was reduced at various major airports by 36 -72%, and

2. Post induction of the aircraft into service, technical issues were experienced on these

failures, which is being addressed by making suitable modifications during shop visits of 
the engines. 
3. As a final mitigation, modified engines with new 3rd stage LPT blades are being installed 
on the aircraft. 
4. DGCA has directed both the airlines to take following proactive measures in the interest

manufacturer have taken steps to expedite replacement of unmodified engines.

European Aviation Safety Agency, who have also committed to the replacement of 
unmodified engines. It involved procurement of about 200 engines. 
(iv) Considering the logistical challenges involved in replacing this unexpected demand of 
large number of engines and after ensuring that at least one modified engine has  been 
placed on all the aircraft, irrespective of the flight hours accumulated, DGCA has 
extended  the t imeline for complete removal of unmodified engine to 31 st May, 2020 
from earlier mandated 31st January, 2020.

Indigo fleet and 22 unmodified engines are installed on aircraft of M/s Go Air fleet.

Reply of the Government 
5.1. An aircraft including aeroplanes and helicopters are manufactured only after its type 
design is approved by the country of design and a type certificate issued. Further, an aircraft for 
commercial/ air transport operations is designed and meets the laid down specific design criteria 
of the St ate of design given for such aircraft before the type certificate is issued. Aircraft

with the age and other relevant mandatory requirements as laid down in the applicable Civil 
Aviation Requirements (CARs ). Further, for the purpose of granting air operator certificate/ 
permit for commercial operations, the operator has to demonstrate airworthiness and operational 
requirements to DGCA.

Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) 
Recommendation/ Observation 
3. The Committee notes that a serious challe nge is awaiting the nation, in the ever 
expanding aviation industry, after 2020 i.e., with regard to buying of carbon credits. As more 
and more areas are connected and expansion takes place, Ministry will have to buy a lot of 
carbon credit, which will invo lve huge financial implications. Under these circumstances, the 
Committee desires the Ministry to have a study of the financial implications involved for future 
expansion of our aviation sector which is presently at a nascent stage, but has a huge potentia l 
for further expansion. The Committee also calls upon the Ministry to take up, this issue 
diplomatically as well as politically, at the highest possible level, to sort it out as early as 
possible so as to secure the future of our civil aviation industry. 
(Para 15.1) 
Reply of the Government 
3.1.   1. It   is   true   that   a   scheme   called   ‗Carbon   Offsetting   and   Reduction   Scheme   
for International Aviation (CORSIA)‘  has been established by the International Civil Aviation 
Organisation (ICAO). The Scheme will commence operation from 2021 in a voluntary form 
which will last till 2026. From 2027 till 2035, it will run in mandatory form for all countries and 
collectively cover around 89% of total international aviation emissions. It will be further 
extended after a review. It provides for a global carbon offsetting mechanism under which the 
international  aeroplane  operators  will  be  required  to  purchase  and  cancel  ‗emissions  units‘ 
(carbon credits) to offset the increase in CO2 emissions covered by the scheme using the average 
annual emissions of 2019 and 2020 as reference. The Scheme lays down a formula for 
calculating the offsetting requirement of individual aeroplane operators. 
2. The Indian carriers will not be required to undertake any offsetting obligations until end of 
2026 since India has chosen not to join the Scheme in the voluntary phase (Pilot Phase 2021 - 
2023 and First Phase 2024 -2026). But from the b eginning of 2027, when the mandatory phase 
begins, India will have to join the Scheme as a member State of ICAO, and its carriers will be 
bound by the offsetting requirements and will have to buy carbon credits from approved sources 
to meet their obligations. 
3. A study has been commissioned by TERI (The Energy and Resources Institute) to assess the 
challenges posed by CORSIA for the air transport sector of India and the impact of CORSIA on 
the Indian airline industry. The first report is expected by the end of October, 2020. 
4. Even though India is committed to addressing the issues of climate change and environmental 
protection, India holds the view that CORSIA is unfair to developing countries like India and is 
also in some respects not in sync with the  UNFCCC. Accordingly, at the 40th ICAO Assembly 
session held in September/October 2019, India raised its concerns through a working paper but 
the updated Resolution on CORSIA was still adopted without any change since there was 

27  
inadequate support for India‗s stand. Still, India has filed its reservations to the Resolution in 
writing. 
5. ICAO has kept a provision for conducting review of the implementation of CORSIA every 3 
years, starting from 2022. In order to present the views of India s trongly and in a concerted 
manner to the ICAO Council during the proposed review in 2022, a Group of Secretaries 
consisting of Secretary, Civil Aviation as Convenor and Secretaries of M/o Environment, Forest 
& Climate Change, External Affairs and Petroleum  and Natural Gases as members, has been 
formed to develop a strategy to take forward the campaign for getting suitable changes in the 
design elements of CORSIA approved by ICAO. The Group has held one meeting in March, 
2020 at which the following points were deliberated: 
a) The proposal to shift the baseline year closer to 2027 needs to be firmly put forth for 
consideration under review of CORSIA scheme. To make the stand stronger, India is 
seeking the support of all states joining CORSIA scheme from 2027 on t he proposal of 
shifting the baseline year. In the recently held 11th BRICS Summit, the issue of CORSIA 
was discussed with the BRICS countries and consensus was built amongst them to work 
together on the review process of the CORSIA framework. 
b) The principle of attributing responsibility of emission reduction to Member  States instead 
of airline operators should be put forth as this will provide a more balanced and fair 
regime for States having large traffic volume of their own but relatively smaller airlines  
vis-à-vis States having low traffic volumes of their own but large airlines. Efforts should 
be made to  relate the emissions of a country to the total international flights from that 
country irrespective of the nationality of airlines operating such flights. 
c) Fast tracking the project for production of indigenous bio -fuels at commercially viable 
cost and to ensure that it meets the ICAO standards for sustainable alternative fuel so that 
the Indian airlines get the benefit of using such fuel under CORSIA scheme. 
d) Exploring diplomatic ways to elicit support of other countries for the above initiatives. 
6. However, due to the onset of the COVID -19 pandemic, the entire focus of the Government 
shifted to the contingency measures required to control the spread of epidemic in the country, and 
therefore, it has not been feasible to hold further meetings of the Group of Secretaries. But efforts 
will be made to organize the next meeting as early as possible. At this meeting, the  impact of 
COVID-19 on the CORSIA scheme  will also be discussed. As international air travel has been 
suspended or drastically reduced by most of the countries, there will be a massive reduction of 
carbon emissions for the year 2020. Hence, CO2 emissions from international civil aviation if 
calculated using the average annual emissions between 2019 and 2020, would result in an 
abnormally lower baseline and lead to higher offsetting requirements for aeroplane operators than 
previously anticipated. It is learnt that this development is being considered by ICAO presently. 
7. The Ministry of Civil Aviation is continuously monitoring the developments at ICAO 
through the Representative of India posted at ICAO in Montreal and efforts are being made to 
project our views at the Council meetings with the su pport of like -minded members of the 
Council. 
 
Further Recommendation/ Observation 

28  
3.2. The Ministry, in its reply, has accepted that there will be deleterious effect on the 
financial health of the Indian carriers operating to foreign dest inations due to the present 
structure of CORSIA, wherein Indian carriers are hardly in any position to ramp up their 
credits due to long -haul international operations during the baseline determination period, 
i.e., 2019-21. The adverse effect will be notic ed after 2027 when the voluntary phase ends. 
The Ministry has indicated that TERI will be assessing the challenges posed by CORSIA

3.3. The Committee terms this as an interim response. The Committee would like to be

redressal mechanism in the overall passenger interest. 
Emergency landing and cancellation of flights 
Recommendation/ Observation 
15. The Committee is anguished that the air travellers get a rough deal instead of care and 
attention, in cases of emergency landings and cancellation of flights by airlines. It is the 
obligation of the airlines to ensure the comfo rt and health of the passengers, especially women, 
children and patients. The Ministry should urgently frame the Guidelines to be scrupulously 
adhered to by the airlines with a clear provision for punitive action in case of violation of the 
guidelines. 
(Para 38.1) 
Reply of the Government 
15.1. In case of denied boarding, cancellation of flights and delays in flights, DGCA had 
issued Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR), Section-3, Series M, Part –IV on ―Facilities to be 
provided to passengers by airlines due t o denied boarding, cancellation o f flights and delays in 
flights‖ , wherein, airlines are required to provide meals and refreshments during substantial‗s 
delays and applicable compensation in case of flight cancellations. 
Further Recommendation/ Observation 
15.2. The Committee is not satisfied with the reply furnished by the Ministry. The 
Committee had recommended that there should be guidelines/rules to address the 
sufferings of the most vulnerable passenger group like the patients, children and women. 
The reply of the Ministry is silent on introducing guidelines/rules to address the sufferings 
of the vulnerable group during emergency landing/cancellation etc. 
Cancellation charges 
Recommendation/ Observation 
16. The Committee notes that there is no uniformity in  the cancellation charges levied by the 
airlines. The Committee lends its support to the demand of rationalising the  cancellation 
charges and is of the view that the airlines may be persuaded to restrict not more than 50% of 

36  
the base far e as cancellation charges. The tax and fuel surcharge collected should be refunded 
to the passengers on cancellation of tickets. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would be 
able to persuade the airlines for such rationalisation in the interest of the passengers. 
(Para 40.1) 
Reply of the Government 
16.1. As per the prevailing regulation, air fare including cancellation charge of pre -booked 
tickets are neither established nor regulated by the Government. However, as per the provision 
mentioned in para 3(i) of Civil Aviation Requirement (CAR) Section 3- Air Transport, Series M, 
Part II titled ―  Refund of Airline Tickets to Passengers of Public Transport Undertakings, ― Under 
no circumstances, the airline or its agent shall levy cancellation charge more than  the basic fare 
plus fuel surcharge‖. 
Further Recommendation/ Observation 
16.2. The Committee observes that absence of a regulatory regime should not allow 
airlines to exploit the hapless passengers by way of exorbitant cancellation charges. The 
Committee, therefore, reiterates that the Ministry should prevail upon airlines to restrict 
the cancellation charges to not more that 50% of the base fare. 
Core group on Safety and Security 
Recommendation/ Observation 
17. The Committee emphasizes the need for a combined  robust security framework to ensure 
safety and security in sectors of Civil Aviation, Road Transport & Highways, Shipping, Tourism 
and Railways. The Committee desires that in order to facilitate effective and periodic 
coordination among the concerned Mini stries and agencies, a core group comprising officers at 
the level of Joint Secretary of the Ministries of Civil Aviation, Road Transport & Highways, 
Shipping, Tourism, Railways, Commissioner of Railway Safety and Petroleum may be set up to 
meet on monthly basis to chalk out ways and means for addressing safety and security concerns 
in these sectors and ensure that international best practices are followed. This core group  
should be headed by Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation. In order to upgrade to in ternational 
standards, the services of consultants (both domestic and international) who are experts in the 
respective fields and have domain knowledge, may be engaged for preparing Reports so that 
they can be implemented. This core group may serve as a th ink-tank and formulate guidelines 
and directions to improve safety and security standards in these sectors. The Committee would 
like the Ministry to furnish the monthly Reports and status of implementation of its decisions, to 
the Committee. 
(Para 47) 
Reply of the Government 
17.1. Recommendations of the C ommittee have been noted for examination in consultation 
with other Ministries/ Departments including attached offices of MoCA viz., DGCA, BCAS and 
AS Division. 
17.2. As per direction of the Parliamentary Standing Committee, a Core Group having 
representations from all concerned ministries was formed under the Chairmanship of the 
Secretary, Civil Aviation to workout the modalities for supplementing each other during the 
various types of Ac cident investigation and suggesting preventive measures to improve safety 
and security standards in these sectors. The first meeting of the Core Group was held on  

37  
23.01.2020 under the Chairmanship of the Secretary, Civil Aviation and various common areas 
of interest with respect to accident investigation and other related activities have been identified 
and discussed, (enclosed as Annexure -II). An action plan based on these will be prepared for 
further coordination. 
Further Recommendation/ Observation 
17.3. The Committee may be apprised of the progress made in this regard.

Projected demand vs. Allocation of Funds 
 
The Committee is at a loss to understand as to why there was delay/rescheduling in 
the delivery of two special Extra Section Flight (SESF) VVIP aircrafts when sufficient 
allocations had been made in BE 2019-20. This delay has resulted in the downward revision 
of BE 2019 -20 allocation from Rs. 4500 c rore to Rs. 3700 crore at the RE stage. The 
Committee would like to remind the Ministry that such shortfalls in utilization of budgeted 
funds would derail the budgetary objectives of the Ministry and expects the Ministry to 
address this issue with due seriousness. 
(Para 1.4) 
The Committee also notes that the Ministry has not adduced any reasons for delay 
in rescheduling the delivery of VVIP aircrafts and would therefore like to apprised of the 
same as also the updated status in this regard. The Committee al so desires to know 
whether any targeted action plan is in place for installation of body scanners at all the 
airports in the country. 
(Para 1.5) 
Savings 
 
The Committee notes that an amount of Rs. 1014.09 crore was allocated to RCS for 
2018-19 out of which only Rs. 403.99 crore was incurred and the balance amount was 
reappropriated/surrendered due to slow pace of expenditure. The Committee is 
constrained to note that a major chunk of the budgeted amount remained unutilized due to 
non-availability of land, en vironmental issues, delay in shifting of State Highways, non - 
finalization of location of heliports, etc. The Committee is of the view that such a huge 
underutilization of allocated funds is indicative of shortcomings in budgetary planning and 
monitoring o f utilization of the budgeted funds which clearly indicates fiscal indiscipline 
and laxity on the part of the Ministry. The Committee would expect the Ministry to be 
more prudent in its budget formulation and make assessment after proper planning. 
(Para 2.4) 
Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) 
 
The Ministry, in its reply, has accepted that there will be deleterious effect on the 
financial health of the Indian carriers operating to foreign destinations due to the present 
structure of CORSIA, wherein Indian carriers are hardly in any position to ra mp up their 
credits due to long-haul international operations during the baseline determination period, 
i.e., 2019-21. The adverse effect will be noticed after 2027 when the voluntary phase ends. 
The Ministry has indicated that TERI will be assessing the c hallenges posed by CORSIA 
and that a Group of Secretaries has been constituted under the Chairmanship of Secretary 

40  
of the Ministry to take forward the campaign for getting suitable changes introduced in the 
CORSIA structure. 
(Para 3.2) 
The Committee terms this as an interim response. The Committee would like to be 
informed of the outcome of TERI study and recommendations of the Group of Secretaries 
in the matter. Furthermore, owing to the severe aviation lockdown due to the pandemic, 
there is a very strong case for reworking the baseline schedule. The Committee may be 
updated on the progress made in the matter. The Committee would like to point out that 
if CORSIA structure is not amended, the airlines operating in this country would be at a 
massive competitive disadvantage against the airlines having the potential to generate huge 
credits due to their existing vast network. 
(Para 3.3) 
Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) 
 
The Committee may be apprised as to whether there is an established mechanism 
for timely VGF release.

Keshod Airport 
 
The Committee desires to be kept apprised of the updated status of implementation 
of the remaining four observations of DGCA. 
(Para 6.2) 
Nagpur Airport 
 
The emphasis made by the Committee in its recommendation was on taking 
necessary action so that the issues plaguing the Nagpur Airport could be sorted out. 
Instead of highlighting the specific measures taken or proposed for improving the facilities 
at Nagpur Airport to international standards, the  Ministry has chosen to absolve itself of 
any responsibility for improving the facilities by shifting the onus to MADC, though 
Airports Authority of India is an equity holder in joint venture of M/s MIHAN INDIA Ltd. 
(MIL). Obviously, there are serious shor tcomings in the role being played by the Ministry 
in acting as a facilitator in upgrading the facilities at the Nagpur Airport. The Committee, 
therefore, does not find the tenor of action taken note of the Ministry to be acceptable and 
recommends that the Ministry should play a proactive role in facilitating appropriate 
remedial measures for overcoming the shortcomings at the Nagpur Airport so that the 
facilities at the Airport are upgraded to international standards at the earliest. The 
Committee also desires that a detailed account of the measures taken in this regard may be 
furnished.

Annexure-I 
 
 
The Terms of Reference (ToR) of the Committee are as under: 
1. Strengthening of the Commission of Railway Safety in order to make its functioning more 
effective and autonomous and with respect to various functions as laid down in Railway 
Act‗1989. 
2. To examine the feasibility of combining the investigating functions and to develop mechanism 
for sharing the best practices and knowledge pool pertaining to accidents concerning the Civil 
Aviation, Railways, Shipping and Oil Sector. 
3. To define a well laid down Inspection Protocol to be followed by IR in case of preventive 
inspections and Accident Investigation as these are well defined duties specified in the Railway 
Act. 
4. Skill upgradation and regular training for the officials involved in technical functions of the 
Commission. 
5. To examine the Recommendations and its implementation related to functioning of Commission 
of Railway Safety as proposed by various Committees and Commissions to examine safety on 
Indian Railways (IR) formed over the years by the Govt. of India. 
6. To suggest suitable Legislation to eliminate duality of Command as CRS is under administrative 
control of MoCA and doing the work of IR. 
7. To examine the stage of implementation of various recommendations given by the 
Commissioners in their Accident Inquiry Report with view to make it more transparent and 
visible so that the accepted recommendations are rolled out in a time bound manner. 
8. To suggest measures to minimize instances of unilateral changes in various Rules, Codes and 
Manuals etc by IR without any consultation with the Commission.

48  
Annexure-II 
 
 
Common areas of interest identified by the Core Group with respect to accident 
investigation and other related activities are: 
 
a. Various specialized agencies dealing with accident i nvestigation should identify area of 
common interest in order to develop a knowledge pool which can be shared amongst all. 
b. Database containing inventory of resources/facilities available with each specialized agency 
should be created. 
c. Identify the areas of  mutual help as each accident has 3 dimensions namely prevention 
measures, relief & rescue and post accident investigation. 
d. Lessons learnt during accident investigations should be shared amongst others. 
e. Case studies should be presented at least once in a y ear. NDRF may also be called during these 
meetings to share their experience of disaster management. 
f. The core group will also provide assistance to other stake holders as and when required during 
accident investigation. 
g. Training and skill upgradation procedures and periodicity in areas of accident investigation. 
h. Instrumentation and technologies adopted by other agencies in accident investigation. 
i. Alarm system for preventing probable accidents and exception reports generated by the 
monitoring mechanism. 
j. Methodology for preventive inspections/checks.

ANNUAL PLAN 2019-20 
Sharp reduction at RE 2019-20 stage  
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee observes that the Ministry has been allocated Rs. 2547.00 crore at RE 
2019-20 stage as against Rs. 3042.35 crore at B.E. 2019 -20 which is a huge reduction of 
over 16%. The Committee observes that many of the projects/activities carried out by the 
Ministry of Culture, if postponed to a future date, will cause irreparable damage to the 
cultural herit age of our country. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry 
may ensure that the available funds are  utilized in an efficient manner, without rushing 
expenditure at the end of a Financial Year.  
      (Para 13) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1 Ministry ensured the utilization of available funds in efficient manner without 
expenditure rushing at year end. Ministry re -prioritized its programmes/ activities and 
accommodated them within the reduced allocation. 
 
ANNUAL PLAN (2020-21) 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee observes that while the Ministry had projected a demand of Rs. 
4323.61 crore for 2019-20, a demand of only Rs. 3857.50 crore has been projected for BE 
2020-21. The Committee may be apprised of the reasons for the substantial reduction in the 
projected requirement of the Ministry, even when there had been a reduction of almost Rs. 
500 crores at RE stage in 2019 -20. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may plead 
the cases of such schemes/projects for higher allocations at RE stage in 2020 -21 so that the 
projects are not stalled due to paucity of funds. 
  (Para 26) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1 The projection for 2019-20 was keeping in view the various commemorations such as 
Celebration of 150 th Birth Anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, releasing various payments 
which remained due for the previous year’s commemorations such as payment to NBCC for 
construction of Pt. Deendayal Institute of Archaeology at Greater NOIDA, etc. The Ministry 
will certainly make efforts for higher allocation depending on the expenditure status at RE 
2020-21 so that the projects may not be stalled due to paucity of funds during the year.

monitor any unauthorized construction in the prohibited/regulated area of a CPM.

expenditure limits. The Committee also desires to be furnished with a factual note 
detailing the specific steps taken to resolve the issues concerning the unspent balances 
with the Autonomous Bodies, delay in appraisal of proposals by the Expert Co mmittee 
and the measures taken / proposed to be taken for sorting out tendering issues. 
(Para 1.3) 
Budget trends over the past years 
The Committee observes that cultural activities promote various economic activities, 
thereby giving employment to a large section of society and contributing to the GDP of 
the nation. Therefore, Culture should not be treated as a marginal sector . A large 
number of our monuments require urgent attention as they suffer due to lack of 
personnel and funds. The Committee recommend s that the Ministry should cite the 
trend of negligible growth in allocation to the Ministry during the last five years and 
justify the importance of more funds to the Ministry at the RE stage in order to carry 
out its mandate in an efficient manner.  
(Para 2.2) 
ANNUAL PLAN (2020-21) 
The Committee reiterates its recommendation made in Para 2.2  of Chapter III of this 
Report. The Committee also expects the Ministry to pay focussed attention for more 
efficient deployment of the available resources.  
(Para 3.2) 
 

43 
 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 
The Committee appreciates that a provision has been made for booking tickets for 
multiple monuments in a single transaction . The Committee, however, reiterates its 
recommendation that the ASI should give tourists, the optio n to buy combined tickets 
or a city/region pass that is valid for a certain duration. The same would allow visitors 
to enter the different monuments present in close vicinity of each other without going 
through the hassle of the ticket purchasing process repeatedly.  
(Para 4.2) 
 
The Committee is of the view that boundary walls are a necessity for the preservation as 
well as clear demarcation of our ancient monuments . Therefore, the Committee 
reiterates its recommendation that a survey of all the monuments s hould be conducted 
to assess the urgency of the construction of boundary wall, along with the budgetary 
requirements for the same.  
(Para 5.3) 
 
NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF INDIA, NATIONAL LIBRARY AND CENTRAL 
REFERENCE LIBRARY 
The Committee is dismayed to note that the Grants Committee of NAI met only once 
during the last Financial Year and even then, the proceedings of the meeting could not 
be initiated. The Committee desires to know the reasons for which the revalidation of 
the schemes being run by the NAI has been pending and why the process for the same 
was not initiated sooner.  
(Para 6.4) 
 
NATIONAL MISSION ON LIBRARIES 
The Committee notes that the BE  in 2019-20 for National Mission on Libraries (under 
Development of Libraries) was Rs. 118.51 crore which was reduced drastically to Rs. 
0.73 crore; but nothing was spent. The reasons for the shortfall in utilization include 
non-submission of proposals by eleven State Governments, non -release of State share 
and non -receipt of claims from the State / UT Library authorities. It appears to the 
Committee that the budget allocations were made under this head without ascertaining 
the status/tenability of the acti vities under this project. The Committee is thus inclined 
to conclude that there is an urgent need to exercise greater due diligence in carrying out 
the budgetary exercise so that such irrational projections of funds are not repeated in 
the future and the practice of overestimation and under -utilization is curbed 
comprehensively.  
(Para 7.2) 

44 
 
DEVELOPMENT OF MUSEUMS 
The Committee feels that the reasons mentioned for slow pace of expenditure are 
routine in nature and could have been sorted out if the Ministry had effectively taken 
up the matter with the concerned State / UT authorities for timely clearances. The 
Committee desires to know the steps taken by the Ministry to ensure that these reasons 
do not cause slow pace of expenditure in the future.  
(Para 8.4) 
 
The Committee observes that merely stating that all museums have been requested to 
ensure the availability of free Wi-Fi facility is not sufficient. The Committee needs to be 
updated on the tangible progress made in this direction.  
(Para 9.2) 
 
The Committee had laid stress on the need on the part of the Ministry in ensuring the 
early completion of the project – “Museum on PMs of India” . But the Committee notes 
from the information furnished that due to the COVID -19 pandemic, this project is 
certain to witness time overrun. The Committee desires that a dedicated mechanism be 
put in place for coordination and completion of the project within shortest possible 
timeframe. Procedural or operational hurdles, if any, should be resolved expeditiously 
at the highest level of the Ministry. The Committee also urges the Ministry to expedite 
action with respect to item no. (ii) and (v) of Para 10.1. Special effort may be made 
especially for item (v) which is the core for the museum.  
(Para 10.3) 
 
CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES/PROJECTS 
The Committee is not at all convinced by the reasons given by the Ministry for slow 
pace of expenditure under this head . The Committee may be informed about what 
caused delays in convening of the Committee meeting under Museum Grant Scheme. As 
admitted by the Ministry, the slow pace of expenditure is the main reason for the severe 
cuts faced by the Ministry at RE stage. India is a resource -constrained country and in 
order to obtain the best possible outcomes, it is imperative that the budge ted funds are 
optimally utilized. Therefore, the Committee recommends that the Ministry may take 
all possible corrective measures to ascertain that similar things are not repeated during 
the current FY.  
(Para 11.2) 
 
 

45 
 
The Committee is constrained to note that the project “Museum on PMs of India” is 
witnessing inordinate delay . Rs. 150.01 crore allocated in BE 2019 -20 was reduced to 
Rs. 69.75 crore at RE 2019-20 stage; but the actual expenditure was even lesser than the 
reduced RE 2019-20 allocation, mainly on account of slow pace of construction activities 
by the executing agency. What is worrisome is that this trend is likely to continue in FY 
2020-21. Such persistent shortfall in the utilization of budgeted funds indicates fiscal 
indiscipline and laxity o n the part of the Ministry. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should take concrete steps for proper utilization of the 
funds budgeted for “Museum on PMs of India” and set up a Coordination Committee 
to oversee the implementation of this project as early as possible.  
(Para 12.2) 
 
The Committee reiterates the recommendation made in Para 11.2 of Chapter III of this 
Report.  
(Para 13.2) 
 
SUPPORT TO LIBRARIES 
The Committee observes that the reply of the Ministry does not address the specific 
issue raised by the Committee . The Committee, therefore, reiterates its 
recommendation that a book exchange programme may be initiated between the 
State/UT Libraries on a periodic basis.  
(Para 14.2) 
 
CAPITAL OUTLAY ON EDUCATION, SPORTS, ART AND CULTURE 
The Committee desires to know the reasons behind the slow pace of expenditure under 
this head during FY 2019 -20 and the steps taken to address those issues impeding the 
pace of expenditure during the ensuing Financial Year.  
(Para 15.2) 
 
VACANCIES EXISTING IN VARIOUS ORGANIZATIONS OF THE MINISTRY 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry may take a holistic look at the staffing 
requirements of ASI and take necessary action to ensure that no further damage is 
caused to our monuments due to lack of staff.  
(Para 16.2) 
 
The Committee is dismayed to note that even though maximum key posts in NGMA 
were created in the year 2011, RRs for the posts could be notified only in the years 2014, 

46 
 
2015, 2017 and 2018 , which is indicative of the inertia and indifference in the matter 
and reflects poorly on the decision -making process in the Ministry.  The Committee 
further notes that several key posts in NGMA are still lying vacant and recommends 
that all out efforts may be made to fill these posts on priority  basis within a specific 
timeframe, so as to enable smooth functioning of NGMA.  
(Para 17.3) 
 
NATIONAL CULTURE FUND 
The Committee would like to know about the status of the Annual Report of the NCF 
for the year 2017-18 onwards.  
(Para 18.2) 
 
The Committee notes that the Ministry has merely chosen to note its observations for 
compliance and no specific mention has been made or details furnished of the initiatives 
for maintaining transparency in the works executed . The Committee, therefore, urges 
upon the Ministry to apprise it in this regard.  
(Para 19.2) 
 
KALA SANSKRITI VIKAS YOJANA 
The Committee notes with concern the huge shortfall in utilization of the budgeted 
funds under the Revenue Head of Kala Sanskriti Vikas Yojana. What is worrisome is 
that the under-utilization of the funds has been mainly on account of factors like non -
compliance of EAT module, non -submission of Utilization Certificates etc. The 
Committee is of the firm view that these issues could have been easily addressed had 
there been a ro bust monitoring mechanism. Given these facts, the Ministry needs to 
urgently put in place a streamlined monitoring mechanism so as to avoid large 
variations in the BE, RE and Actual Expenditure. The Committee desires to be kept 
apprised of the action taken in this regard.  
(Para 20.2) 
 
ARTISTS PENSION SCHEME AND WELFARE FUND 
The Committee is surprised to note that though the number of beneficiaries has been 
increasing with every meeting since 2017 -18 to 2019 -20,  the fund allocation under the 
‘Artist Pension Scheme and Welfare Fund’ decreased from Rs. 23.40 crore at RE 2018 -
19 to Rs. 21.15 crore at RE 2019 -20. Less expenditure on this scheme is not possible 
without either decreasing the number of beneficiaries or decreasing the amount 
obtained by the b eneficiaries of this scheme, both of which are not desirable. The 
Ministry, therefore, owes an explanation to the Committee in this regard. The 

47 
 
Committee also recommends that the Ministry may make sincere efforts to ensure 
optimum expenditure under this head so as not to face cuts at RE stage in 2020-21.  
(Para 21.3) 
 
 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry may provide clear instructions to the 
beneficiaries detailing the conditions of this Scheme so as to permit them to avail 
benefits of the same . The Ministry should reach out to those who are registered as 
beneficiaries but fail to submit the required documents. Beneficiaries who repeatedly 
fail to submit the required documents should be removed from the list of beneficiaries 
so as to permit others to be beneficiaries of the scheme.  
(Para 22.3) 
 
The Committee notes that the reply of the Ministry does not mention any steps that 
have been taken to ensure equitable representation of artistes from States that are 
under-represented in the Artists Pension Scheme. The Committee, therefore, reiterates 
its original recommendation that the Ministry should look into the reasons for under -
representation of several States in this scheme and take necessary corrective measures.  
(Para 23.5) 
 
NATIONAL MONUMENTS AUTHORITY 
The Committee may be apprised of the process followed by ASI to ensure the 
compliance of Section 20A of the AMASR Act . The Committee may be furnished with 
information on the number of cases wherein ASI has intervened in unauthorized 
construction in the protected or prohibited area of a Centrally Protected Monument in 
the last five years and the outcome thereof.  
(Para 24.3) 
 
 The Committee further recommends that physical copies of the same may be placed at 
visible places outside the monuments concerned so as to create awareness of the rules 
among people living in the vicinity of those monuments.  
(Para 25.2) 
 
The Committee understands that preparing the detailed site plan and Heritage Bye -
Laws for all the 3691 monuments/sites is an enormous task . The Committee 
recommends that the NMA may convey its staffing/budgetary requirements to allow 

48 
 
this process to be carried out parallelly for monuments across the country, to Ministry 
of Culture and take effective measures to complete this important task at the earliest.  
(Para 26.7) 
 
MISCELLANEOUS 
Indian Institute of Heritage and Conservation 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should expedite concretization and 
implementation of the proposal for setting up the Indian Institute of Heritage and 
Conservation. The Committee desires to be updated in this regard.  
(Para 27.3) 
 
CHAPTER-IV 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLY OF 
THE MINISTRY IS STILL AWAITED 
 
ARCHAEOLOGICAL SURVEY OF INDIA 
The Committee would like to be apprised of the progress made in this regard.  
(Para 1.2) 
 
NATIONAL SCHOOL OF DRAMA 
The Committee is dismayed to note that the last communication quoted in this regard is 
from 2017. The Committee may be apprised of the present status in this regard.  
(Para 2.2) 
 
SUPPORT TO AKADEMIES 
The Committee would like to be updated on the action taken in this regard.  
(Para 3.2) 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE HIGH POWERED COMMITTEE 
The Committee desires to know the steps taken by the Ministry to implement the 
abovementioned recommendation of the High Powered Committee.  
(Para 4.2) 

49 
 
NEED FOR BETTER CO -ORDINATION WITH MINISTRIES AND STATE 
GOVERNMENTS  
The Committee may be apprised of the action taken by the Ministry and the progress 
made in this regard.  
(Para 5.2)

DEMANDS FOR GRANTS (2020-21) OF THE MINISTRY 
Recommendation/Observation  
1. The Ministry of Shipping which has drawn ambitious program for Port infrastructure 
development and capacity augmentation will become handicapped because of the budgetary 
cuts which will jeopardize the targeted outcomes. The Committee takes note of the fisc al 
constraints faced by Ministry of Finance due to moderation in economic growth and the 
impact of global slowdown. Still, while seeking a balance between public good and need for 
containing fiscal deficit, the Committee would advocate higher budgetary pro visions in 
favour of Sagarmala Scheme and Kolkata Port Trust at the RE 2020 -21 stage. The 
Committee recommends that when the growth momentum is revived and the additional 
resources become available as a result of revenue buoyancy, the allocation for the Mi nistry 
should be increased further.              (Para 7) 
Reply of the Ministry 
1.1. The recommendation of the C ommittee has been noted. Based on the expenditure 
trend, targets and absorptive capacity of the implementing agencies, additional fund 
requirement will be assessed from time to time and will be projected to the Ministry of 
Finance at appropriate stage. 
Recommendation/Observation  
2. The Committee observes that there is a huge gap between the projected demand and 
the sanctioned budget for the Ministry for the FY 2020 -21. As against the projected demand 
of Rs. 3328.70 crores, the Ministry has been provided with Rs. 1800.00 crores only. 
Obviously, such huge variation is suggestive of the shortcomings in the budgetary planning. 
The Committee would urge upon the Ministry to exercise due diligence in the budget 
formulation with proper planning and assessment, taking into account its needs an d the 
capacity to deliver the functions assigned to it.          (Para 8) 
Reply of the Ministry 
2.1. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. As per the availability of 
funds, projects priorities will be re -defined and funds will be released accordingly after due 
assessment of all deliverables. 
PORT CAPACITY- ADDITION WORK 
Recommendation/Observation  

3 
 
3. The Committee observes that in Major Ports productivity in terms of ship turn-around 
time, waiting time and average output per ship berthday  continues to be modest when 
compared with global standards and performance of Ports in developed maritime countries. 
Since globalization, rapid adoption of technology and competitiveness are critical objectives 
to the exporters and importers in India, mod ernization of Major Ports is critical to the 
success of their supply chain objectives. It is in this context that, the capacity addition at five 
Ports, namely, Deendayal Port Trust, Mormugao Port Trust, V.O. Chidambaranar Port 
Trust, Cochin Port Trust and Visakhapatnam Port Trust assumes added significance. The 
Committee desires that the progress of implementation of these projects should be monitored 
regularly and that proper guidelines should be issued for their timely completion. The 
Committee also desir es to know whether traffic flows at the above Ports have shown any 
correlation with the GDP subsequent to the capacity addition during 2019-20.    (Para 20) 
Reply of the Ministry 
3.1. The Ministry is regularly monitoring the progress o f Port modernization projects. In 
case of any deviations from the target date, suitable instructions/guide lines used to be issued 
to the P orts from time to time to streamline the same. Due to the various initiatives taken 
towards modernization of Major Por ts, the average Turn-round time, which was 87.36 hours 
during 2015-16, has come down to 61.75 hours  during 2019-20.  Like -wise, average output 
per ship berthday, which was 13156 tonnes during 2015-16, has increased to 16433 tonnes 
during 2019-20. 
3.2. Capacity available as on 31.03. 2019 and traffic handled at five Ports, namely  viz.,
